## stream traffic data in stream objects

*2023-07-25 to 2024-12-17 · 50 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/stream.20traffic.20data.20in.20stream.20objects/with/1615442)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-07-25 03:16 UTC

We currently include the stream traffic information using `stream_weekly_traffic` field in `Subscription` data sent to clients and not `Stream`data. This means the `stream_weekly_traffic` data is sent to client via -
- the `subscribed`, `unsubscribed` and `never_subscribed `fields in `register` response.
- the response of `GET users/me/subscriptions`endpoint
- the `subscription/add` event sent to clients.

Now, I was thinking of including the stream traffic data in stream objects itself instead of subscription objects. Just to note that the stream traffic data will be inlcuded in all of the above objects since those essentially include all the stream information. There has been some discussion on https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26234#discussion_r1260040965.

One possible use case for including the stream traffic data in stream objects is when a user receives a stream create event. When receiving the stream create event for a just created stream, the `stream_weekly_traffic` field would be `null`as the stream was just created, but there can be cases when stream create event is sent to a user for an already existing stream like when a stream is changed from being private to public. In such cases, the `stream_weekly_traffic` might not be null, but the client will not have the correct data till a reload as stream object passed with stream create event does not include the stream traffic data.

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-07-25 03:16 UTC

Now, we are not sure whether we should move the `stream_weekly_traffic` to be inlcuded to stream data as a whole or just include it in the stream create event. Only including it in the stream object sent with stream creation event would make it inconsistent with the other stream data that client receives.

There can be concerns of performance, but it should be fine I think. We make one query to `StreamCount` table to get the data for multiple stream IDs and a simple computation for each streams results in the average data.

```py
def get_streams_traffic(stream_ids: Set[int]) -> Dict[int, int]:
    stat = COUNT_STATS["messages_in_stream:is_bot:day"]
    traffic_from = timezone_now() - datetime.timedelta(days=28)

    query = StreamCount.objects.filter(property=stat.property, end_time__gt=traffic_from)
    query = query.filter(stream_id__in=stream_ids)

    traffic_list = query.values("stream_id").annotate(value=Sum("value"))
    traffic_dict = {}
    for traffic in traffic_list:
        traffic_dict[traffic["stream_id"]] = traffic["value"]

    return traffic_dict
```

```python
def get_average_weekly_stream_traffic(
    stream_id: int, stream_date_created: datetime.datetime, recent_traffic: Dict[int, int]
) -> Optional[int]:
    try:
        stream_traffic = recent_traffic[stream_id]
    except KeyError:
        stream_traffic = 0

    stream_age = (timezone_now() - stream_date_created).days

    if stream_age >= 28:
        average_weekly_traffic = int(stream_traffic // 4)
    elif stream_age >= STREAM_TRAFFIC_CALCULATION_MIN_AGE_DAYS:
        average_weekly_traffic = int(stream_traffic * 7 // stream_age)
    else:
        return None

    if average_weekly_traffic == 0 and stream_traffic > 0:
        average_weekly_traffic = 1

    return round_to_2_significant_digits(average_weekly_traffic)
```

I'd prefer to avoid making a distinction where it's sometimes null and sometimes absent. In this case I think leaving it out would be a bit better than making it null, but either of those would be much better than making it sometimes one and sometimes the other.

That's because in general I'd like to avoid introducing new situations in our API where a client potentially needs to track the difference between whether some named property in a JSON object was missing, or was present with value `null`.

For a client written in JavaScript, that distinction is easy to track because it maps directly to JS's idiosyncratic distinction between two values `null` and `undefined`. But for clients written in many (most?) other languages, and in particular Dart, it's significantly more annoying.

## highlight topic-wildcard mention

*2023-08-08 to 2023-11-10 · 24 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/highlight.20topic-wildcard.20mention/with/1621559)*

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-08-08 19:19 UTC

We highlight the `@all` text for a user if it mentions the user.

For `@all` mentions, we highlight the text if the user is subscribed to the stream. 

Similarly, for `@topic` mentions, we should highlight the text for topic participants.

Topic participants:
* Anyone who sent a message in the topic. 
* Anyone who reacted to any of the messages in the topic.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-08-08 19:20 UTC

In #26382, we calculated the topic participants in the frontend code itself, (which actually gives [inaccurate results](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26382#discussion_r1286203554)). 

@Tim Abbott [suggested](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26382#issuecomment-1668330094):

> after seeing this logic, my leaning is that we are probably going to want to introduce such a `UserMessage` flag such that we don't need to do an expensive and potentially inaccurate calculation when rendering individual messages (note that what you have potentially does quadratic work... since each message containing @topic will require us to loop through all messages in that topic!).

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-08-08 19:22 UTC

## Linkifier priority

*2023-08-09 to 2023-08-24 · 38 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Linkifier.20priority/with/1622195)*

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-08-09 18:22 UTC

We want to introduce linkifier priorities as discussed in #**issues>linkifiers**. Currently, they are sorted by the ID. To switch to explicit ordering, we need to add an integer priority field to `RealmFilter` and use that as the sorting key (the lower the more prioritized).

There are two ways that we may communicate the priorities between the client and the server:

1. Make priority internal to the server:

- `GET /realm/filters`,  `POST /register` and `GET /events` return the linkifiers in sorted order without the additional priority key, and the client should assume the ordering represents the priorities already.
- `PATCH /realm/filters/priorities` *(new)* accepts the list of reordered linkifier ids. 
- `PATCH /realm/filters/{id}` remains unchanged.

2. Make priority a part of linkifiers:

- `GET /realm/filters`,  `POST /register` and `GET /events` return the linkifiers with an additional integer priority field.
- `PATCH /realm/filters/{id}` allows updates to the integer value of the priority of each linkifier. Dragging and resorting linkifiers require multiple calls. Alternatively, we can have a new endpoint `PATCH /realm/filters`  to update the priorities in bulk, by having the client pass all linkifier objects it wants to update.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-08-09 18:26 UTC

I'm preferring design 1. Because reordering can result in all linkifiers' priority values being changed, if the client is required to manage the priorities for each linkifier individually, they might often still end up updating the priorities of all linkifiers.

``` python
def try_reorder_realm_custom_profile_fields(realm: Realm, order: Iterable[int]) -> None:                
    order_mapping = {_[1]: _[0] for _ in enumerate(order)}                                              
    custom_profile_fields = CustomProfileField.objects.filter(realm=realm)                              
    for custom_profile_field in custom_profile_fields:                                                  
        if custom_profile_field.id not in order_mapping:                                                
            raise JsonableError(_("Invalid order mapping."))                                            
    for custom_profile_field in custom_profile_fields:                                                  
        custom_profile_field.order = order_mapping[custom_profile_field.id]                             
        custom_profile_field.save(update_fields=["order"])                                              
    notify_realm_custom_profile_fields(realm)                                                           
```

Make priority internal to the server: - `GET /realm/filters`, `POST /register` and `GET /events` return the linkifiers in sorted order without the additional priority key, and the client should assume the ordering represents the priorities already. - `PATCH /realm/filters/priorities` *(new)* acce …

What does `PATCH /realm/filters/priorities` do if it gets a list of linkifier IDs that doesn't contain all the existing linkifiers? Does it drop the ones that are missing?

I think it's probably better if that endpoint stays focused on just reordering (as its name suggests), so that if the input is missing one of the existing linkifiers then that's an error, just like if it has a duplicate entry or if it has an entry that isn't an existing linkifier. Then we'd have a separate endpoint, like `DELETE /realm/filters/{id}`, for explicitly removing a linkifier when that's what the user wants.

That's because otherwise there's a race: you add a new linkifier, you reorder the old set of linkifiers, and the reordering clobbers the addition even though neither user intended that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-24 23:23 UTC

There's definitely a possible race where a user clicks "add" to add a new linkifier and during the network delay for that request drags other linkifiers around such that the API request to do that is sent before the client learns that the request to add the new linkifier succeeded; in that case the browser will send a stale list of linkifier IDs in the reorder request. I think that's basically the only realistic race here, and it's very small, in that the API request to add a new linkifier doesn't do anything expensive, so it's just a network RTT.

I think both this race and the level of frequency of multiple users editing linkifier settings for an organization at the same time are likely low enough that it's totally fine to get an error and have to do it again -- almost nobody will be affected by whatever error handling we do.

## unknown user IDs

*2023-08-17 to 2025-04-16 · 68 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/unknown.20user.20IDs/with/1627069)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-17 18:47 UTC

So I wanted to flag that a thing that we're hoping to do is support for guests who don't get access to all the users in the organization. I'm not sure how that will end up working in terms of the APIs yet; @Sahil Batra for the discussion.

The product purpose is to support #10970.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-17 18:48 UTC

I can see a few different designs:
* The server sends you `realm_user` data on all the user IDs in the organization, but the ones you don't have access to are all identical "Unknown user" users, differing only in user ID or something. This would be the simplest for compatibility and might be what we start with (with a better implementation gated behind a client capability).
* The server sends you `realm_user` that only contains users that you have access to details on, and clients need to make up an "Unknown user" entry locally whenever they see a user ID that doesn't mean anything to them.
* Something else.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-23 22:35 UTC

I think we'll likely need some version of that first design ­— with a client capability, as you say, to opt into a better design instead. In zulip-mobile we take it as an invariant that all the user IDs the server tells us about are users we can find in the data we have from the event system. There are probably other clients taking that approach too.

In zulip-flutter, partly because I knew this product feature was on the horizon, we've been taking a different approach: we systematically having the code handle the case of an unknown user, with UI code deciding e.g. to say "(unknown user)" for their name or to use a blank space for their avatar.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-23 22:46 UTC

I think the much better design is to not have the server in the business of making up bogus data, though. Which basically means that second design — the data the server provides only contains the users that you have permission to know about.

For a handful of properties — the full name, the avatar, perhaps one or two others — the bogus data is fairly benign. Specifically those are the properties where the main thing the client can do with the information anyway is just to present it to the user in the UI, and so the server can make up a bogus value and the effects of that value are relatively predictable.

But there are a lot of other properties on user objects. For most of them, there is no sensible value for the bogus data to use. Should `is_admin` be true or false? What about `is_guest`? When pressed to make up bogus data, we'll probably make both of those false… but there's nothing especially principled to recommend that choice. We'll sometimes be pretending the other user has less privilege than they do, and sometimes pretending they have more.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-23 23:06 UTC

Looking through the API docs, I guess this situation isn't as bad for users as it is for, say, streams.

Earlier in zulip-mobile's history, we had an object called "`NULL_STREAM`" which was a big bundle of bogus data for all the different properties of a stream, and we'd pass that around in various parts of the code when something wanted a stream object but we didn't know about such a stream. That one was truly offensive, because it meant this code had made up an answer to whether this stream was private or public.

Similarly we had a "`NULL_MESSAGE`" (which was a stream message, in case you're wondering; apparently a DM would have been non-null), and many others.

But a user object doesn't have much more to it beyond name, avatar, role (which is denormalized across a bunch of properties), and whether it's a bot (and some more details if it is). And there aren't many situations that would call for a client to condition on those, for a user other than the self-user, beyond deciding how to present that user in the UI.

So although I think it's still best for the server to stay away from making up bogus data — and I'd want to have a client capability to ask it not to do that — I think I won't actually feel that bothered about the default being that it does make up bogus users, or about that staying the default indefinitely.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-23 23:08 UTC

## register: Be more informative about push-bouncer setup

*2023-08-21 to 2023-12-06 · 42 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/register.3A.20Be.20more.20informative.20about.20push-bouncer.20setup/with/1628834)*

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-08-21 20:09 UTC

(Paraphrasing Greg in a private stream a few months ago.)

Currently, the [`register`](https://chat.zulip.org/api/register-queue) response gives `realm_push_notifications_enabled`:

> Whether push notifications are enabled for this organization. Typically `false` for self-hosted servers that have not configured the [Mobile push notifications service](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/mobile-push-notifications.html).

But that's less informative than one might hope:

```python
# $ grep -A30 'def push_notifications_enabled' zerver/lib/push_notifications.py
def push_notifications_enabled() -> bool:
    """True just if this server has configured a way to send push notifications."""
    if (
        uses_notification_bouncer()
        and settings.ZULIP_ORG_KEY is not None
        and settings.ZULIP_ORG_ID is not None
    ):  # nocoverage
        # We have the needed configuration to send push notifications through
        # the bouncer.  Better yet would be to confirm that this config actually
        # works -- e.g., that we have ever successfully sent to the bouncer --
        # but this is a good start.
        return True
    # …
```

IOW, it confirms that they've written down config in the server's settings to talk to the bouncer (or else to talk to APNs and FCM directly), but not that that config is at all valid.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-08-21 20:13 UTC

I plan to file an issue to be more informative here; people should chime in here if they have thoughts on how to focus that issue (e.g., to say we should change `realm_push_notifications_enabled`'s meaning, or add a separate value, etc.)

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-21 21:42 UTC

Thanks for raising this!

I think it'd be good to change the behavior of `realm_push_notifications_enabled` so that it's more skeptical about deciding that push notifications have been set up for the server.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-21 21:45 UTC

That comment (which I probably wrote) suggests tracking whether we've ever successfully sent a notification through the bouncer. That's OK but it's slightly awkward in that before the very first notification, we'd be saying push notifications aren't enabled, and then we go and send a notification after all.

Another alternative would be to add an endpoint on the bouncer that requires the same credentials but doesn't send a notification — perhaps an endpoint that's just for confirming the credentials are valid.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-08-21 21:51 UTC

> Another alternative would be to add an endpoint on the bouncer that requires the same credentials but doesn't send a notification — perhaps an endpoint that's just for confirming the credentials are valid.

Do you mean credentials belonging to the Zulip realm? And the Zulip server gets a new startup task to check those credentials with the bouncer using the new endpoint?

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-21 21:54 UTC

The credentials I mean are those `settings.ZULIP_ORG_KEY` and `settings.ZULIP_ORG_ID` values. They belong to the Zulip server, as credentials for talking to the push bouncer.

And yeah, it'd mean the server at some point checks the credentials for validity, and then it knows they're valid and can proceed. Probably we'd want it to remember the answer somewhere in the database (if it's a yes, anyway), so that it doesn't have to recheck in the future.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-21 21:56 UTC

(And the information it would remember should be not just "I have valid credentials" — because if the credentials in the settings change for whatever reason, we'll want to re-check the new credentials — but instead something like "The credentials with such-and-such hash are valid".)

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-08-21 22:04 UTC

> Probably we'd want it to remember the answer somewhere in the database (if it's a yes, anyway), so that it doesn't have to recheck in the future.

If the request isn't expensive (say, compared to sending one push notification to one device), I wonder about checking every time the server starts up.
- `settings.ZULIP_ORG_KEY` and `settings.ZULIP_ORG_ID` can change with any startup, and I believe only on a startup (not mid-session).
- Startup seems like a good time to learn if there was a network reconfiguration that broke access to the bouncer.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-08-21 23:07 UTC

In fact, what if the server refused to start up if it saw that notification support was intended, but those credentials were wrong or the bouncer was unreachable.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 01:25 UTC

Hmm, yeah, @Alex Vandiver may have deeper thoughts here, but I thought it would be reasonable for the startup process specifically for the push notifications queue worker on the local Zulip server to do such a check on startup, and log and error (and store that information for the server to use) if it fails.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-22 01:37 UTC

The main thing I'd want to find a way to avoid, if going in that direction, is for the value to flap if the server (or for that matter the bouncer) temporarily has network trouble or another transient operational issue.

**Greg Price** · 2023-08-22 01:40 UTC

In the client, we use this value to drive a fairly conspicuous warning telling the user they shouldn't expect push notifications to work. That's appropriate when a false value here means the server's setup has *never* been known to work; but if the server just temporarily has trouble, that's another matter.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2023-08-22 02:55 UTC

There's a little complexity to what "the startup process" is.  Crash-looping `zulip-django` is probably not a good experience to have and have to debug.

This smells like something that the [system check](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.2/topics/checks/) framework might be reasonable for, but I've not written one, nor do I think there's an existing one in the codebase.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-08-22 04:09 UTC

(replying to Greg Price)
> In the client, we use this value to drive a fairly conspicuous warning telling the user they shouldn't expect push notifications to work. That's appropriate when a false value here means the server's setup has *never* been known to work; but if the server just temporarily has trouble, that's another …

During temporary server trouble, presumably all the user's notifications will be dropped, so I think the mobile client has an interest in knowing about it. The case might be stronger for showing "temporary server trouble" in a view like Settings > Notifications (> Troubleshooting) than in an alert that interrupts what you're doing. That's doable. "Temporary" could be like a week, or at least long enough for the user to notice and check their "Notifications" view.

In some cases, something will have gone sideways and the server admin hasn't kicked it back into place again. (I don't yet know what-all this could look like in real life but I'm happy to learn. :smile:) So someone needs to mention the user's symptom to the  admin and ask them to take a look. I do prefer a system where the app can give that task to the user, instead of a system that needs some variation of user > Front > @Mateusz Mandera > me > user > me > user > server admin > me > @Alex Vandiver > me > server admin > [etc.]

```

    if not push_notifications_enabled():                                                                
        if settings.DEVELOPMENT and not settings.TEST_SUITE:  # nocoverage

        logger.warning(                                                                                 
            "Mobile push notifications are not configured.\n  "

And so that would just do some sort of "ping" request to the server to check it's connection is working, and store the answer somewhere.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-22 22:08 UTC

And then this function would check the value stored by that check:
```
def push_notifications_enabled() -> bool:                                                               
    """True just if this server has configured a way to send push notifications."""                     
    if (                                                                                                
        uses_notification_bouncer()                                                                     
        and settings.ZULIP_ORG_KEY is not None                                                          
        and settings.ZULIP_ORG_ID is not None                                                           
    ):  # nocoverage                                                                                    
        # We have the needed configuration to send push notifications through                           
        # the bouncer.  Better yet would be to confirm that this config actually                        
        # works -- e.g., that we have ever successfully sent to the bouncer --                          
        # but this is a good start.                                                                     
        return True                                                                                     
    if settings.DEVELOPMENT and (apns_enabled() or gcm_enabled()):  # nocoverage                        
        # Since much of the notifications logic is platform-specific, the mobile                        
        # developers often work on just one platform at a time, so we should                            
        # only require one to be configured.                                                            
        return True                                                                                     
    elif apns_enabled() and gcm_enabled():  # nocoverage                                                
        # We have the needed configuration to send through APNs and GCM directly                        
        # (i.e., we are the bouncer, presumably.)  Again, assume it actually works.                     
        return True                                                                                     
    return False                                                                                        
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-21 22:01 UTC

The tricky question is where we store the state of whether push notifications are working... we don't actually have a database table for storing server-level state like "Are push notifications currently working for this server" at all. I see several options for where we could store the information:
* Store the state in a file, perhaps in `/var/run` somewhere.
* `memcached` is probably bad because of LRU configuration -- we don't want it to be possible for this to be evicted.
* `redis` could work, in that the information there is semi-persistent in the right way.
* Make a new `class Server` table with a single field `push_notifications_working` field on it.
* Add a new `realm.push_notifications_enabled` field on `Realm` in the database. This might actually be the best plan, because in theory a self-hosted Zulip server with multiple realms could have push notifications working/enabled for some but not all of those realms.

## client_capabilities for other endpoints

*2023-08-28 to 2023-09-08 · 19 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/client_capabilities.20for.20other.20endpoints/with/1632497)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-28 17:09 UTC

So, currently, we only have one endpoint, `/register`, that accepts a client_capabilities object, because almost all of the things that they do are changes in that endpoint's semantics. The other `client_capabilities` type flags that we have, for example `client_gravatar`, are older things predating the `client_capabilities` concept, that are just passed as independent parameters to individual endpoints.

With the API changes in #**api design>highlight topic-wildcard mention**, we would be adding to the two endpoints for fetching messages a new `stream_wildcard_mentioned_flag` client capability -- and #26382 as written passes it as an independent parameter, resulting in a handful of lines [like this](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/26382#discussion_r1307654734).

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-28 17:11 UTC

I think it's potentially OK to do that once just to get that PR integrated, as there's a lot of complexity in that PR already, but I think it could make sense to ask the question of whether we want to have a model where either just those endpoints or maybe in the future, every API endpoint, will accept a `client_capabilities` object (and potentially basically ignore it if that endpoint doesn't have behavior that depends on them).

If we did that, then you'd be able to just have the common API code (like `channel.ts` in the web app) be responsible for passing the set of capabilities for the client implementation, rather than having to worry about individual call points forgetting to pass the right thing.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-28 17:13 UTC

I think my proposal would at least be to use the formatting of a `client_capabilities` object for the couple new ones we're adding, such that we'll be able to save a migration of those endpoints towards that model in the future, if it's not a hard change; @Prakhar Pratyush thoughts?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-28 17:16 UTC

And then we can use this thread to discuss if we want to move in the direction of having every API endpoint accept a capabilities object (which might mean just excluding it from being marked with `ignored_parameters_unsupported` if passed to an endpoint that doesn't need it). 

I think the main class of thing that might be annoying here is just the server-side implementation semantics of `GET /events`, where probably it will continue to makes sense to only consider the client capabilities at the time the queue was registered, and store those, since it is isn't really a coherent idea for us to change what capabilities to expect of a client during the lifetime of an event queue.

@Zixuan James Li FYI as well since you may have some extra insight on this from your work on reworking the internals of how the API parses parameters.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-08-28 19:38 UTC

I think reusing `client_capabilities` is fine for these affected endpoints. To allow it for all other endpoints, how do we want to document this, especially for the ones that do not support it?

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-08-28 19:42 UTC

It would be easy to make the endpoint decorator add the parameter programmatically. Then we can include client capabilities in all operations in our OpenAPI spec, where most of them are noted to have no effect.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-08-28 19:45 UTC

It will perhaps make the documentation more clumsy, but I think it is better than leaving `client_capabilities` intentionally undocumented.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-28 19:49 UTC

(replying to Zixuan James Li)
> I think reusing `client_capabilities` is fine for these affected endpoints. To allow it for all other endpoints, how do we want to document this, especially for the ones that do not support it?

Yeah I'm not sure. The Zulip API currently ignores parameters that are not expected. A first step might be to just write such a decorator and apply it to just `POST /register` and be able to use it with the two new endpoints that will accept it, just to get a bunch of the moving parts in place and unblock #26382.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-28 19:51 UTC

From a clutter/readability standpoint, I'm not thrilled with the idea of having `client_capabilities` be something that appears on the list of parameters for 100 endpoints when only 3 of them ever inspect it. So that might argue for just having the endpoints that will use it expect the parameter both in code and documentation.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-08-28 20:04 UTC

Yeah, I don't see much benefits to allowing this for all endpoints other than making it potentially easier to write the bindings, and I think passing a parameter to all endpoints is unusual for generated bindings. We can just reuse client capabilities for endpoints that need it, and let the client pass the capabilities object explicitly per call.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-28 20:25 UTC

I think we should just add boolean flags to the endpoints rather than trying to unify this concept with `client_capabilities`.

If you were imagining that client binding libraries could accept a `client_capabilities` object once when the client object is constructed and automatically reuse it for all API calls, that approach would make it hard or impossible for most type systems to correctly express how the static types of the API calls depend on the runtime configuration from the constructor.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-08-28 21:09 UTC

OK, individual boolean parameters for the other two endpoints are what the PR does as written. (With a `client_capabilities` value of the same name added to `/register`)

**Abhijeet Bodas** · 2023-08-29 17:52 UTC

> where probably it will continue to makes sense to only consider the client capabilities at the time the queue was registered, and store those

How about storing the `client_capabilities` sent by the client when the event queue is registered and looking at it for every endpoint? Would that be possible/useful?

**Abhijeet Bodas** · 2023-08-29 17:53 UTC

One more question specific to the webapp -- currently even the webapp has to use the client capabilities model. Why can't the server always assume all capabilities to be present if the client is the webapp? That will always be a correct assumption, right?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-08-29 18:47 UTC

We do not want to make assumptions like that, because we want to make it possible in the future to run the web frontend independently from the backend and connect it to an arbitrary server.

**Abhijeet Bodas** · 2023-08-30 01:29 UTC

Oh OK, that makes sense. Thanks!

**Greg Price** · 2023-09-08 21:28 UTC

(replying to Abhijeet Bodas)
> How about storing the `client_capabilities` sent by the client when the event queue is registered and looking at it for every endpoint? Would that be possible/useful?

The bulk of the endpoints in the API aren't tied to an event queue, so there isn't such a thing to look at.

The /api/get-events endpoint is unusual in that it refers back to a particular previous request the client made, and to a session-like state created by that previous request.

**Greg Price** · 2023-09-08 21:40 UTC

I agree with this reasoning:

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> If you were imagining that client binding libraries could accept a `client_capabilities` object once when the client object is constructed and automatically reuse it for all API calls, that approach would make it hard or impossible for most type systems to correctly express how the static types of t …

and so I expect client binding libraries will want to expose these flags in the parameters passed to the individual endpoint methods, just like they expose any other parameter accepted by the endpoints.

**Greg Price** · 2023-09-08 21:40 UTC

I think there's still potentially value in having a unified `client_capabilities` concept… *if* we think there'll be several such flags that are cross-cutting, meaning they're accepted by a swath of different endpoints. For any flag that's cross-cutting, it's useful to give it a uniform shape across all the relevant endpoints, and if there are several such flags it can start being useful to have them bundled together.

I'm not sure that's likely, though. We only have a couple of such flags now, like `client_gravatar`, and even those apply only to a handful of endpoints each (most of them closely related, like /api/get-user, /api/get-users, /api/get-user-by-email).

*2023-08-29 to 2023-09-01 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/error.20subscribing.2Funsubscribing.20unexpected.20user.2C.20.2326593/with/1633039)*

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-08-29 16:07 UTC

Currently, if a deactivated user (or unknown user ID or API email for the organization) is sent, then an HTTP status code of 403 is returned and the error code in the response is `"UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL"`. These changes are up in #26601  for folks to review.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-08-29 16:07 UTC

The special `"UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL"` code wasn't in the API documentation anywhere, but that doesn't mean that either the mobile or terminal clients don't rely on that being in the error response, or the HTTP status code being 403, when handling these errors, so I wanted to check in with folks here.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-08-29 16:07 UTC

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-08-31 16:09 UTC

@Greg Price, @Chris Bobbe and @Neil Pilgrim (neiljp) mentioning you all to get your feedback about how these changes to the HTTP status code and `code` field in the json error response for these two endpoints would (or wouldn't) impact the current mobile/terminal clients. Thanks!

I think that change wouldn't affect the mobile client.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2023-09-01 00:13 UTC

That doesn't affect the terminal client either.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-01 01:09 UTC

## error code and msg overlap question

*2023-09-06 to 2023-09-08 · 15 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/error.20code.20and.20msg.20overlap.20question/with/1635492)*

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-09-06 12:52 UTC

While doing some work on the error reponses in the API documentation, I noticed that in 3 of the view functions in `zerver/views/invite.py`, we have a check for whether the user is an administrator. And if not we raise the generic `JsonableError` with the `msg` string as `"Must be an organization administrator"`. The error `code` for these is currently `BAD_REQUEST`.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-09-06 12:52 UTC

But in `zerver/lib/exceptions.py`, we do have `OrganizationAdministratorRequiredError` with the same `msg` string as above, but a different error `code`: `UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL`. This is used in `zerver/decorator.py` as well as a few other places:

```console
$ git grep -c OrganizationAdministratorRequiredError zerver/
zerver/decorator.py:2
zerver/lib/exceptions.py:1
zerver/lib/streams.py:2
zerver/lib/users.py:3
zerver/views/users.py:3
```

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-09-06 12:52 UTC

So, should these invite users views be raising the more specific `OrganizationAdministratorRequiredError` error? Or was it intentional for these to be using the more generic `JsonableError`?

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-09-06 12:52 UTC

And does it matter if errors have the same `msg` string with different `code`s? We obviously use the same `code` for many different `msg` strings, as is the case when we raise `JsonableError` throughout the backend.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-06 14:25 UTC

Probably would be good to raise the more specific error. The history is almost certainly that we added the more specific error later and didn't update those existing call sites.

Bad request is the default code; it's usually better to replace it with something more specific if that something already exists. I would expect probably most cases where we have the same error message in different codes would be a minor bug.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2023-09-06 14:41 UTC

That was my instinct, but I thought it would be good to check-in. I can have a PR for changing those views for the more specific error code with the API feature level/documentation updates.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-06 20:38 UTC

Ok.

**Greg Price** · 2023-09-06 22:17 UTC

That change seems fine.

The name `UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL` is unfortunate — "principal" is an echo of Zephyr that hasn't made sense for Zulip for many years — but I guess it's what we already send in a variety of other situations, so matching those is better than making up a new name.

**Greg Price** · 2023-09-06 22:20 UTC

Separately from the error code in the JSON, it looks like `OrganizationAdministratorRequiredError` and its friends are returning an HTTP status code of 400, the default. For these it'd probably make more sense to send 403 (by setting `http_status_code: int = 403` on the error class).

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-07 17:19 UTC

After some quick grepping, pretty sure none of our clients actually look for the value of `UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL`, so if we wanted to rename that, we certainly could. I think `UNAUTHORIZED_ROLE` would be more accurate for what it's used for today:

```
class OrganizationMemberRequiredError(JsonableError):                                                   
    code: ErrorCode = ErrorCode.UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL                                                  
                                                                                                        
    def __init__(self) -> None:                                                                         
        pass                                                                                            
                                                                                                        
    @staticmethod                                                                                       
    def msg_format() -> str:                                                                            
        return _("Must be an organization member")                                                      
                                                                                                        
                                                                                                        
class OrganizationAdministratorRequiredError(JsonableError):                                            
    code: ErrorCode = ErrorCode.UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL                                                  
                                                                                                        
    def __init__(self) -> None:                                                                         
        pass                                                                                            
                                                                                                        
    @staticmethod

        return _("Must be an organization administrator")                                               
                                                                                                        
                                                                                                        
class OrganizationOwnerRequiredError(JsonableError):                                                    
    code: ErrorCode = ErrorCode.UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL                                                  
                                                                                                        
    def __init__(self) -> None:                                                                         
        pass                                                                                            
                                                                                                        
    @staticmethod

        return _("Must be an organization owner")

and is used for when you're not logged in at all, i.e. unauth*enticated*.

And enabling the client to maintain an accurate replica of various chosen swaths of the server's state is the whole point of the event system.

"""
Event sent when another user subscribes to a stream, or their subscription is newly visible to the current user.

When a user subscribes to a stream, the current user will receive this event only if they

When the current user gains permission to see a given stream's subscriber list,

In particular I think that summary sentence is general enough that it accurately describes the semantics we'll want even with any future wrinkles we add, like perhaps guest users only being able to see some fellow subscribers. **Greg Price** · 2023-09-08 23:54 UTC

Concretely, in the case at hand, I think the main issue would be what to do when the realm's setting changes from some specific URL to falling back to the server-level value.

If that's just a single event setting a single value to `null`, then the client has to have logic to recognize that that means the value in effect is now the server-level value (and so also has to remember the server-level value from the beginning, as well as the realm-level value, in case that happens). At that point it's not clear the client has gained any simplicity vs. just saying `realm_jitsi_server_url ?? server_jitsi_server_url` whenever it needs to know the current effective value.

So in order for the server to successfully take some complexity load off the shoulders of a client that doesn't care about an org settings UI and just needs to know the value currently in effect, it probably needs to emit an event that specifically updates the value-in-effect. Which in particular means that when the realm-level setting gets cleared, it'll need to say that that's now null and separately say that the value-in-effect is now whatever it is (namely, whatever the server-level setting is).

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-09-13 03:55 UTC

Recipe:

1. Log into two accounts on web: Account A and Account B.
2. Ensure there's a stream that Account A is subscribed to and Account B is not. Call it Stream A.
3. Ensure both accounts are subscribed to a particular stream (a different one). Call it Stream B.
4. As Account B, open up Stream B.
5. As Account A, send a new message in Stream A (to ensure it's the latest message).
6. As Account A, move that message to Stream B. (Simplest for the experiment to uncheck the boxes about sending bot messages about the move.)

    # means if a non-subscriber is viewing the narrow, they won't get
    # a real-time updates. This is a balance between sending
    # message-edit notifications for every public stream to every user
    # in the organization (too expansive, and also not what we do for
    # newly sent messages anyway) and having magical live-updates
    # where possible.
    users_to_be_notified = list(map(user_info, ums))
    if stream_being_edited is not None and stream_being_edited.is_history_public_to_subscribers():
        subscriptions = get_active_subscriptions_for_stream_id(
            stream_id, include_deactivated_users=False
        )
        # We exclude long-term idle users, since they by
        # definition have no active clients.
        subscriptions = subscriptions.exclude(user_profile__long_term_idle=True)
        # Remove duplicates by excluding the id of users already
        # in users_to_be_notified list.  This is the case where a
        # user both has a UserMessage row and is a current
        # Subscriber
        subscriptions = subscriptions.exclude(
            user_profile_id__in=[um.user_profile_id for um in ums]
        )

        if new_stream is not None:
            subscriptions = subscriptions.exclude(user_profile_id__in=losing_access_user_ids)

        # All users that are subscribed to the stream must be
        # notified when a message is edited
        subscriber_ids = set(subscriptions.values_list("user_profile_id", flat=True))

        if new_stream is not None:
            # TODO: Guest users don't see the new moved topic
            # unless breadcrumb message for new stream is
            # enabled. Excluding these users from receiving this
            # event helps us avoid a error traceback for our
            # clients. We should figure out a way to inform the
            # guest users of this new topic if sending a 'message'
            # event for these messages is not an option.
            #
            # Don't send this event to guest subs who are not
            # subscribers of the old stream but are subscribed to
            # the new stream; clients will be confused.
            old_stream_unsubbed_guests = [
                sub
                for sub in subs_to_new_stream
                if sub.user_profile.is_guest and sub.user_profile_id not in subscriber_ids
            ]
            subscriptions = subscriptions.exclude(
                user_profile_id__in=[sub.user_profile_id for sub in old_stream_unsubbed_guests]
            )
            subscriber_ids = set(subscriptions.values_list("user_profile_id", flat=True))

        users_to_be_notified += list(map(subscriber_info, sorted(subscriber_ids)))
```

`ums` is the `UserMessage` objects with for the target message after excluding the obejcts which will lose access due to the move.

## mark-as-read events with message moves?

*2023-09-13 to 2025-02-26 · 50 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/mark-as-read.20events.20with.20message.20moves.3F/with/1639275)*

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-09-13 03:41 UTC

When unread messages are moved from a stream I'm subscribed to, to a stream I'm *not* subscribed to, those messages' state on the server becomes read. (Confirmed empirically, and see [discussion](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/3-backend/topic/update.20has_message_access.3F/near/1638961): "Zulip has an invariant that all unread messages must be in streams the user is subscribed to". That invariant is an interesting part of the API that would be good to document.)

The client should update its unreads data structure to mirror the server's state.

I think we can accomplish that without API changes: empirically, clients get an `update_message` event if messages are moved this way (as I noted in a [different thread](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/378-api-design/topic/messages.20moved.20from.20unsubscribed.20to.20subscribed.20stream/near/1639249)), so I think we could just handle that.

However, that would be inconsistent with how we're meant to handle a different case of messages exiting a subscribed stream (and so getting marked "read" on the server): the case where you simply unsubscribe from the stream. There, [we get explicit mark-as-read events](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/412-api-documentation/topic/mark-as-read.20events.20on.20stream.20unsubscribe/near/1639261), which clients will of course be handling.

I think I'd be OK with that inconsistency, but wanted to mention it in case there’s some deeper problem I’m not aware of. :smile:

That invariant is an interesting part of the API that would be good to document.

(Following a couple of links, here's previous discussion of that invariant in more detail:
https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/378-api-design/topic/unreads.20in.20unsubscribed.20streams/near/1456534

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-09-13 05:50 UTC

I see, thanks for that context. It sounds like we were unsure at first whether we want the invariant, but:
1. We decided we do, and
2. It remains "soft". Servers want to uphold it and will work toward upholding it, but might not uphold it at all times. In at least the following case, the invariant is broken, hopefully for a short time. The server doesn't mark a stream "unsubscribed" and mark its messages as read in the same transaction, so there will be a period where the former is done but the latter is not. (I guess the client gets a clue about this, in the fact that the two actions are signaled by a stream-unsubscribed event and [a mark-as-read event](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/412-api-documentation/topic/mark-as-read.20events.20on.20stream.20unsubscribe/near/1639261) separately.)

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-09-13 05:55 UTC

Despite the wrinkle in 2, I think it’s probably OK for clients to keep the invariant in their own data structures, if that’s what they want to do. Even if that means their state isn’t a perfect replica of the server’s for some of the time.

**Greg Price** · 2023-09-13 22:03 UTC

I think that approach can basically be OK, but is tricky because it means that now when you're interpreting subsequent events, you're starting from a state that isn't quite the same as the one the server expects you to be starting from.

For the unreads model for stream messages in zulip-mobile (which is one of the areas that we built relatively recently, and I'm basically happy with), the approach we took was instead:
* The data structures take the event stream literally, so as to stay in sync with the state in the server's database. This means that the unreads model doesn't respond to `subscription/remove` events — any unreads in the unsubscribed stream remain present in the unreads data structure, until a subsequent `update_message_flags` event removes them.
* But then when *reading* the model to present its information to the user, we suppress unsubscribed streams, so that this soft invariant does hold in the UI.

**Greg Price** · 2023-09-13 22:04 UTC

In the function in `unreadSelectors.js` that prepares the data for the unreads/inbox screen:
```js
    for (const [streamId, streamData] of unreadStreams.entries()) {
      const subscription = subscriptionsById.get(streamId);
      if (!subscription) {
        // We have a loose invariant that you can't have unreads in a stream
        // you're not subscribed to.  It's "loose" because when you unsubscribe
        // from a stream you had unreads in, the server only asynchronously
        // marks them as read:
        //   https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/378-api-design/topic/unreads.20in.20unsubscribed.20streams/near/1456534
        // In the UI, though, we generally want to fix things up so that
        // it's as if the invariant were a real invariant.  So if we find
        // some supposed "unreads" in a stream with no subscription,
        // avert our eyes; those "unread" records don't count.
        continue;
      }
```

export function update_unread_topics(                                                                   
    msg: Message & {type: "stream"},                                                                    
    event: UpdateMessageEvent,                                                                          
): void {                                                                                               
    const new_topic = util.get_edit_event_topic(event);                                                 
    const {new_stream_id} = event;                                                                      
                                                                                                        
    if (new_topic === undefined && new_stream_id === undefined) {

    unread_topic_counter.delete(msg.id);                                                                
                                                                                                        
    unread_topic_counter.add({                                                                          
        message_id: msg.id,                                                                             
        stream_id: new_stream_id ?? msg.stream_id,                                                      
        topic: new_topic ?? msg.topic,                                                                  
    });                                                                                                 
}                                                                                                       
```

*2023-09-18 to 2025-02-26 · 29 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Send.20group.20settings.20configuration.20data.20to.20client/with/1642366)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-09-18 18:29 UTC

Currently, we define the configuration for a group setting (i.e. can the setting be set to only system groups and which of them are allowed, the default group for the setting) in [backend in `models.py`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/e5f7f1701ff4423170c88ec1ade4eef0e8663b18/zerver/models.py#L762) and in [the web-app](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/e5f7f1701ff4423170c88ec1ade4eef0e8663b18/web/src/group_permission_settings.ts#L9) as well.

@Tim Abbott [suggested](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/25884#issuecomment-1709240370) that we should instead sent this data from server to client and not define them in client. We can send these in `/register` response (that means in `page_params` object for the web-app) and can have 3 different fields - one for realm level settings, one for stream-level settings and one for group-level settings.

If this idea sounds good, would be good to have some suggestions for naming of these fields. One that I can think of is `realm_group_permission_settings_configuration`, or maybe some shorter word to replace `configuration` and similarly for stream-level and group-level settings as well.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-18 22:52 UTC

Maybe something like `server_supported_permission_settings`? It's a function of the server version, not the organization.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-18 22:52 UTC

I am a bit hesitant about adding something like this to the API because we're not entirely sure what the long-term set of properties should be. But at the same time, I don't think hand-syncing this sort of configuration between client implementations and the server is going to work at all:
```
        "can_remove_subscribers_group",
        {
            require_system_group: true,
            allow_internet_group: false,
            allow_owners_group: false,
            allow_nobody_group: false,
            allow_everyone_group: true,
        },
```

And while the immediate solution for that might be "don't implement group-based settings that the mobile apps  need to understand yet", I think ultimately we are going to need an API of this form.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-26 16:44 UTC

Yeah, we can do this.

## user group deactivation/reactivation API

*2023-09-21 to 2024-06-05 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/user.20group.20deactivation.2Freactivation.20API/with/1644262)*

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-09-21 02:45 UTC

We are planning to implement user group deactivation (previous discussion: #**design>Support user group deactivation**) to replace user group deletion.

The proposal is that we change the behavior of `DELETE /user_groups/{user_group_id}` so that it will deactivate, replace the internal code that handles deletion with deactivation, and add a new endpoint `POST /user_groups/{user_group_id}/reactivate` that handles reactivation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-22 22:12 UTC

@Zixuan James Li that sounds very reasonable for the URLs part of the plan.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-22 22:13 UTC

The other direction one could do is just add `deactivated` as a flag one can toggle in `PATCH /user_groups/{user_group_id}` , but we've not gone in that direction with users/streams/realm, so I don't see a reason to consider that here.

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-05-29 07:38 UTC

As we recently discussed in #**design>Support user group deactivation**, we do not want to support complete deletion of groups for now.

So just wanted to confirm it once that we should proceed to use the endpoints as discussed above, i.e. the existing delete endpoint `DELETE /user_groups/{user_group_id}` for deactivation and `POST /user_groups/{user_group_id}/reactivate` for reactivation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-29 18:59 UTC

Those URLs sound good to me.

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-29 22:07 UTC

When we're giving an endpoint a meaning that's more nuanced than outright deleting a thing, it'd be better to avoid using the `DELETE` method. Instead it can be `POST` at an appropriate URL path.

This is similar to the point @Anders Kaseorg raised a little while ago at #**api design>Invalid HTTP DELETE requests**:

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> I think this is just one of many manifestations of how “REST-style” is nonsense. HTTP verbs should be selected for their properties as defined by the HTTP standard, not for their loose analogies with the concepts in your API.

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-29 22:09 UTC

This particular example wouldn't be invalid in the mechanically-detectable way that the examples in that thread are, because it doesn't involve sending any parameters in the body. But it still doesn't fit with the [defined semantics of `DELETE`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-delete):
> The DELETE method requests that the origin server remove the association between the [target resource](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#target.resource) and its current functionality. In effect, this method is similar to the "rm" command in UNIX: it expresses a deletion operation on the URI mapping of the origin server rather than an expectation that the previously associated information be deleted.

**Greg Price** · 2024-05-29 22:09 UTC

So for example
`POST /user_groups/{user_group_id}/deactivate`

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-05-29 23:08 UTC

Oh right, yeah we should do that.

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-06-03 11:40 UTC

As discussed in #**design>Support user group deactivation** , we would want to allow the users to rename the deactivated group name if user wants to rename an active group to the name which is already used by a deactivated group.
We already have code in webapp to check whether there already exists a group with the same name that is being used for creating a new group. So, it makes sense to handle this in client as well instead of first passing the server a request and then doing something like sending a specific error code which client will interpret as "need to update the name" and will show the UI accordingly.

To do this, we would need to send the data for deactivated groups as well to the clients with the `/register` response. How we would prefer to do that?
We could just sent active and deactivated groups in separate objects like we do for users. We currently use `realm_user_groups` field and we can keep using it for active groups and we can add a field like `realm_deactivated_user_groups` for the deactivated groups.

Other way can be to include them in existing `realm_user_groups` field with each entry containing `deactivated` field and let clients handle it, but that would be issue for older clients like deactivated groups would be shown in mention typeaheads.

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-06-03 18:33 UTC

Also any suggestion regarding the event to send on deactivation?
We currently send `user_groups/remove` event for deletion, so maybe we can just send that or do something similar to what we do for user where we send `update` event with `is_active` field, which can be `deactivated` field for groups.

**Greg Price** · 2024-06-05 04:48 UTC

(replying to Sahil Batra)
> We could just sent active and deactivated groups in separate objects like we do for users. We currently use `realm_user_groups` field and we can keep using it for active groups and we can add a field like `realm_deactivated_user_groups` for the deactivated groups.

I'd much prefer to avoid this option. The similar thing which we do for users is a longstanding wart in the API, which caused a series of bugs in zulip-mobile that lasted for several years and took me quite a lot of refactoring to remove. So it'd be better not to create more pitfalls of that kind.


> Other way can be to include them in existing `realm_user_groups` field with each entry containing `deactivated` field and let clients handle it, but that would be issue for older clients like deactivated groups would be shown in mention typeaheads.

I would prefer this over the `realm_deactivated_user_groups` option. It'd cause some incompatibility, but shouldn't be catastrophic; and then it leaves the API in a reasonable state for the future.

**Greg Price** · 2024-06-05 04:48 UTC

A third option, the way to really nail the compatibility without messing up the API for the long term, would be to add a client capability. Could e.g. call it:
`deactivated_user_groups`
or
`user_groups_include_deactivated`

**Greg Price** · 2024-06-05 04:51 UTC

(replying to Sahil Batra)
> Also any suggestion regarding the event to send on deactivation? We currently send `user_groups/remove` event for deletion, so maybe we can just send that or do something similar to what we do for user where we send `update` event with `is_active` field, which can be `deactivated` field for groups.

Doing the same pattern as for users sounds like a good plan.

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-06-05 06:55 UTC

Third option of adding a client compatibility sounds good. I guess the major use of user groups in the current mobile (and possibly terminal) clients would be to mention them and would not need the deactivated groups data, which can be done by adding a client compatibility.

**Greg Price** · 2024-06-05 19:15 UTC

Yeah exactly. The only thing mobile currently uses user groups for is in autocomplete for @-mentions.


## Push bouncer endpoints namespaces

*2023-09-21 to 2023-09-21 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Push.20bouncer.20endpoints.20namespaces/with/1644516)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2023-09-21 13:35 UTC

Currently our push bouncer endpoints get registered under both `/api/v1/....` and `/json/...`:
```
# Zilencer views following the REST API style
v1_api_and_json_patterns = [
    remote_server_path("remotes/push/register", POST=register_remote_push_device),
    remote_server_path("remotes/push/unregister", POST=unregister_remote_push_device),
    remote_server_path("remotes/push/unregister/all", POST=unregister_all_remote_push_devices),
    remote_server_path("remotes/push/notify", POST=remote_server_notify_push),
    # Push signup doesn't use the REST API, since there's no auth.
    path("remotes/server/register", register_remote_server),
    remote_server_path("remotes/server/deactivate", POST=deactivate_remote_server),
    # For receiving table data used in analytics and billing
    remote_server_path("remotes/server/analytics", POST=remote_server_post_analytics),
    remote_server_path("remotes/server/analytics/status", GET=remote_server_check_analytics),
]

urlpatterns = [
    path("api/v1/", include(v1_api_and_json_patterns)),
    path("json/", include(v1_api_and_json_patterns)),
]
```

Is there any reason we're doing this? A remote server authenticates with http basic auth, and I don't think we ever use sessions, so I don't think `/json/...` makes any sense?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-21 15:20 UTC

No that's probably just being lazy, we should cut the /json/ versions, good find.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2023-09-21 16:35 UTC

#26804

As discussed in the design thread, there's currently two pretty different scenarios that both use this field:
* A user account imported from a third-party chat product like Slack via a data import process that has never been logged into.
* A user account that was automatically created to serve as the displayed sender for messages sent by software mirroring content with a third-party chat tool, like the Zephyr mirror (but it has been used with IRC/XMPP as well).

I think it'd make sense to have two flags, given that these are pretty different scenarios (which clients will want to display differently) and given that it's been the same list of two for years and we don't foresee adding a third.

I'd want each of the flags to be present only when true, so that in typical cases the user objects don't get bigger. The user lists are the biggest part of the /api/register-queue response in large open organizations, and there's a cost to letting them grow. The cost in physical network transmission should be mitigated by compression; but then the uncompressed version occupies memory on the client device, and has to be deserialized from JSON (occupying more memory, as well as CPU).

```py
def need_accept_tos(user_profile: UserProfile | None) -> bool:
    if user_profile is None:
        return False

    if user_profile.tos_version == UserProfile.TOS_VERSION_BEFORE_FIRST_LOGIN:
        return True

    if settings.TERMS_OF_SERVICE_VERSION is None:
        return False

    return int(settings.TERMS_OF_SERVICE_VERSION.split(".")[0]) > user_profile.major_tos_version()

```

```
def login_and_go_to_home(request: HttpRequest, user_profile: UserProfile) -> HttpResponse:
    mobile_flow_otp = get_expirable_session_var(
        request.session, "registration_mobile_flow_otp", delete=True
    )
    desktop_flow_otp = get_expirable_session_var(
        request.session, "registration_desktop_flow_otp", delete=True
    )
    if mobile_flow_otp is not None:
        return finish_mobile_flow(request, user_profile, mobile_flow_otp)
```

so if you're doing this from mobile, you won't go to `/` - but instead a `zulip://` redirect will be served, delivering your account's API key to the mobile app.

## register: maintaining `unread_msgs.mentions` correctly

*2023-09-29 to 2023-10-24 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/register.3A.20maintaining.20.60unread_msgs.2Ementions.60.20correctly/with/1649584)*

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-09-29 00:38 UTC

As I've [foreshadowed](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/412-api-documentation/topic/register.3A.20.60unread_msgs.2Ementions.60/near/1645170) [a](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/412-api-documentation/topic/unreads.3A.20messages.20from.20muted.20users.3F/near/1646697) [bit](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/412-api-documentation/topic/unreads.3A.20messages.20from.20muted.20users.3F/near/1646829) recently, I'd like to point out that the design of the "unreads" subsystem doesn't yet support correctly maintaining a `mentions` component. :smile:

Here's the doc for the snapshot in `/register` that's meant to initialize this component (following a small bugfix in zulip/zulip#26848):

> Array containing the IDs of all unread messages in which the user was mentioned directly, and unread [non-muted](/help/mute-a-topic) messages in which the user was mentioned through a wildcard. **Changes**: Before Zulip 8.0 (feature level 213), the unmute and follow topic features were not handled c …

The important surprise there is that the server deliberately represents some unread messages indistinguishably from read ones. (I.e., unread [muted](https://chat.zulip.org/help/mute-a-topic) stream messages that are wildcard- but not directly mentioned.) So, as a statement of which mentioned messages are known to be unread, it's not true.

Probably the intended statement is different, like "the set of unread mentions that deserve highlighting in the UI", with a helpful-sounding bit about which messages those are. But for clients who want to keep track of that set across time, it reads as a prompt to go look for and study the relevant events. As it turns out, though, there isn't a pair of events designed to announce a message's entrance or exit from that set. And the data structure doesn't hold enough data for the client to interpret events that *do* exist into all the relevant state changes the doc brings to mind:
- an unread, [muted](https://chat.zulip.org/help/mute-a-topic) message that's directly mentioned becomes only wildcard-mentioned; it should disappear from `mentions`
- an unread, [muted](https://chat.zulip.org/help/mute-a-topic) message with no mention becomes only wildcard-mentioned; it should not appear in `mentions`
- an unread, [muted](https://chat.zulip.org/help/mute-a-topic) message that was only wildcard-mentioned becomes directly mentioned; it should appear in `mentions`
- a message becomes read or unread: `mentions` should either change or not change, depending on whether the message is [muted](https://chat.zulip.org/help/mute-a-topic) and only wildcard-mentioned
- the user's choices about the stream or topic change such that an unread, only-wildcard-mentioned message becomes muted
- the user's choices about the stream or topic change such that an unread, only-wildcard-mentioned message stops being muted

Also, I think even if clients had what they needed to handle those state changes and maintain `mentions` correctly, doing so would make the system pretty brittle, since the meaning of "unread mentions that deserve highlighting in the UI" is likely to change as the product evolves.

-----

To see some buggy behavior that I think follows from this design bug, please try these steps in the web app:

1. Have two users join a private stream by themselves; call them User A and User B. The stream should be muted by User B.
2. Make sure User B won't automatically mark-as-read messages in the stream
3. Have User A send a message in the stream with an `@all` mention
4. As User B, notice an "@" sign appear by the stream, even though it's muted and the mention wasn't direct (unexpected)
4. Have User B refresh the page to reload data
5. As User B, notice that the "@" sign is absent (expected)
6. But have User B unmute the stream, taking care not to mark the message as read while doing so
7. As User B, notice that the stream has no "@" sign by it, even though it's unmuted and it has a mention in it (unexpected)

and then, just for fun:

8. As User A, edit the message's text to add "asdf" at the end and save
9. As User B, see the "@" sign is now visible, as it should have been since step 6

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-09-29 00:47 UTC

## guest user indicator #26766

*2023-10-04 to 2023-10-04 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/guest.20user.20indicator.20.2326766/with/1654199)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-04 00:19 UTC

So in #26766, we're adding a pseudo-security feature that prominently displays ` (guest)` next to all guest users in an organization. The current proposed interface is a `enable_guest_user_indicator` realm setting. Thoughts on that name?

The other high-level API design I can imagine is one where we instead have a `guest_user_indicator` string-type setting, which if null does nothing, but if specified is the string to use. (A use case I could imagine is if all of your guests are "students" or "contractors", one could set this to "(student)" or whatever ... at a cost to internationalization, since presumably whatever string you pick would be the same for everyone in the organization, not translated into your personal language.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-04 00:20 UTC

I'm tempted to integrate this feature in its current form and if we want to do something fancier, try to build it around groups.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-04 00:20 UTC

I believe this is a feature we would probably want to implement a version of in other client apps, but not necessarily with much urgency.

**Greg Price** · 2023-10-04 01:57 UTC

That design sounds fine.

I agree that for a fancier version, it'd be good to build it on top of groups. That way it's possible for a realm to have several different kinds of such labels — I'm thinking of how some large tech companies have "contractors" and "temps" and "vendors" all as distinct categories, for example.

Also just if some realm does want to use a custom term like "student" or "contractor", I imagine it'd be common that that term wouldn't cover quite 100% of what they use the Zulip "guest" feature for. So it might be hard to successfully use a custom term without the ability to decouple it from all the other things the Zulip "guest" feature does.

**Greg Price** · 2023-10-04 02:01 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> I believe this is a feature we would probably want to implement a version of in other client apps, but not necessarily with much urgency.

Because the use case for this feature has a security flavor to it, I feel like it's one where a relatively high part of the value of the feature is in making sure it appears on everyone's clients. And conversely, it should be a pretty simple feature to implement. So I think this likely falls into the category where I'd want to implement it for zulip-mobile, i.e. to implement it for mobile in the near term before we roll out zulip-flutter.

Concretely, if that issue is on the 8.0 priorities board, I'd want to fill in the "Mobile" field as "maybe", so that it appears on the list of features to consider implementing for mobile before the 8.0 release:
https://github.com/orgs/zulip/projects/6/views/3

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-04 17:27 UTC

Yeah, I think this is reasonable. The web app implementation is a bit fancy in that it displays the name in italics in some places where that'll look nicer, but I think we can skip that sort of embellishment for zulip-mobile.

Discussion regarding #26900

When we send a message and that causes a topic to be automatically followed or unmuted, we should tell the user via a post-send-message banner.

Here's the proposed API design:

In the response of [`/api/send-message`](https://zulip.com/api/send-message), we should send an optional `boolean` field named `visibility_policy_changed`.

thoughts?

E.g. if we wanted a "You are now following this topic" banner to appear after sending the message, that's a lot easier to implement if we return the new visibility policy.

So I would propose a `new_visibility_policy` enum response.

## Invalid HTTP DELETE requests

*2023-10-23 to 2023-10-24 · 24 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Invalid.20HTTP.20DELETE.20requests/with/1667168)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-10-23 06:27 UTC

These five API endpoints expect parameters in a `DELETE` method request body, which has no defined semantics in the HTTP standard.

- `DELETE /default_streams`
- `DELETE /messages/{message_id}/reactions`
- `DELETE /users/me/alert_words`
- `DELETE /users/me/subscriptions`
- `DELETE /users/{user_id}`

From [RFC 9110 §9.3.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-9.3.5-6):

> Although request message framing is independent of the method used, content received in a DELETE request has no generally defined semantics, cannot alter the meaning or target of the request, and might lead some implementations to reject the request and close the connection because of its potential as a request smuggling attack ([Section 11.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112#section-11.2) of [[HTTP/1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#HTTP11)]). A client SHOULD NOT generate content in a DELETE request unless it is made directly to an origin server that has previously indicated, in or out of band, that such a request has a purpose and will be adequately supported. An origin server SHOULD NOT rely on private agreements to receive content, since participants in HTTP communication are often unaware of intermediaries along the request chain.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2023-10-23 06:34 UTC

This is also a problem from an OpenAPI perspective (once we fix the more egregious problem that our specification of request bodies is 100% bogus: #**api documentation>OpenAPI requestBody**). From the [OpenAPI 3.0.3 standard](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.0.3#fixed-fields-7):

> The `requestBody` is only supported in HTTP methods where the HTTP 1.1 specification [[RFC7231](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.0.3#bib-RFC7231)] has explicitly defined semantics for request bodies. In other cases where the HTTP spec is vague, `requestBody` SHALL be ignored by consumers.

This language was slightly loosened in [OpenAPI 3.1.0](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0#fixed-fields-7) (to which we haven’t yet upgraded) but still gives no defined semantics:

> The `requestBody` is fully supported in HTTP methods where the HTTP 1.1 specification [[RFC7231](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0#bib-RFC7231)] has explicitly defined semantics for request bodies. In other cases where the HTTP spec is vague (such as [GET](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-4.3.1), [HEAD](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-4.3.2) and [DELETE](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-4.3.5)), `requestBody` is permitted but does not have well-defined semantics and SHOULD be avoided if possible.
