**Greg Price** · 2023-10-30 23:21 UTC

I think if zulip-mobile gets a `realm_user`/`add` event for a user that already exists as a deactivated user, the effect will actually be that not much happens — most of our code will continue to treat the user as deactivated.

That's because zulip-mobile's data structures for users follow the peculiarity of the API where the `realm_users` list (in /api/register-queue ) excludes system bots and deactivated users, and the latter come in two separate lists `cross_realm_bots` and `realm_non_active_users`. The latter two get treated separately, stored in a separate part of the state and managed by the corresponding separate part of the code. Then — just as one might predict once those categories are handled in separate parts of the code — a lot of the things that ought to apply uniformly across all three categories only get applied to the one most salient category (the users in `realm_users`) and the others are forgotten.

There's a lot less of that non-uniformity now than there was early on — I spent some time clearing up a lot of it several years ago — but it's still there in the maintenance of the data structures. (Partly, at the time, I had too much of an assumption that there was some good reason the code and the API had that structure, and paid too much respect to the existing code: moving incrementally step by step, and leaving things in place until I worked out 100% of the implications of changing them.)

The effect is that if we get such a `realm_user`/`add` event, we'll add the user to the `state.users` list… but there'll still be the version over in `state.realm.nonActiveUsers`. And when the two are combined by the `getAllUsers` selector, the latter is the version that will win because it comes last.

**Greg Price** · 2023-10-30 23:21 UTC

So we may as well not send those events — there's no material compatibility benefit to doing so.

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-01 18:07 UTC

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-01 18:08 UTC

**Greg Price** · 2023-11-01 19:54 UTC

Yeah, "deprecated" is a bit of an understatement here. Could perhaps say this instead:

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-03 04:04 UTC

The PR is now merged.

Now for losing guest user access to users, do we want to use `remove` event or a new `delete` event like we do for bots?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-08 17:03 UTC

Is this just a naming question for what we want to call it when a user ceases to exist for the current user (either due to some sort of hard deletion or losing access to the other user)?

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-08 17:44 UTC

Just a naming question for a event that we would sent for losing access to the other (at least for now as we do not send any events other than the ones sent with deactivation when we delete a user). I was asking this because we have already document `remove `event which we do not send anymore (and it also passed `full_name` field in the user object which is not needed) and `delete` event would make it consistent with what we use for bots.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-08 18:30 UTC

Probably `delete` is better, since this will be the main event used for completely deleting a user, but I don't have strong feelings.

**Greg Price** · 2023-11-09 01:15 UTC

I happened to have a list of all Zulip's documented event types and type/op pairs, in #F135, so I took a quick look there for existing patterns in our names.

We have op `delete` for 2 event types: `stream` and `realm_bot`.

We have op `remove` for 10 event types: `realm_user`, `reaction`, `update_message_flags`, `subscription`, `user_group`, `attachment`, `drafts`, `scheduled_messages`, `realm_domains`, `realm_bot`. We have variants in a further two cases `user_group`/`remove_members` and `user_group`/`remove_subgroups`.

So I think using `remove` would be best. That makes it consistent with our naming in the rest of the events, which is good for predictability.

## "Automatically follow topics where I'm mentioned" setting.

*2023-11-22 to 2023-12-10 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/.22Automatically.20follow.20topics.20where.20I.27m.20mentioned.22.20setting.2E/with/1687285)*

**Kunal Sharma** · 2023-11-22 09:36 UTC

I have opened [a PR](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/27174) regarding issue [#26795](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/26795) which adds a setting that lets users automatically follow topics where they are mentioned.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-22 17:46 UTC

This is not a good way to start an API design discussion. We need to present what the proposal is:

> * [`PATCH /realm/user_settings_defaults`](/api/update-realm-user-settings-defaults), [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue), [`PATCH /settings`](/api/update-settings): Added a new user setting,`automatically_follow_topics_where_mentioned` that allows user to automatically follow topics where the us …

And then in `zulip.yaml:
> Whether to automatically follow the topics where mentioned. **Changes**: New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 228). schema: type: boolean example: true

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-22 17:47 UTC

So there's a few things to talk about here. 

One is the setting's format -- `automatically_follow_topics_where_mentioned` as a boolean flag. I think if we want to make the setting more complicated, it's probably going to be in the direction of per-stream overrides, not additional options that might suggest an `enum`, and I think this choice of name fits well alongside `automatically_follow_topics_policy` and `automatically_unmute_topics_in_muted_streams_policy`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-22 17:49 UTC

And the second is its semantics. First is just what software is responsible for enforcing the setting.

> Whether to automatically follow the topics where mentioned.

is completely ambiguous about that. I propose for that detail:

> Whether the server will automatically mark the user as following topics where the user is mentioned.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-22 17:52 UTC

And then the other semantics detail is how this feature interacts with wildcard mentions -- does a wildcard mention make you follow the topic where it occurred? I don't really want the extra complexity of having this be an enum where you pick from one of several options around this -- it seems like just too much subtle complexity leaking through to the UI, especially since we already have the `wildcard_mentions_notify` setting for whether you should get notifications from wildcard mentions.

But I suppose one thought is that we could connect those two features, such that if the `wildcard_mentions_notify` for the user as processed for this message (e.g. including per-stream overrides, etc.) means the wildcard mention isn't being treated for this user as notifiable, then we'd not auto-follow the user to the topic. I'm not sure whether or not that would be a good idea, but it seems like it might be?

We will want to add a sentence to the API documentation description clarifying that detail, and also it'll be something that potentially goes into the /help/ documentation for the feature.

**Kunal Sharma** · 2023-11-22 18:51 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> This is not a good way to start an API design discussion. We need to present what the proposal is:
Sorry for that. This was my first time for starting api discussion.

**Kunal Sharma** · 2023-11-22 18:59 UTC

I will make necessary changes in zulip.yaml.

I think it makes sense for this setting to only consider users where ```wildcard_mentions_notify``` is True for wildcard mentions.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-22 21:05 UTC

OK -- I think that `wildcard_mentions_notify` interaction fits my intuition as well -- how hard is that to implement?

**Kunal Sharma** · 2023-11-22 21:48 UTC

## client capability for sending unknown users data

*2023-11-22 to 2023-12-04 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/client.20capability.20for.20sending.20unknown.20users.20data/with/1687602)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-22 17:46 UTC

We discussed about adding client capability to send the unknown users data in the `realm_users` field of `register` response in #**api design>unknown user IDs**. Wanted feedback about name and how we will use it.

 Apart from the `register` response, we would also check the client capability when sending user creation events. We currently send event with bogus data to all the guests, and we can not send those based on the client capability.

For `GET /users` endpoint, we can add a parameter to decide whether to include unknown users data or not. We currently inlcude the unknown users data.

For endpoints like `GET /users/{user_id}` and `GET /users/{email}`, we return error if a user tries to get inaccessible user.

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-22 17:46 UTC

Regarding name, we can probably have something like `require_inaccessible_users_data`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-22 17:53 UTC

Hmm, that name seems a bit inverted -- we want something that's a positive capability of the client.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-22 17:54 UTC

I think something like `supports_incomplete_realm_users` might be a good choice? It directly references the field that specifying you have this capability modifies, and is framed in the positive sense of "A client turns this on if it has the feature of supporting this situation".

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-23 03:41 UTC

Yes, that seems like a good name.

**Greg Price** · 2023-11-28 06:26 UTC

Looking at the [existing values](https://zulip.com/api/register-queue#parameter-client_capabilities) we have for `client_capabilities`, I think a way that'd match the form of those would be `realm_users_incomplete`.

That is, "supports" is implicit in the meaning of the `client_capabilities` list itself; and usually the part of the API it's about comes first, and then the modifier for how that part of the API behaves comes after that.

**Greg Price** · 2023-11-28 06:31 UTC

Thinking about the name a bit further, though, "`realm_users`" seems a bit over-specific. That's the name of one property within the /api/register-queue response, but that particular property is already less than the full list of users: there's `realm_non_active_users`, and `cross_realm_bots`.

IIUC this setting affects `realm_non_active_users` as well as `realm_users` (and I'm not sure if it also affects `cross_realm_bots`), so just "`realm_users`" doesn't cover everything it does; plus "`realm_users` can be incomplete" sounds a lot like the description of how things always have been.

(Also the existence of these three separate lists has long felt to me like not our best work in API design. So I'd prefer to avoid naming further pieces of the API after those names.)

**Greg Price** · 2023-11-28 06:31 UTC

With that in mind, perhaps something like `user_list_incomplete`?

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-28 07:23 UTC

We are keeping access to cross-realm bots for everyone including all the guests, so this should not affect `cross_realm_bots`.

And regarding the `realm_non_active_users` list, we decided to keep `is_active` as `True` for all unknown users, so even when the data for unknown users is included, they would always be included in `realm_users` list only.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-11-28 18:34 UTC

I think that's fine -- that kind of detail might change in the future. And `user_list_incomplete` seems clear enough?

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-04 01:42 UTC

BTW @Sahil Batra when you have an implementation of this client capability, please mention the PR here. Then we can implement the client side of it and test end-to-end that everything works smoothly as intended.

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-04 01:43 UTC

In particular that'll let us keep unknown users out of some UIs where they don't belong, which will be a nice cleanup for people using Zulip as guest users; details at https://github.com/zulip/zulip-mobile/issues/5787#issuecomment-1837706706 .


## passing realm.host in message event

*2023-11-30 to 2023-12-22 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/passing.20realm.2Ehost.20in.20message.20event/with/1692000)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2023-11-30 03:29 UTC

As done in [this commit](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/27944/files/9173c789076db59d0e8128fda3fac9f3feb03aa0..21c99339debcac233660b33a3b4461794dcf49ef#diff-fb9fbf142b94b64da12cd59aa089840524a6f39d619ae839e1d7f6edc1433882), we would need `realm.host` value in the message event such that we can compute the fake email of the sender to be used for `sender_email` field in the message event sent to users who cannot access sender.

## test notification: unexpected error message

*2023-12-02 to 2023-12-06 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/test.20notification.3A.20unexpected.20error.20message/with/1693312)*

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 00:48 UTC

Hmm. In my draft for the "send test notification" button, I tapped the button on CZO on an iOS development build, just to see what would happen. I didn't expect it to actually send a test notification; see this bit of our doc on how to test client-side push-notification logic on iOS:

https://github.com/zulip/zulip-mobile/blob/main/docs/howto/push-notifications.md#testing-client-side-changes-on-ios
> APNs […] does not allow our production bouncer to send notifications to a development build of the app.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 00:49 UTC

But I think the error message I got from `POST /mobile_push/test_notification` might have been wrong:

> Device not recognized by the push bouncer

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 00:51 UTC

What does it mean for the device to be recognized by the push bouncer? Didn't it fail because of an Apple policy, and not because of a data problem within the bouncer?

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-12-02 01:28 UTC

@Chris Bobbe the only cause for that error message is that the device token has not previously been registered with the push bouncer service.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-12-02 01:28 UTC

So the typical cause is not having called `remotes/push/register` with the test device.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 01:33 UTC

Ah OK, so it sounds like the push bouncer keeps its own record of devices, just like the org's own Zulip server does; I'm glad to be reminded of that detail.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 01:35 UTC

I see in the [`POST /mobile_push/test_notification` doc](https://chat.zulip.org/api/test-notify) that it might error with "Device not recognized", and it might error with "Device not recognized by the push bouncer". So the org's server and the push bouncer both need to have a record for the device, or presumably the test notification will fail.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 01:35 UTC

And it sounds like in this case, the push bouncer did not have a record. I think CZO would have had a record; if not, I think I would have gotten "Device not recognized" instead.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 01:36 UTC

Is there some client behavior that would cause the device to be registered with the org's server but not with the bouncer? Could Apple's policy (of not letting the bouncer send notifications to an app's dev build) have been a factor?

**Chris Bobbe** · 2023-12-02 01:58 UTC

Could the bouncer have *had* a record for the device, but then removed it? In the bouncer's code for handling `remotes/push/register` (it's a function named `register_remote_push_device`), there's code that looks like it deletes a record:

```python
    if user_id is not None and user_uuid is not None:
        kwargs: Dict[str, object] = {"user_uuid": user_uuid, "user_id": None}
        # Delete pre-existing user_id registration for this user+device to avoid
        # duplication. Further down, uuid registration will be created.
        RemotePushDeviceToken.objects.filter(
            server=server, token=token, kind=token_kind, user_id=user_id
        ).delete()
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-12-03 18:27 UTC

Hmm. I think the more likely situation for such a state is that the push bouncer deletes token registrations when it gets certain errors from Apple/Google indicating those are no longer valid.

The code path you point to is not using transactions properly to avoid doing the deletion without the creation step if errors occur... we should probably fix that regardless of whether it might have caused the failure mode you're seeing.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-12-03 18:44 UTC

I guess the case where the bouncer got feedback from Apple/Google to delete the token that I noted is tracked in https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/27483#issuecomment-1806486367.

'ZulipFlutter/0.0.15+15 (macOS, 14.5.0)'

Thanks!

One observation is that looking at examples of other user-agent values:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/User-Agent

**Greg Price** · 2024-06-06 16:45 UTC

Then the other question is those build numbers, the "+15" at the end of "0.0.15+15".

They look a little redundant. But I think my inclination is to keep them.
* That full string "0.0.15+15" is the actual version number of the package, as recorded in our `pubspec.yaml`.
* Even though our [current practice](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/blob/e85d6c5fbc5b5df528c857ba5e23fab7d044296d/docs/release.md#prepare-source-tree), for the beta, is that those last two numbers (here 15 and 15) are equal, I'm not sure what we'll choose for version numbering when the app reaches launch. We might make it something like "1.0.24+24" (in which case the build number stays redundant), or we might go instead for something like "1.0.0+24". So using the full version number, with no assumptions about its structure, leaves us flexibility.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-12-27 05:17 UTC

git grep `TODO/compatibility` would be helpful.

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-28 01:23 UTC

Cool. So, currently each item within `message_details` has an optional property `mentioned: true`.

As I understand it, the proposal is to deprecate that, and replace it with `mentions` which would be an array of strings. More precisely, an array of a string enum: the allowed values would be `direct_mentioned`, `stream_wildcard_mentioned`, `topic_wildcard_mentioned`, `group_mentioned`.

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-28 01:25 UTC

I think the question @Tim Abbott asked above still needs to be answered, which is whether we need to make that distinction here — whether there's some benefit the client would get from it.

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-28 01:31 UTC

Typically a key way of looking at that sort of question is to consider what data structure the client is expected to be maintaining as the events come in.

For these `message_details` objects in particular, the purpose of them is to enable the client to faithfully update the data it got from /api/register-queue under `unread_msgs`.

That data structure has a `mentions` array which is a list of all the message IDs of unread @-mentions (within the window of 50k or so unreads). Updating that is what the `mentioned` property inside `message_details` is for.

It's actually a bit subtle just which unreads count for that list:
> Array containing the IDs of all unread messages in which the user was mentioned directly, and unread non-muted messages in which the user was mentioned through a wildcard.

Looking back at the block comment Tim quoted, it looks like it's talking about that. I guess the comment must be from the web client where it's processing these events?

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-28 01:32 UTC

OK, and so now I understand what the context is of why there's a change being proposed here. The point is to give the client more information in order to correctly update that `mentions` array (or rather, the equivalent of that array in the client's internal data structures).

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-28 01:38 UTC

I think my inclination would be to have the API in the events make only the same set of distinctions that appear in the API for the data structure the events are updating.

That is, the `message_details` objects would distinguish "mentioned directly" from "mentioned through a wildcard" from "not mentioned", because those are part of the definition of which message IDs appear in the `mentions` array. But they wouldn't distinguish all the different flavors of wildcard mention, because those distinctions don't matter to `mentions`.

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-28 01:44 UTC

One thought I have there is that given that there are three flavors of wildcard/indirect @-mention now, it seems quite possible we might come up with a fourth flavor to add in the future.

In the proposal where `message_details` encodes the distinction between those flavors, a client needs to know the list of different flavors and needs to know which ones count even for muted messages and which ones don't. That means that adding a new flavor of @-mention is a breaking change: a client won't be able to know how it should treat those.

But if instead we treat them all together in this API — for example if we make it `mentioned?: 'directly' | 'indirectly'`, so that all three flavors of indirect @-mentions are expressed as `mentioned: 'indirectly'`, then if we add a fourth flavor it can just slot right in with no change to this API at all.

**Greg Price** · 2023-12-28 01:45 UTC

Conversely, if we have an API that expresses only the distinctions that are relevant, and then later end up having to change that API, it can only be because we're doing something actually new in the logic — the API change can only be forced by a genuine behavior change that makes some kind of API change fundamentally necessary.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-04 20:28 UTC

To some extent I wonder if we should pause work on this until we've done a next revision on the main `unread_msgs` data structure and how it encodes mentions -- if it gets extended to send the full set of mention-related message flags like we have in an actual message object, then we'd perhaps want to do the same thing here to parallel that?

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-04 20:34 UTC

Yeah, definitely any change we make to the `unread_msgs` data structure, we'd want a parallel change as needed to the events to support updating the new data structure.

**Yadhira Morales** · 2024-01-18 23:21 UTC

Hi all, this seems to be a bit complex for me so I have closed my PR, but the work I've managed to do is still [available](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/28126). I did have an additional thought about @Greg Price 's proposal, which is that `mentioned?` has no representation for a message with both a direct and an indirect mention. If that is important, then maybe we can use an array that can contain only the values `directly` and `indirectly`, or we can stick with `mentioned?` but add a value like `both`.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 03:29 UTC

(replying to Yadhira Morales)
> no representation for a message with both a direct and an indirect mention.

I'd want to represent that simply as `mentioned: 'directly'`, the same way as if it had only the direct mention. The direct mention subsumes the effects of the indirect mention.

This is similar to the fact that the presence of a (direct) mention is represented as a flag, not as a count — so if you're @-mentioned twice in a given message, we don't represent the fact that you were mentioned twice, only that you were mentioned at all.

*2024-01-03 to 2024-01-04 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/max.20topic.20length.20limit.20for.20.2Fuser_topics/with/1712322)*

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2024-01-03 11:49 UTC

For the following two endpoints:
* [/users/me/subscriptions/muted_topics](https://zulip.com/api/mute-topic)
* [/user_topics](https://zulip.com/api/update-user-topic)

Currently, we neither document nor truncate the `topic` parameter to have a max length of [max_topic_length](https://zulip.com/api/register-queue#response). Resulting in errors like #27796

#28419 fixes that.

Question:
* Should we document this change in API  changelog, in its own feature level ?

  I think 'NO' because this is more on the side of bugfix where using topic having length > `max_topic_length` was resulting in error. We should just document explicitly that topic length should be at max, `max_topic_length` (This is true currently, we are just adding logic to handle the case when length is greater than that).

* Should we also add a line to explain - what happens if topic length is greater than `max_topic_length`.

  If yes, we should add such a line for:

  - https://zulip.com/api/update-message#parameter-topic

  - https://zulip.com/api/send-message#parameter-topic

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-03 20:20 UTC

Hmm, good question. I think I agree this is mostly just a bug; I don't expect a normal client to ever be interacting with a topic that is too long. I'm actually not sure the right thing to do is to truncate; I would sorta hope that the client is responsible for not sending a too-long topic to the server in these endpoints, and it might be simpler/cleaner from an API design perspective to just return a 400 for too-long topics. 

We have the server truncate in some message-sending code paths because that puts extra burden on very simple clients that might not want to have to think about maximum lengths, but these API endpoints are mainly going to be used by full-featured clients (and usually they'll be interacting with an already existing message to that topic).

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-03 20:20 UTC

So I'd be tempted to just change the error from a 500 to a 400, with no API changelog entry or documentation.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-03 22:20 UTC

I agree it'd be best to reject these requests with a 400, rather than truncate the topic and try to act on the request.

On those endpoints (and probably every endpoint that mentions a topic name, except possibly /api/send-message and I guess scheduling a message), truncating the topic would pretty much completely change the meaning so that the request doesn't have its intended effect at all.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2024-01-04 08:40 UTC

> We have the server truncate in some message-sending code paths because that puts extra burden on very simple clients that might not want to have to think about maximum lengths, but these API endpoints are mainly going to be used by full-featured clients (and usually they'll be interacting with an already existing message to that topic).

## typing notifications for editing messages

*2024-01-16 to 2025-07-24 · 73 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/typing.20notifications.20for.20editing.20messages/with/1720430)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-16 19:26 UTC

In #25719 / #28585 / #**design>typing notifications for editing?**, it's proposed that we add typing notifications for editing messages. 

The proposed web app design is showing an animation in the location where `EDITED` would appear should the message be edited; in the screencast in #28585, I'd say this looks pretty reasonable and is likely to work well.

I'd like to start with discussion of how the API endpoint to request/send a typing notification should work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-16 19:30 UTC

So this would be an extension of https://zulip.com/api/set-typing-status#parameters to add some way to indicate what message is being edited. There are two required parameters today. `op`, which is `start` or `stop` we definitely need. And `type` should probably be something like `edit`, rather than `stream` or `direct`?

And then to specify the message we're editing, one could add a `message_id` or perhaps `edit_message_id` parameter to the endpoint indicating what message is being edited, and pass none of the other optional parameters (`to`, `stream_id`, `topic`)?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-16 19:31 UTC

We don't have any current ambitions to do a "someone is working on moving a topic" feature (I only just thought of it in passing now, but it could be cool to help avoid races where multiple people try to move the same thing!), but if we did that, it could be encoded with a `type` of `move`, and the `stream_id`/`topic` parameters the current topic.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-16 19:32 UTC

So I think I propose:
* A new value `edit` for the `type` parameter.
* A new optional parameter `edit_message_id` for the ID of the message being edited.

Thoughts?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-16 19:35 UTC

And then looking at the [events API](https://zulip.com/api/get-events#typing-start), the parallel thing to do there would be:
* A new value `edit` for the `message_type` field? This feels a little more awkward.
* A new optional `edit_message_id` field for that property type.

And of course for any of these options, we'd need to investigate whether existing clients will crash when receiving an unexpected message type in those events.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 03:39 UTC

I guess we called it `message_type` because `type` is taken by the event type, hm.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 03:43 UTC

That proposal all sounds like as good as we're likely to get for shoehorning this feature into the existing endpoint and event type. (Despite that non sequitur of `message_type: 'edit'`; keeping it consistent between the endpoint and event type seems more important than avoiding that non sequitur.)

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 03:46 UTC

I don't totally love shoehorning it like that, and I'm tempted to say this is a case where it'd be better to make a new endpoint and new event type — better to duplicate some code than to have an abstraction that's a wrong one.

I guess the main interesting part that's getting shared between these related features is the timing logic for when the author's client should send updates, and for when the readers' clients should decide they're not typing anymore.

Still, a client could have a single copy of that code and just invoke it from two places. Possibly that'd be the cleanest solution.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-24 18:14 UTC

(replying to Greg Price)
> I guess we called it `message_type` because `type` is taken by the event type, hm.

Hmm. While it doesn't solve this immediate problem, I suppose we could think about a transition to rename `type` to `event_type` in the events API with backwards compatibility and a client capability; I feel like this is not the only time that's been annoying.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 19:47 UTC

I think in general `type` has been a good name for the type field in events. The thing is an event, so its `type` is the event type.

If we renamed it away, and then in some events used the name `type` for some *other* kind of type that isn't the type of the event, that seems like it'd be confusing.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 19:51 UTC

We could decide we want to make a practice of never saying just `type` for a field name, and instead like `foo_type`. That would simplify things when we have an object that wants to talk about the types of several different entities; it'd be a bit like the often-popular convention in database schemas of always saying `foo_id` rather than just `id`, even for the row's own ID.

But if we had that practice I think it wouldn't have avoided this particular awkwardness, because we'd still have called this field `message_type`. (We'd just have done so on the endpoint as well as on the event.) Fundamentally the awkwardness is coming because we originally conceived this field as being a message type, corresponding to the `type` field on a message object, and we're now retconning it to be something new and broader because we're broadening the meaning of the feature.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-24 20:10 UTC

I guess a major benefit of using a new event type is the backwards-compatibility story becomes simple: A client that doesn't know about the new event type can just happily ignore it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-24 20:19 UTC

So I think doing a new event type is probably a clear improvement; thoughts on a name? We have `update_message` as the main thing for editing a message, `typing` as the thing for typing notifications. And we might want to pick a naming scheme that makes a theoretical "working on moving a message" not crazy to add later, though it's a very speculative idea and I doubt would be hard to fit into any mode.

Maybe something like  `typing_edit_message` is clear enough?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-24 20:20 UTC

I guess for whether a new endpoint is good -- a new endpoint would only need a single parameter, the message ID, right?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-24 20:20 UTC

  });

For new APIs, we should avoid building objects with discriminators that only affect a subset of fields like that. We can deal with those APIs in Zod with `.and` (albeit with some [unintuitive TypeScript hacks](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/3b727d2b5123aaa96f5e04584cb3cf803b92c481/web/src/message_store.ts#L110-L112) in places), but Pydantic has no corresponding concept since Python’s type system is so limited.

It’s much cleaner to use a subobject.

```ts
z.object({
    message_id: z.number(),
    op: z.enum(["start", "stop"]),
    type: z.literal("typing_edit_message"),
    sender: typing_user_schema /* or just an id */,
    recipient: z.discriminatedUnion("type", [
        z.object({
            type: z.literal("stream"),
            stream_id: z.number(),
            /* do we want topic too? */
        }),
        z.object({
            type: z.literal("direct"),
        }),
    ]),
});
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-17 01:46 UTC

In #28478 / #26661 / #**design>archived streams (renaming)**, we will be making archived/deactivated streams visible to clients, both in the web app and the API. Eventually, it'll be possible to reactivate them, but at present, the goal is just to be able to have messages in such streams that you might have access to display in a reasonable fashion, as preparation for that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-17 01:47 UTC

This requires extending the various APIs for fetching streams to support returning archived/deactivated streams. At present, the field in the data model is called `deactivated`, but given that we're calling this "archived" in the UI, probably we should probably align around "archived" as the name for a boolean parameter here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-17 01:48 UTC

It might be the case that clients need some special logic to handle archived streams to avoid backwards-compatibility issues where they appear as normal streams in the UI.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-17 01:53 UTC

These are I think easy to manage the migration for:
* In /api/get-subscriptions, no special action may be required -- you can't be still subscribed to an archived stream. We probably don't need an `archived` property on those objects, unless we want to enforce the invariant that subscription objects always extend the stream object?
* In /api/get-streams, I think we could add an `include_archived` parameter that defaults to `false`; probably basic clients are not interested in archived streams, and that also means no action is required for backwards-compatibility on that endpoints.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-17 01:55 UTC

This one is harder:
* In /api/register-queue, the `stream`, `unsubscribed` and `never_subscribed` properties would presumably start returning archived streams, which legacy clients that don't inspect the `archived` field probably don't want to display as though they were normal streams. The simplest answer is probably to add an `archived_streams` client capability and have `register` and the events system pretend `archived: true` streams don't exist like the existing API does. But if others have ideas for how to avoid adding one, that's worth considering; client capabilities do come with some long-term burden.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 03:34 UTC

I think a client capability is the best idea I have.

One alternative would be to put the archived streams in a separate list. But the fact we have those three separate lists is already a mess that's a recurring source of bugs (as is the similar situation with `realm_users`, `realm_non_active_users`, and `cross_realm_bots`). So I wouldn't want to add any new examples of that pattern; that'd be an ongoing cost of its own, and I think a much bigger one than the client capability.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-24 21:55 UTC

OK let's plan on a client capability for `register`. Is `archived_streams` the right name?

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 04:51 UTC

This definitely sounds good to me.

In zulip-flutter, we actually explicitly model the invariant that subscription objects contain all the fields that stream objects do:
```dart
class Subscription extends ZulipStream {
```
(Stream objects are called `ZulipStream` because `Stream` is a name used in the Dart stdlib.)

If the invariant did break, we could always hack around it there. But the invariant is convenient; and given that we've maintained it with so many fields thus far, it seems cleanest to keep maintaining it and getting the full convenience of it.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 04:57 UTC

If the motivation for being tempted to break the invariant was to make subscription objects smaller by exploiting a property that they always (at least in some parts of the API) have `archived: false`, then there's another way to accomplish that optimization:

We could suppress the `archived` property entirely, on both stream and subscription objects, when its value is false. In other words the type could be `archived?: true`, an optional property whose value when present can only be `true`; when absent, the semantics are effectively that it's false.

That's an optimization we've used in a few places in the API before. For example, the `mentioned` flag in `message_details` objects in [`update_message_flags/remove` events](https://zulip.com/api/get-events#update_message_flags-remove).

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 04:59 UTC

In this case, the "absent means false" optimization is particularly appealing because the client side of it is exactly the same logic that version-compatible clients (i.e. all clients except web) will need to have anyway for handling old/existing servers: existing servers won't send the `archived` property, and its absence should be interpreted as false because existing servers don't send a stream or subscription in the first place if it's archived.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-17 00:26 UTC

I think probably `Stream` objects have small enough cardinatality, and compression over the wire is good enough, that there's no need to consider that kind of compression for them.

Those proposals sound good to me!

**sanchit sharma** · 2024-05-10 14:06 UTC

Here is what PR implements:
* Changes made to the archiving logic of streams; no renaming or prefix addition when a stream is archived.
* Archived streams are now sent back to the client; previously, they were excluded.
* Archived streams are now included in the unsubscribed streams list.
* Archived streams are filtered out and not displayed in settings menu.
* APIs '/streams/{stream_id}' and '/events' now include an `is_archived` property for streams and subscriptions.
* For '/streams', an `exclude_archived` parameter is added.
* For '/register', a client capability parameter `archived_streams` is added.
* Add a new test for deactivating a stream.
* Show an '*(archived)*' label next to archived stream names in the client, similar to the '*(guests)*' label.
* Allow users with permissions to rename an archived stream when creating a new stream with the same name.
* NOTE: There's a problem with the stream archiving process that makes archived streams `invite_only: true`, making them invisible to non-admin users. This will be fixed in a follow up PR.

## unread_msgs API for huddles

*2024-01-19 to 2024-01-25 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/unread_msgs.20API.20for.20huddles/with/1722773)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-19 20:27 UTC

So as part of #25713 in #**general>Renaming  Huddle to DirectMessageGroup**, we're considering renaming "Huddles" in the server internals. That only leaks into the API in one place, the `unread_msgs` data structure has a `huddle` field. 

My temptation is to do nothing as part of this project. I believe we had ambitions to just replace `unread_msgs` with a modernized data structure for other naming reasons, including the `msgs` abbreviation and some other issues with its format... and just drop the `huddle` name as part of that revision.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2024-01-19 22:54 UTC

Doing an API transition in one go sounds good to me :+1:

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-24 03:25 UTC

SGTM.

My feeling has always been that it was a mistake for the name "huddle" to appear there in the first place, and equally a mistake for that data structure to separate `pms` from `huddles` rather than represent all DM conversations in a uniform way. The different representations of 1:1 DMs vs. group DMs is an important optimization in the database and the server, but we've largely been successful in keeping that an internal implementation detail so as to present them uniformly in the API, and this is one of very few places it's leaked.

So it'll be great to someday unify those and otherwise clean this up. But pending that, I don't think it's worth renaming that field.

**Greg Price** · 2024-01-25 05:49 UTC

(replying to Greg Price)
> The different representations of 1:1 DMs vs. group DMs is an important optimization in the database and the server, but we've largely been successful in keeping that an internal implementation detail so as to present them uniformly in the API, […]

(Oh and I see in #25713 that we're actually now talking about making that uniform in the database and server as well, by making 1:1 DMs work much the same way as group DMs already do.)

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-25 18:23 UTC

Yeah, exactly; we now have both performance and "we may want to support metadata on DM conversations" reasons to change the model for DMs, which seems pretty compelling.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2024-01-20 02:30 UTC

Reviving [an old API-documentation discussion](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/412-api-documentation/topic/audit.20for.20change.20entries.20vs.2E.20central.20changelog/near/1404115).

[`authentication_methods`](https://chat.zulip.org/api/get-server-settings) in the `GET /server_settings` response is marked as:

- Do we offer a "Log in with SSO" button? (Yes if it has `remoteuser: true`.)

:question: Should we perhaps:

- make `external_authentication_methods` answer the question about "Log in with SSO"

```
 cat tools/cache-zulip-git-version 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
remote="$(git config zulip.zulipRemote)" || remote=upstream
{
    git describe --always --tags --match='[0-9]*'
    if [ -z "${OVERRIDE_MERGE_BASE+x}" ]; then
        branches="$(git for-each-ref --format='%(objectname)' "refs/remotes/$remote/main" "refs/remotes/$remote/*.x" "refs/remotes/$remote/*-branch")"
        mapfile -t branches <<<"$branches"
        if merge_base="$(git merge-base -- HEAD "${branches[@]}")"; then
            git describe --always --tags --match='[0-9]*' -- "$merge_base"
        fi
    else
        echo "$OVERRIDE_MERGE_BASE"
    fi
} >zulip-git-version
```

## temporary alternative to `zulip://` URLs

*2024-01-30 to 2025-11-25 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/temporary.20alternative.20to.20.60zulip.3A.2F.2F.60.20URLs/with/1728430)*

**Chris Bobbe** · 2024-01-30 00:18 UTC

Opening a thread to have the server use web-auth URLs with a scheme other than `zulip://`, just for the Zulip Flutter client, and only needed between now and when the Flutter app replaces the RN app as the officially published app. Background [here](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/243-mobile-team/topic/flutter.20web.20auth.3A.20multiple-apps.20issue/near/1725213), but to summarize, this is how we intend to avoid sadness where the RN app and the Flutter app are installed simultaneously, and a web-auth in one app ends up dumping you into the other app, which is confusing. (Once we're ready to formally replace the old app with the new one, we can make it so people won't generally have both apps installed at the same time.)

**Chris Bobbe** · 2024-01-30 00:20 UTC

Quoting Tim from there:

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> […] I guess we should think in #**api design** about how to encode what the app wants the Zulip server to do -- might need a new parameter or something, and this might be a thing we want to backport to 8.x.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2024-01-30 00:23 UTC

More concretely, in the [`GET /server_settings` response](https://zulip.com/api/get-server-settings), under `external_authentication_methods`, where currently the elements have:

```json
"login_url":"/accounts/login/social/google"
```

should they instead have

```json
"login_url":"/accounts/login/social/google?flutter=true"
```

or something, if we pass a new param in the server-settings request?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-30 18:42 UTC

Hmm, yeah, having the server return the parameter to use is nice in that the URL constructions remain entirely in the server implementation.

We should probably implement it via having `server_settings` accept a `auth_redirect_url_scheme` boolean parameter whose value, if set, must be `zulip-beta` (so it'd be `zulip-beta://` URLs used), and probably use the same parameter name/format in those `login_url` values that the server generates if that parameter is passed.

(This makes it a bit more generic, so we can support different values in the future without rewriting anything)

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-30 18:49 UTC

@Mateusz Mandera would you be able to look into the server-side implementation for this? 

I think the existing `extra_url_params` mechanism might manage to plumb the parameter through to the social authentication backend internals to the code that actually generates the final redirect URLs?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-01-30 20:08 UTC

Well it can't be the full URL, since we need to add parameters, but sure we could do the full base URL. I still want to have the server validate it's one of the expected values though, since that reduces security risk.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-11-25 20:49 UTC

What did we end up doing here?

**Greg Price** · 2025-11-25 22:39 UTC

I don't recall us ending up doing any version of this.

I believe that meant that on iOS, if you have both the "Zulip beta" app and the "Zulip" app installed, web auth might not work because it might redirect you to the wrong app.

This stopped mattering with the Flutter launch, when there stopped being a reason to have "Zulip beta" installed. Before that, I guess people maybe worked around by deleting the "Zulip" app if they wanted to use the Flutter app (then available only as "Zulip beta") and ran into this.


## status end time to clear user status

*2024-01-31 to 2026-07-08 · 34 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/status.20end.20time.20to.20clear.20user.20status/with/1729425)*

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-01-31 18:51 UTC

In  #28543 /  #28766 / #**feedback>Status expiration time** , in order to add a status expiration time, I am proposing to add an Optional parameter => `status_end_time`  to the endpoint `users/me/status`.  In case the `Never` option is chosen, the `status_end_time` is set to None, whereas if a particular datetime is chosen, the timestamp is `POST`ed to `status_end_time`

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-01-31 18:53 UTC

In case the `status_end_time` is present, then the corresponding `user_profile` along with the `datetime` of expiry is stored in a new model `ScheduledUserStatus`.  So when `timezone_now()` becomes more than the `status_end_time`, then this model is updated, `update_user_status` is called, and an event of type `user_status` is sent to clear out the status.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-01-31 18:56 UTC

what do you think of this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-01 21:18 UTC

So I think we don't need `status_` in the name -- it's already a property of the `status` object.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-01 21:18 UTC

`scheduled_end_time` seems clear to me -- the point being that it's not when it actually ended, but when it is scheduled to end.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-01 21:19 UTC

The other thing to decide is what API mechanism we want -- does the server notify clients when it expires, or are clients expected to just stop displaying it when the time arrives?

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-02-02 03:20 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> The other thing to decide is what API mechanism we want -- does the server notify clients when it expires, or are clients expected to just stop displaying it when the time arrives?
So currently, once the status expires, the server would update backend and send an event of removal to users. 
The user's status expiry time is also fetched initially so as to render the status modal to display the same.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-03 01:52 UTC

Hmm. Is that a good interface design? It places a lower burden on clients, but it also means we're sending them information that they already have, and places more operational burden on the server to remember to process the scheduled job.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-03 01:53 UTC

Whereas this could just be a new `scheduled_end_time` field on `UserStatus` objects that gets synced around, with the server not sending the status for a user when the current status is expired, and clients responsible for not displaying expired statuses.

I guess the main downside of that would be a bit of added complexity for clients to process the new field -- clients might show a stale status until the next time they reload; realistically that should be mostly fine for existing copies of the mobile apps, since those rarely stay active for a long time.

Thoughts?

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-02-03 06:36 UTC

I feel though this approach would remove the load from the server, the status not being dynamically updated (until that component is re rendered) could be a huge downside in message feed view -- you might be reading a really long thread and seeing the status of one of the user in the `message_list`, you might feel he's on a vacation... but it is likely that the user's status has expired while you were reading... just that the status didn't update in the list.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-03 07:01 UTC

The load is likely immaterial either way; it's more about what is more robust I think.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-06 01:30 UTC

@Greg Price thoughts on where it would be best to do the status expiration? I see good arguments for both client-side and server-side expiration logic.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-06 01:35 UTC

I guess we should think about what algorithm the client would need. I think it'd be roughly this:
* In the every-minute-or-so equivalent of the right sidebar presence update-and-rerendering logic, check if any statuses are expired, and if so clear their data structures through whatever code processes a status-update event.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 05:08 UTC

I agree that that algorithm is pretty doable. It's akin to what clients already have to do to handle the semantics of typing notifications.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 05:10 UTC

Another consideration, though, is whether we want this information to be exposed to other users' clients, and therefore in principle to other users even if our first-party clients don't expose it in the UI.

@Alya Abbott suggested in the issue #28543:
> Should the expiration time be visible to others? It might not be something you want to share publicly, so I would lean toward not.

I'd lean in the same direction. And if the product decision is that the expiration time isn't visible because the user might not want to share it publicly, then it definitely seems best if the server doesn't expose it to other users in the API.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-16 16:51 UTC

Yeah OK I think the next step is probably to research how other products with expiring status features handle that decision; I can imagine "On vacation for 7 days" being a useful status to display. I'll bump #**feedback>Status expiration time** with that question.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-02-23 16:46 UTC

I updated the [pr](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/28766)  with expiration time in the server, and addressed the reviews.

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-06-16 11:47 UTC

In current version of the PR - #28766 for this issue, whenever a user updates his status and the status end time, two kinds of events are sent:
- an event containing the status and `scheduled_end_time`, just to the user.
- an event of containing status text and status emoji of the user, to all the other users.
This separation is done to prevent the `scheduled_end_time` of the user being sent to other users 

Currently, the request to the server would contain both the status text and emoji, even if only the `scheduled_end_time` is updated. In latest [review](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/28766#discussion_r1638384403), @Prakhar Pratyush  suggested to just send the `scheduled_end_time` in the request, in case only the `scheduled_end_time` is updated. This could be helpful because we can avoid the second section of events being sent here, and just send event of `scheduled_end_time` to the user.

However, this would mean we need to do an additional db query to check if the user has some status already set and only the `scheduled_end_time` is updated. This will save unnecessary events sent to other users when only end time is updated. Else, we could save the db query, and send the additional unnecessary event of status test and emoji to other users even though only the `scheduled_end_time` is updated from /api/update-status.

Thoughts on this?

**Rohan Gudimetla** · 2024-06-16 11:49 UTC

cc @Prakhar Pratyush

> suggested to just send the `scheduled_end_time` in the request, in case only the `scheduled_end_time` is updated

I didn't suggest this actually... The suggestion is to validate that atleast one field is changing then if only end_time is changing send the event only to the concerned user instead of sending to all.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-06-16 20:12 UTC

I don't think we should be worrying about a single extra database query in this sort of code path.

**Kunal Sharma** · 2025-10-28 11:23 UTC

In #36352, I have used a `SCHEDULED_END_TIME_CLEAR_FLAG=-1` flag, which can be passed in the API request to clear `scheduled_end_time`, thus differentiating it from the cases where this field is not provided.

An alternative way to do this is to use `MissingType` from `pydantic_partials`. But I think we still need to use a flag to distinguish between the two cases in events (or we could make `scheduled_end_time` non-optional in the event object when it is not cleared, so that a missing value would implicitly indicate it has been cleared)?

**Greg Price** · 2025-10-29 02:31 UTC

**Greg Price** · 2025-10-29 02:46 UTC

Yeah, that seems like a fine way to do that.

No, I think it'd be better to keep the pattern of the user-status objects consistent: they contain any given field only when it differs from the default, "zero" value.

For `scheduled_end_time`, the default value will be that it doesn't expire, expressed as `null`. So when that's the value, it shouldn't appear.

## restart events

*2024-02-09 to 2024-02-16 · 30 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/restart.20events/with/1734795)*

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-09 17:23 UTC

I'm working on decoupling sending the `restart` event from Tornado restarts themselves, so we can restart Tornado without forcing clients to reload, enable doing some of the load-skewing server-side rather than client-side, and potentially signal for client reloads when Tornado has not been restarted.

It looks like currently terminal doesn't do anything when it gets a `restart` event, `zulip-mobile` uses the information to update the `zulipVersion` and `zulipFeatureLevel` of the server, and Flutter doesn't handle them at all yet (#F135).  None of them request a new queue, as the web client does.

https://zulip.com/api/get-events#restart says:
> Event sent to all the users whenever the Zulip server restarts. Specifically, this event is sent whenever the Tornado process for the user is restarted; in particular, this will always happen when the Zulip server is upgraded. Clients can use this event to know when they should get a new event queue …

A few notes on that:
- Web [skews over 5 minutes](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/0d25efd4a09c9b4f5771319626d2df451f912867/web/src/reload.js#L238-L244), not the documented 10 (though we have currently relaxed Zulip Cloud to 10 for load reasons).  We should potentially fix the documentation to be 5 minutes.
- It is not clear if clients *must* get a new event queue, or *may* get a new event queue -- "can use [..] to know when they should" is very ambiguous about expectations.
- This will require a documentation change, since it will not longer be "whenever the Zulip server restarts" or "always happen when the Zulip server is upgraded" -- but rather "when we want clients to restart."

But we should also be clear on our intentions for *why* we may want a restart, before mandating what clients should do when they get the event.  For web clients, we send the event primarily to make sure that the client-side JS is refreshed so that it is in sync with the server's APIs -- and this happens to result in also requesting a new queue as a byproduct.  I don't think we rely on the new queue in any way.

Since non-Web clients have no manner to get updated code from the server, encouraging them to get a new event queue is the only reason to do so.  But since that's a "may," we can't rely on it.  So it seems like either we should strengthen that to *must* (though I can't think of any reason to mandate that) or make clear that the only purpose of the event for non-Web clients is that the server *may* send it if the version or feature level has changed.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 19:38 UTC

Thanks for all the research on this!

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 19:42 UTC

I think given that clients are generally designed to support any recent feature level, it is probably correct for clients to be responsible for determining whether they want to restart / or get a newer queue following a change in feature level of the server. I think most of our API version upgrades should not require any action on the part of the client other than updating its understanding of the server's feature level. (There's perhaps a few, where the client's expectations as to what data it has, might be relevant).

I can also imagine cases where the client code is not written to handle certain server feature level transitions, such as certain major version release downgrades, but can easily detect that is the case and restart.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 19:43 UTC

I think it's reasonable to interpret a `restart` event as informing the client that the server has restarted, not asking the client restart.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 19:45 UTC

And then I wonder if we want to consider just creating a new event type intended to communicate with the desktop/web apps about a new web app version being available and recommended to reload into when idle?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 19:46 UTC

And then the `restart` event could preserve having semantics that it'll be sent whenever the server's version changes, while the `web_app_reload` event (or whatever we call it; haven't thought about naming for it) would be one that the server can optionally send when it wants the web app to reload.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-09 19:55 UTC

Yeah, spitting server restart events from webapp-reload events seems like a good call.  We can always insert `restart` events, and choose if/when we sent webapp-reload events.

Would we want to attempt to filter which queues get the webapp-reload events?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 23:33 UTC

Well, it'd be nice to be able to skip any that got a newer version of the web app when they started in the first place.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 23:34 UTC

I think it would be nice to have queues be created with the web app having passed a parameter with the web app version (some main bundle ID) included in the parameters for the queue creation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 23:35 UTC

And then the events system could send the event to all clients that provided that parameter, but where its value isn't the one we're migrating to.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-09 23:36 UTC

But it would probably also be fine to just send it to everyone and the client can ignore if it's "already on that version"?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-10 03:29 UTC

Yeah, I've already built the functionality to only send it to clients that are not new -- by flagging which ones we loaded from disk from the previous version.

My question, which I didn't make clearly, was if we should only send it to ones whose `client.client_type_name == "website"`.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-10 07:40 UTC

#28899 only pushes the events to `website` queues, but that's easily changeable.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-10 07:41 UTC

We could thus theoretically not document the `reload_web_client` event type, since other clients will presumably not ever see them or need to handle them, but it seems prudent to be complete.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-11 15:08 UTC

If we are filtering by client, we need to look for the desktop app as well, and I think it's probably fine to document; folks working on web do use the documentation sometimes to check how the API is expected to work. 

I would prefer to not filter on client type at all and instead just have a parameter sent in queue registration for whether the client wants this class of event; that seems more explicit.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-12 22:00 UTC

Repushed to let clients just use the `event_types` as usual to filter the event out.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-15 00:02 UTC

Reviewing this again now, though there is a CI failure, it seems likely minor: Unexpected logging of:

> 2024-02-14 23:12:56.760 WARN [] reload_web_client during apply_events

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-15 00:03 UTC

I guess we should remember to think about how we're going to deploy this -- the Tornado URL transitions might want some care to avoid breaking the old URLs until we've restarted all the Tornado processes?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-15 00:17 UTC

Oh, should we call the event type `web_reload_client` instead of `reload_web_client`? We've been using the `web_` namespace for settings that are specific to the web app, and this seems like it should fit into that pattern.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-15 00:37 UTC

(I don't think any of the other variables, like internal URLs, have a reason to follow that convention).

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-15 04:16 UTC

Yeah, I added the warn but hadn't updated the test.  Will fix shortly.

My belief is that all of the URL transitions are actually fine during the deploy, because of retries, but I'll do a more concrete analysis tomorrow morning.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-15 14:35 UTC

> We've been using the `web_` namespace for settings that are specific to the web app, and this seems like it should fit into that pattern.

The only place I see this parttern is user settings, and that's *very* inconsistent (e.g. `web_stream_unreads_count_display_policy` but not `user_list_style`, `demote_inactive_streams`, `display_emoji_reaction_users`, `high_contrast_mode`, ...).

IMHO starting with the verb is more readable, but I can be argued into it.  But I don't think that we actually have a pattern here currently.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-15 14:46 UTC

The `/notify_tornado` -> `/api/internal/notify_tornado` move is irrelevant, since that's only used in tests.

The `/email_mirror_message` -> `/api/internal/email_mirror_message` move means that until the `deployments/current` symlink is moved, posts will continue to go to `/email_mirror_message`, and thus in the window between when Django is restarted and the symlink repointed, incoming emails will get a 404, and thus returns a `4.4.2 Connection dropped: Internal server error.`  The only thing between Django restarting and the symlink repointing is the new step of triggering rolling client reloads; so if we do the deploy with `--skip-client-reloads`, then this window will likely be extremely short.

The first time we use this codepath, there is no point to sending client reload events, since none of the clients know about that event yet -- they will all reload on the `restart` event.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2024-02-15 14:47 UTC

So I think the only consideration is to make the first deploy with `--skip-client-reload` to minimize the window we reject email mirror messages, and to know that reloads will not be rolling the first time.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-15 18:36 UTC

`user_list_style` and friends are all the legacy ones created before we discussed adding the `web_` convention; so the intent is to rename those eventually.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-15 18:38 UTC

The ones with `web_` names are `web_home_view`, `web_escape_navigates_to_home_view`, `web_mark_read_on_scroll_policy`, `web_stream_unreads_count_display_policy`, so I guess we've got 4 that we've added since making that naming convention for user settings.

## set a group setting to multiple groups

*2024-02-14 to 2024-04-02 · 17 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/set.20a.20group.20setting.20to.20multiple.20groups/with/1737436)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-02-14 18:11 UTC

We discussed about this #**design>group permissions UI** and #**backend>set a group setting to multiple groups**. 

I wanted to discuss about how do we want to design the API for updating the setting. For group creation, we can simply pass list of IDs. But not sure how to handle updating the setting.

For updating [members](https://zulip.com/api/update-user-group-members) or [subgroups](https://zulip.com/api/update-user-group-subgroups), we use `add` and `delete` parameters which are set to list of user/group ids to add or remove. But would be non-trivial to do so by using single endpoint for all settings.

One way can be to just include all the group IDs in the list in the API request and then we can update the setting accordingly by removing the existing groups not present in list and adding the ones that are present but not included in the existing groups.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-14 21:41 UTC

Yeah, I think the cleanest API for these settings will be to pass a new list of group IDs, and the server makes it so, without use of `add`/`delete` parameters, just like it was previously being passed a single group ID and setting that as the value of the setting.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-14 21:43 UTC

And it'd be an internal implementation detail of the server whether it it in fact changes the `can_do_foo_groups` by writing a new value of a "list of IDs" field of some type (not how it'll work) or the `ManyToManyField` manipulations that the server will actually do to make it so.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 05:21 UTC

I agree that it seems like it'd be a pain for every endpoint (and parameter!) that takes a list of groups for a permission to bifurcate into a pair of "add" and "delete" operations.

The thing I'd be concerned about, though, with just sending the complete new list each time, is the risk of clobbering another user's changes by sending something based on stale data. For example:
1. Admin A removes user X from some access list.
2. Admin B adds user Y to the same access list.
3. But admin B's client computes the new list based on a list from before admin A's change. So effectively they silently add user X back to the list — and neither admin B nor admin A has any reason to suspect that that happened.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 05:32 UTC

That's potentially pretty bad if it happens, because an access list can naturally be something that people care a lot about getting right.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 05:33 UTC

I think it's fundamentally unavoidable that a client can be working from old data when it makes a request.

The basic options for preventing that fact from resulting in this kind of corruption are:
* the client sends some kind of intended diff, instead of an intended new value — e.g. it sends "add" and/or "delete" operations;
* or a compare-and-set approach where the client sends the old version it has alongside the desired new version, and the edit gets rejected if the given old version doesn't equal the current version. (I guess in principle this is just another form of diff.)

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-16 05:42 UTC

Possibly the least annoying way to handle this would be, given each field `can_do_foo_groups` that the server sends when describing some object, to have the corresponding endpoint for updating that object take a cluster of related parameters:
- `can_do_foo_groups_add`: a list of group IDs to add to the access list
- `can_do_foo_groups_remove`: a list of group IDs to remove from the access list
- `can_do_foo_groups`: a new complete list of group IDs to set the access list to — which risks the issue described above, so clients should avoid using it as the back end of a UI, but can be useful for integrations that are e.g. syncing access lists from some external source of truth.

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-02-16 19:08 UTC

Yes, we would need to do something like this to avoid the issue you mentioned above.

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-02-20 17:56 UTC

@Tim Abbott any suggestions on how we should proceed here?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-20 19:06 UTC

Hmm. I agree we should address that race. I don't love the idea of every group-valued setting requiring 3 parameters in the view functions for talking about it -- that's going to lead to some very verbose API documentation, among other things.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-20 19:15 UTC

So one theory is that could have a single `can_do_foo_groups` parameter for each such setting, and its value can have the type of either a list of group IDs, or the preferred format of a dictionary of the form `{"add": [17, 34], "remove": [12, 19]}`. So effectively we'd have a `GroupListChangeRequest` type for what one can pass into one of these fields in the API.

Or we could just always require a dictionary, and have something like `{"set": [18]}` as a way to express just replacing the current set of group IDs with a new value for use by simpler API clients.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-20 19:16 UTC

I think something in that direction feels to me like a nicer way to structure requests, but we haven't really used this pattern before, so I'd be curious for others' thoughts on it.

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-20 20:29 UTC

Yeah, that dictionary approach sounds reasonable.

I think I'd want the "set" case expressed explicitly in the dictionary, to avoid making it feel simpler or more basic than add/remove. It's the appropriate thing to use when you already knew the desired list without reading the old list from Zulip — so effectively because you're syncing from some kind of external source of truth, perhaps LDAP groups for example — but even the simplest API client should be using "add" or "remove" if what it would otherwise have done was read-then-"set".

**Greg Price** · 2024-02-20 20:30 UTC

So the type could be like
```
type GroupListChangeRequest =
  | {add: int[], remove?: int[]}
  | {remove: int[]}
  | {set: int[]};
```

i.e. it can have either just `set`, or one or both of `add` and `remove`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-02-21 00:42 UTC

Yeah that seems reasonable to me. @Sahil Batra thoughts?

**Sahil Batra** · 2024-02-21 02:50 UTC

Yes, this sounds good.

**Greg Price** · 2024-04-02 00:54 UTC

Cross-referencing: a related thread [picked up today](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/378-api-design/topic/groups.20redesign/near/1772449) at #**api design>groups redesign**.

*2024-03-05 to 2024-04-21 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/stream.2Fchannel.20rename.3A.20.40stream.20wildcard.20mention/with/1752174)*

Greg says:

> It'd be good to flag this in… `#api design`, I guess. The server should make sure that it starts accepting the new form, either at the same time as the web UI switches over or before then. No harm in accepting it early — it can keep accepting the old form, and probably should do so for a good while …

**Chris Bobbe** · 2024-03-05 19:17 UTC

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-05 20:40 UTC

I expect the API feature level for "the webapp renamed this" will come with at least making `channel` supported as a message type in the send message API. We can include this mention feature in it as well to keep feature level cutoffs simple.

@Lauryn Menard FYI, I suppose you could start preparing the commits for these parts that shouldn't merge-conflict much with other work, while we're still delaying doing the string sweep until mobile confirms they're ready for us to do that.

**Greg Price** · 2024-03-05 20:47 UTC

That works as long as the commit that makes @-channel supported definitely comes before the commit that causes the web UI to change all the strings.

**Greg Price** · 2024-03-05 20:50 UTC

The thing about the sequencing of these changes is that there's only one change here where it's important that the client uses a threshold that's actually the same as the one where the server changed behavior, neither earlier nor later. Namely that's the change where the web UI starts using the new strings.

The other changes, like accepting `channel` as a message type in /api/send-message or `@channel` as a wildcard mention, are like most of our API changes in that they only add a new option for the client to use, and clients can (at least at first) happily keep doing the old thing. That means that it's only important that the threshold the client uses be no earlier than the one where the server actually changed behavior — it's fine for the threshold to be later than the actual server behavior change.

**Greg Price** · 2024-03-05 20:51 UTC

As a result, the client can cheerfully keep the thresholds simple so long as all the other changes happen absolutely no later than the change to the server's strings. As long as that's the case, the client can just use that change as the threshold for the whole bundle of changes.

**Greg Price** · 2024-03-05 20:53 UTC

If we try to do them all at the exact same time, I'll be a bit nervous about us actually succeeding in doing that and not forgetting something, or forgetting to put it before the strings change. So that's why my preference would be that we go ahead and make the other changes as soon as the code for them is ready, while holding off on the strings change.

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-05 23:01 UTC

Yeah, that commit ordering logic makes sense to me.

**Lauryn Menard** · 2024-04-21 12:21 UTC

Just wanted to update this conversation to note that [#29311](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/29311) was merged to add server side support for the "channel" wildcard string.


## web information density settings

*2024-03-06 to 2024-03-27 · 60 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/web.20information.20density.20settings/with/1753264)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-03-06 22:36 UTC

We have a few information density settings being added in #29148: `web_font_size_px`, `web_line_height_px`, and `web_full_line_space_px`. These should only affect the web app, and we expect these to initially be mostly invisible, hidden except in the development environment, while we make them do something. But they will be visible in the API, and we should presumably name them.

The proposed names use the `web_` prefix to namespace them to the web app, and the `_px` suffix to indicate units, in line with how we name other properties. 

These are currently expected to work like the existing `dense_mode` (probably to-be-deleted when we get around to it, as a previous boolean-format setting for font size), and I expect it'll be trivial to rename them later as other clients won't look at them, but seems still work discussion.

As for the "why this arrangement of 3 settings to define the font configuration", here's some notes from the code comments:
```
    # Information density is established user by user through
    # adjustments to the font size, line height, and full line
    # space (the amount of space between one block element and
    # another).
    WEB_FONT_SIZE_PX_LEGACY = 14
    WEB_LINE_HEIGHT_PX_LEGACY = 20
    # Default to 100% of the line height for full-line space.
    # This setting allows, for example, users to prefer a
    # tighter line-height, but with more generous, skimming-
    # friendly spaces between block elements in messages.
```

But as a general response, I think that a) relative units (`em`, sometimes `rem`) are a superior way to do typesetting in CSS over pixel values, and b) that those same relative units are easier to set and reason about if they’re calculated from a source value expressed in pixels.

I think I also need to better understand the expectations held by consumers of Zulip’s API. I unconditionally agree it would be lunacy to to render the UI with a font-size value equivalent to, say, 22px, and a line-height value equivalent to 11px. **Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-03-07 18:32 UTC

We established before that you know the browser calculates `em` and `rem` relative to `font-size`, not `line-height`, so a) and b) don’t entail anything here. There exist very new `lh` and `rlh` units that are relative to `line-height`, but we [can’t use them yet](https://caniuse.com/mdn-css_types_length_lh) and I don’t think you were proposing to. I also disagree with b)—the entire point of relative units is that you *aren’t* worrying about how many pixels something is, since it’s calculated for you—but that question isn’t relevant here in the absence of `lh` and `rlh`, so we can skip it.

My point is not that we should enforce line-height ≥ 1. My point is that line-height as a unitless ratio is the only meaningful setting for someone to configure, if font-size is also a setting. If we start from font-size = 14px and line-height = 1.214, and one reconfigures font-size = 18px, things will look proportionally equivalent. If we start from the visually identical font-size = 14px and line-height = 17px, and one reconfigures font-size = 18px, things will look broken. But the real moral isn’t that we don’t want this reconfiguration to change the proportions to the point of brokenness; it’s that we don’t want this reconfiguration to change the proportions at all.

Ultimately the relevant API design constraints for this sort of setting intended for the web UI are:
- They appear in the API documentation, and we pay overhead for documenting them and changes to them, so it's worth making sure they follow our naming conventions.
- It's always a bit of effort to change the database or API, so it's worth figuring out what actually makes sense as data structures, and this is the forum where we have those discussions as a general practice. So even though this setting is not directly relevant to folks working on the mobile apps, the people who spend their time thinking about what would be a maintainable API are probably the right folks from an expertise standpoint to review a proposed API even for a web-only feature.
