**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-02-19 03:20 UTC

It’s also important in some contexts to remember that methods have different [safety, idempotency, and cacheability](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods#safe_idempotent_and_cacheable_request_methods) specifications. The idempotency of DELETE means the browser is allowed to silently retry it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-19 06:52 UTC

I suppose we may find it makes sense to add it even if we only expect it to be used in nice end-to-end backend tests verifying that edit/delete changes took effect properly, since that at least does seem like a reasonable use case for such a feature. **Greg Price** · 2025-03-12 22:13 UTC

For the `update` event, the PR currently says that the entire object will get included in the update.

I think it'd be best to follow the pattern we recently demonstrated at https://zulip.com/api/get-events#user_group-update , and discussed for saved snippets here:
#**api design>saved replies@2106747**

For this feature it doesn't make much difference in terms of the size of the event, since the objects have so few fields anyway. But it'd be good to keep our patterns consistent.

**Greg Price** · 2025-03-12 22:22 UTC

For the name of the event type, I'd be inclined to make it singular: `navigation_view`.

That's more logical since each event concerns just a single navigation view, not a list of them.

Our existing practice is mixed:
https://zulip.com/api/get-events#events-by-type
where the older types (e.g. `realm_user`, `stream`) are pretty consistently singular, and the newer ones include both plural and singular (e.g. `saved_snippets`, but `user_group`). So I think consistency between event types weighs slightly in favor of singular.

The one real disadvantage I see of using singular is that it means the feature's name has two different forms: singular and plural. But I think in a codebase it's basically unavoidable to have the singular form — there'll always be code operating on a single item at a time — so the only way to get absolute consistency there is to avoid the plural. (And I think doing that 100% comprehensively isn't super realistic either.) So in general my inclination is to accept that both forms will exist, use the semantically natural one when it's clear which that is, and default to the singular when ambiguous. For these events, it's clear the singular is most natural.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-07 17:54 UTC

Just as notes on what we might do in the future, we might be able to change this code path to have users with an appropriate `deactivation_reason` to disable gravatar too, but I definitely don't want us to work on that right now; it's likely a bit of a plumbing rabbit hole.
```
def _get_unversioned_gravatar_url(email: str, medium: bool, realm_id: int) -> str:                      
    use_gravatar = settings.ENABLE_GRAVATAR                                                             
    if realm_id in settings.GRAVATAR_REALM_OVERRIDE:                                                    
        use_gravatar = settings.GRAVATAR_REALM_OVERRIDE[realm_id]                                       
                                                                                                        
    if use_gravatar:                                                                                    
        gravitar_query_suffix = f"&s={MEDIUM_AVATAR_SIZE}" if medium else ""                            
        hash_key = gravatar_hash(email)                                                                 
        return f"https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/{hash_key}?d=identicon{gravitar_query_suffix}"      
    elif settings.DEFAULT_AVATAR_URI is not None:                                                       
        return settings.DEFAULT_AVATAR_URI                                                              
    else:                                                                                               
        return staticfiles_storage.url("images/default-avatar.png")                                     
```

## transcoded full-size images (#32587)

*2025-01-06 to 2025-01-09 · 19 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/transcoded.20full-size.20images.20.28.2332587.29/with/2029610)*

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 19:00 UTC

For #32587 we're generating more-full-size images for HEIC and TIFF images, in addition to the normal thumbnail sizes.  We need some way to advertize the existance of these to clients -- the list of thumbnail formats is provided at the server level.

We don't want to write the `<a>` to be this larger-res (we don't promise full-res, but it often will be) thumbnail.  So that implies that we want some additional `data-` attribute on the image tag which clients can opt to use for full-size lightbox display if they do not support the original content-type.

As a strawman, I offer `data-transcoded-image` be a URL to a sized-for-lightbox webp image, which only exists if the image is a HEIC/TIFF.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 19:02 UTC

Other questions include:
- Should we specify the content-type of the image, so clients can determine if they need to use the transcoded version?  We expect that it is obvious from the file extension, but I've not verified that we can promise that the file extension for the uploaded file matches its format (e.g. a jpg might be uploaded as `foo.gif`)

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 19:04 UTC

- Do we allow on-demand generation of these high-res versions for historical uploads?  The current API says "no" since it's not in the server-advertized list of thumbnail formats.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-06 20:04 UTC

I don't think it's a priority to allow on-demand generation on historical uploads; I prefer doing a full history backfill if we want to offer that. We'd need to rewrite the existing HTML markup for clients to actually use that anyway, right?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 20:06 UTC

Yeah, unless we want to support clients getting greedy and requesting the transcoded thumb without it having been in the message HTML.  But there's no promises the server makes on what that resolution will be, so I don't know how they'd know what URL to request.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 20:06 UTC

So I agree there's no need to support these transcoded versions for previously uploaded files.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 20:09 UTC

I guess I'll adjust my proposal above that the `data-transcoded-image` is a *thumbnail format*, not a full URL -- e.g. `4032x3024.webp`

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-06 20:49 UTC

Sure, that seems OK.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 20:51 UTC

#32930 for a draft.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 20:51 UTC

This does not add an attribute to ship original content-type to clients.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-06 20:53 UTC

I guess the way to decide if we want to ship that is to try to write the client-side code for how to use that.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 21:44 UTC

Oh, I lied.  I did add that attr, and just forgot. :)

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-06 22:21 UTC

I think the way we'd make use of it is:
```diff
commit 3f655835a54df1b53200c8e218af478273e6f0db
Author: Alex Vandiver <alexmv@zulip.com>
Date:   Mon Jan 6 21:56:41 2025 +0000

    lightbox: Use original HEIC if on it is supported.

diff --git web/src/lightbox.ts web/src/lightbox.ts
index 2024b565d7..afb7f9f154 100644
--- web/src/lightbox.ts
+++ web/src/lightbox.ts
@@ -463,6 +463,18 @@ export function show_from_selected_message(): void {
     }
 }

+function supports_heic(): boolean {
+    if (!util.is_client_safari()) {
+        return false;
+    }
+    const match = /Version\/(\d+)/.exec(navigator.userAgent);
+    if (!match) {
+        return false;
+    }
+    const version = Number.parseInt(match[1], 10);
+    return !Number.isNaN(version) && version >= 17;
+}
+
 // retrieve the metadata from the DOM and store into the asset_map.
 export function parse_media_data(media: HTMLMediaElement | HTMLImageElement): Payload {
     const canonical_url = canonical_url_of_media(media);
@@ -532,7 +544,12 @@ export function parse_media_data(media: HTMLMediaElement | HTMLImageElement): Pa
         if ($media.attr("data-src-fullsize")) {
             source = $media.attr("data-src-fullsize");
         } else if (transcoded_image && preview_src) {
-            source = preview_src.replace(/\/[^/]+$/, "/" + transcoded_image);
+            if ($media.attr("data-original-content-type") === "image/heic" && supports_heic()) {
+                // It's an HEIC and we support it -- don't use the transcoded version
+                source = url;
+            } else {
+                source = preview_src.replace(/\/[^/]+$/, "/" + transcoded_image);
+            }
         } else {
             source = url;
         }
``` 

...with better detection for HEIC support, ideally.

## Error codes when creating channel

*2025-01-07 to 2026-09-01 · 45 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Error.20codes.20when.20creating.20channel/with/2032104)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-07 20:58 UTC

In #32725, we're looking to replace some hacky web app code for error handling of trying to create a channel that fails because a private or archived channel has the same name.

It currently does this hilarious thing: ` if (error_message?.msg?.includes("access"))`.

The PR proposes adding two new error codes:
- `CANNOT_ACCESS_ARCHIVED_STREAM`
- `CANNOT_ACCESS_PRIVATE_STREAM`

I assume both of those should use "CHANNEL", like the `CANNOT_ADMINISTER_CHANNEL` just above. I think also private s/PRIVATE_//` would be helpful, since it doesn't matter why you can't access the channel. So:
- CANNOT_ACCESS_CHANNEL if the channel is not archived.
- CANNOT_ACCESS_ARCHIVED_CHANNEL if the channel is archived.

I think my only concern here is whether we feel comfortable exposing the bit of whether the channel with that name is archived to someone who can't access the channel, but does have permission to create channels, to give a better error message here. 

- Error creating channel: A private channel with this name already exists.
- Error creating channel: An archived channel with this name already exists.

**Greg Price** · 2025-01-08 21:01 UTC

And in fact that resolves one awkwardness about `CANNOT_ACCESS_CHANNEL` — which is that the thing you were actually trying to do was to create a *new* channel, not access an existing one

The `CANNOT_ACCESS_CHANNEL` isn't wrong, because of the way we use a single endpoint for creating a new channel or subscribing to an existing one. The channel turned out to exist, and if it had been one you had access to join, then the request would have succeeded (but just subscribed you to it), so "access channel" is indeed the last permission check that failed and caused the request to fail. **Sairam Bisoyi** · 2026-08-04 13:44 UTC

Quick status + one question that came up in review of #38290.

**Where it stands:** the PR now implements the generic PermissionDeniedError (403, code PERMISSION_DENIED) we settled on above, and returns it from three paths : POST /users/me/subscriptions, POST /channels/create, and PATCH /streams/{id} - whenever the name collides with a channel the requesting user cannot access. When the user *can* see the channel, the clearer 409 "already exists" is returned instead, so the existence/archived-status leak is closed in all three cases.

A design question surfaced in review:

Which access level should gate "reveal vs. hide"?**
The create-channel and rename paths (via check_stream_name_available) gate on *metadata* access: if you can see the channel you get 409 "already exists", otherwise 403. The subscribe endpoint instead gates on *content* access. So a user with metadata-but-not-content access e.g. a realm admin who sees a private channel in the browser but isn't subscribed gets 403 from subscribe but 409 from create-channel for the same name.

The web app doesn't expose this (its client-side check catches metadata-visible collisions before sending the request), so it's a direct-API-consumer inconsistency only. My thinking is to align the subscribe endpoint to the metadata bar (return "already exists" when the user has metadata access to the collision). The one problem is that a genuine subscribe request would then return "already exists" for a channel the user can see but can't join, which is a little unintuitive. Preferences?

Also note: on the subscribe endpoint this replaces a generic 400 BAD_REQUEST (no distinguishing code) with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED.

We want both: (a) don't leak the channel's name/private/archived status, and (b) don't let someone who can't create the channel tell a taken name from a free one. (a) is done; for anyone who can create channels, existence is inherently revealed anyway (200 vs error).

create/rename do both since the name check runs last. But on subscribe a no-create-permission user still gets 403 for a taken inaccessible name vs 400 for a free one, and closing that is awkward since the endpoint both creates and subscribes - a real subscribe attempt to a channel you can see but can't join should stay a permission error, not "already exists".

So how do we want subscribe to handle (b)?

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-09-01 05:25 UTC

I am confused about what we are trying to achieve with these changes especially for the [`POST /users/me/subscriptions`](http://zulip.com/api/subscribe) endpoint which is for both creating and subscribing channels.

Firstly, I think we are on the same page that we cannot completely hide existence of inaccessible channels from users if they have the relevant permissions, like creating channels, etc., and pass all the valid data in the request. The PR updates this for [`POST /channels/create`](https://zulip.com/api/create-channel) by moving the name check at the last so that we return `PermissionDenied` only when user has the permission to create channels and all other request data is correct.

For [`PATCH /streams/{stream_id}`](https://zulip.com/api/update-stream) users can still get to know if stream exists or not if we pass some invalid data, like a non-existence ID for `folder_id`, as we would get `400` if there is no channel already with that name and `403` if  an inaccessible channel exists already with same name.

As @Sairam Bisoyi mentioned, it is difficult to avoid leaking name when user does not have permission to create channels for the [`POST /users/me/subscriptions`](http://zulip.com/api/subscribe) endpoint, because how the current code is structured and we use this endpoint to create new streams as well to subscribe to existing streams. So, for this endpoint, PR only changes the error message to be generic "Permission denied" .

We still return the channel name in `unauthorized` field returned in the response if `authorization_errors_fatal` is passed as `False` in the request.

*2025-01-14 to 2025-01-14 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Modifying.20deactivated.20groups/with/2042168)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-14 19:37 UTC

So in #33041, we are looking at adding support for editing fields of deactivated user groups. Previously, we only allowed editing the name, to permit renaming the thing out of the way if you want to make a new group with that name. And as a reminder, we deactivate rather than deleting user groups so that we can easily preserve complete audit logs of all permissions-relevant actions in an organization, which is very important for responding to security incidents wherein an administrator account is compromised.

This was discussed in #**design>Support user group deactivation**; I should mention I'm not 100% certain that this feature is a good change. But the thinking is that it's simpler UI-wise and maybe convenient to be able to edit all fields, using the normal UI for editing a group, rather than needing to do something special, and we do have a product use case for being able to edit at least the description.

I haven't come up with a reason it particularly matters whether we allow you to edit inactive settings on a deactivated group.

Wanted to flag this question since I could imagine some issues that are either annoying or have security concerns around this sort of functionality. **Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-11 17:48 UTC

So I encountered a buggy interaction with `prev_content_sha256`, which is a mismatch in stripping algorithms between the web app and the server.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-11 17:49 UTC

Namely, the web app strips trailing whitespace on the original Markdown content, while the server does this:
```
def normalize_body(body: str) -> str:                                                                   
    body = body.rstrip().lstrip("\n")                                                                   
    if len(body) == 0:                                                                                  
        raise JsonableError(_("Message must not be empty"))                                             
    if "\x00" in body:                                                                                  
        raise JsonableError(_("Message must not contain null bytes"))                                   
    return truncate_content(body, settings.MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH, "\n[message truncated]")                 
```

i.e. it also strips leading newlines. The server also does truncation, but the web app pre-truncates, so that shouldn't be relevant.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-11 17:50 UTC

The result is that the `raw_content` used by the web app to edit a just-sent message with a blank first line is wrong until you refresh the page -- since it has what it sent the server, and that had that leading newline on it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-11 17:52 UTC

I think it's reasonable to address this bug by just having the web app strip leading whitespace, but we should probably also do one or both of the following:
- Extend the protocol to have the server include `raw_content` in its API response to the client in the event that it normalized that content to something different from what the client sent, so a correct client can overwrite accordingly and be able to do edits.
- Specify in the description of the `message_content` field and/or the `prev_content_sha256` field that we expect leading newlines and all trailing whitespace to be trimmed.

## Push notifications registration transfer flow

*2025-01-19 to 2025-01-30 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Push.20notifications.20registration.20transfer.20flow/with/2049734)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-01-19 12:07 UTC

In #32399 we are adding a flow that a self-hosted server can use to gain control over a push notifications registration for domain X, if the self-hosted server can serve requests at that domain.

This will allow self-hosters to regain their registration after e.g. moving their Zulip server to a different machine and losing the original credentials; and in general after any other kinds of credentials loss. So far this required a somewhat annoying process of having to contact support so that we could delete the original registration and let them make a new one for the domain.

As detailed in the PR, the designed flow is as follows:
(host is a self-hosted server, the bouncer is our push notifications service)

1. The host sends a POST request to the bouncer to
   `/api/v1/remotes/server/register/takeover`.
2. The bouncer responds with a signed token.
3. The host prepares to serve this token at `/zulip-services/verify` and
   sends a POST to `/remotes/server/register/verify_challenge` endpoint of
   the bouncer.
4. Upon receiving the POST request, the bouncer GETS
   `https://{hostname}/zulip-services/verify`, verifies the secret and
   responds to the original POST with the registration credentials.
5. The host can now save these credentials to its `zulip-secrets.conf` file
   and thus regains its push notifications registration.

The main question here is as noted by @Tim Abbott in https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/32399#discussion_r1855942850 - what should be the final path for the `/zulip-services/verify` endpoint?  Do we want to do `/api/v1/services/verify` instead?
My argument against putting it in `/api/v1/...` namespace was that it doesn't use an authentication scheme like other `/api/v1/...` endpoints and thus should be distinct. But it might be nicer to have this in the proper API namespace rather than like a random, one-off endpoint.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-21 14:59 UTC

I think that `/api/v1` does not guarantee anything about authentication method -- see also `/api/v1/jwt/fetch_api_key`

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-01-21 15:02 UTC

Being under `/api/` also changes the headers that nginx returns.  They're not relevant right now, (they're only ACAO and friends) but having everything which is an automated API be under `/api/` will make it easier if we want to enforce other headers later.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-21 21:03 UTC

I think `/api/v1/` is a useful namespace for this, yeah.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-28 18:59 UTC

I went with `/api/v1/services/verify` for integrating this. We can change our mind pretty easily before 10.0, so please speak up if you think that was the wrong choice.

**Greg Price** · 2025-01-29 02:16 UTC

SGTM.

**Greg Price** · 2025-01-29 02:22 UTC

I'd recommend also finding a way to get this into the API docs.

It doesn't really matter to me directly whether this gets documented — it's not an endpoint the mobile app will be talking to. But it's an endpoint that will
* (a) exist on people's servers out there that have deployed Zulip, and then
* (b) the bouncer will want to interact with across a range of different Zulip Server versions,

so that makes it something where it'll be useful to have a clear record of what it was like at past versions, and exactly when any given change happened. That takes it out of the realm where the usual `git grep` class of tools suffice for understanding interactions, and makes it share one of the major reasons why API docs are useful for client apps.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-30 00:16 UTC

Yeah, that does seem worth doing; it's a pretty simple API, so shouldn't be a lot of work. But it's OK if it misses 10.0, so we should focus on release goals over that.

 def get_invitee_emails_set(invitee_emails_raw: str) -> set[Invitee]:
    invitees = set()

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-03-18 21:42 UTC

```python
def get_invitee_emails_set(invitee_emails_raw: str) -> set[Invitee]:
    return {
        Invitee(email=email, full_name=full_name)
        for full_name, email in getaddresses(invitee_emails_raw.splitlines())
        if email
    }
```

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2025-01-30 09:00 UTC

That doesn't account for unmuted mentions (or muted ones):

```js
    // A message is said to have an unmuted mention if message contains a mention and
    // if the message is a direct message or
    // if the message is in a non muted topic in an unmuted stream or
    // if the message is in a followed or an unmuted topic in a muted stream.
    const is_unmuted_mention =
        message.mentioned &&
        (message.type === "private" ||
            (!stream_data.is_muted(message.stream_id) &&
                !user_topics.is_topic_muted(message.stream_id, message.topic)) ||
            (stream_data.is_muted(message.stream_id) &&
                user_topics.is_topic_unmuted_or_followed(message.stream_id, message.topic)));

    if (is_unmuted_mention || message.mentioned_me_directly) {
        unread_mentions_counter.add(message.id);
        add_message_to_unread_mention_topics(message.id);
        if (message.type === "private") {
            direct_message_with_mention_count.add(message.id);
        }
    } else {
        unread_mentions_counter.delete(message.id);
        direct_message_with_mention_count.delete(message.id);
        remove_message_from_unread_mention_topics(message.id);
    }
```

**Greg Price** · 2025-02-11 02:13 UTC

Making the parameter required is simpler because there's fewer cases: the set of users who get subscribed is always just what the client specified. If it's required, there's no additional detail specifying something that happens if it's missing; having it missing is just an error, and gets the request rejected in the same way as for infinitely many other kinds of malformed requests.

There might be situations where an empty subscribers list would cause the request to give an error, but that'd be the same as whatever behavior the existing endpoint has.

```python
def send_messages_for_new_subscribers(
...
    # Inform the user if someone else subscribed them to stuff,
    # or if a new stream was created with the "announce" option.
    notifications = []
    if new_subscriptions:
        for id, subscribed_stream_names in new_subscriptions.items():
            if id == str(user_profile.id):
                # Don't send a notification DM if you subscribed yourself.
                continue
            if bots[id]:
                # Don't send notification DMs to bots.
                continue

            # For each user, we notify them about newly subscribed streams, except for
            # streams that were newly created.
            notify_stream_names = set(subscribed_stream_names) - newly_created_stream_names

            if not notify_stream_names:
                continue

## general handling HTTP status code 401

*2025-02-13 to 2025-02-13 · 12 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/general.20handling.20HTTP.20status.20code.20401/with/2090004)*

**Zixuan James Li** · 2025-02-13 17:43 UTC

We are implementing such a check in #F1183 to handle HTTP 401's in `POST /register` error responses. The current approach is to ensure that the rejected credentials is never used in subsequent requests (i.e., by logging out the account).

**Zixuan James Li** · 2025-02-13 17:44 UTC

For context, this was prompted by [Greg's comment here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/pull/1183#discussion_r1953903929):

> (For most things in the API we just work from the API docs with no further consultation — but this is an area of the API that's not clearly documented. The closest is https://chat.zulip.org/api/rest-error-handling , but for most errors that doesn't specify HTTP status codes, and indeed it specifies a Zulip API error code of INVALID_API_KEY which we learned at [#1183 (comment)](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/pull/1183#discussion_r1945865983) isn't what the server actually produces in the most obvious case of an API key being invalid.)

**Zixuan James Li** · 2025-02-13 17:51 UTC

Looking at the backend code, I do find `INVALID_API_KEY` (`InvalidAPIKeyError`) being raised via `validate_api_key`, but the actual code we got, at least for this particular endpoint, is `UNAUTHORIZED`.

Because both and probably more errors of this nature share the same HTTP status code, I think checking for HTTP status code is sufficient for handling them.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-13 17:53 UTC

I believe checking for HTTP 401 is coprrect, yeah.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2025-02-13 17:54 UTC

I guess the `InvalidAPIKeyError` is caught here and an `UnauthorizedError` gets raised with its message:
```python
def authenticated_rest_api_view(...):
    ...
            # Now we try to do authentication or die
            try:
                user_profile = validate_api_key(
                    request,
                    role,
                    api_key,
                    allow_webhook_access=allow_webhook_access,
                    client_name=full_webhook_client_name(webhook_client_name),
                )

                if webhook_client_name is not None:
                    request_notes = RequestNotes.get_notes(request)
                    request_notes.is_webhook_view = True

            except JsonableError as e:
                raise UnauthorizedError(e.msg)
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-13 17:57 UTC

Hmm, it looks like that code has been that way since at least 2013: 365db42a6e59b07dfd12a570baad75a3499aa0e6

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-13 18:03 UTC

I suspect the right fix involves removing that `except` clause around `validate_api_key`, making sure that `validate_api_key` and `access_user_by_api_key` always raise HTTP 401 errors where appropriate. More tactical would be just to exclude a couple exception types from that.

It looks like there's a handful of that are being converted into a 401 by that logic, including:
- Deactivated user, valid API key. I'm not sure if there are security reasons to avoid leaking whether the API key was valid here.
- Deactivated realm. 
- Incoming webhook bot trying to access an inaccessible API endpoint for such users.
- API key is valid but for wrong organization, which we currently are careful to not present as a different user-facing exception from "invalid API key".

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-13 18:03 UTC

So we might want to think about whether any of those want a different status code (should deactivated realm be a 404, for example?) and write future-proof behavior into the client.

## edit history visibility

*2025-02-14 to 2025-02-26 · 14 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/edit.20history.20visibility/with/2091730)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-14 20:30 UTC

In #32840, we're replacing the `allow_edit_history` boolean setting with an enum setting 3 possible values: All/None/Moves-only. A few questions:
- Do we need to preserve an `allow_edit_history` boolean for clients, which presumably would have the values true/false/true? The server would be enforcing not sending to clients content-edit history, so I think the most correct behavior for a client that is unaware of this API change would be to continue to offer to show edit history. (Potential bugs may include the client preserving edit history ).
- It's an integer enum field stored as 1/2/3 in the database and API in the current implementation. I'm tempted to stick with our existing integer-based approach for similar enums if we're merging it this month. But if this gets delayed for some reason, we could think about switching it to use string identifiers in the API. (I kinda don't want to go down the rabbit hole of figuring out how to do that just before a release).
- The current proposed name is `message_edit_history_visibility`; we could think about adding `_policy` to the end of its name, to match how similarly encoded enums are named. (`realm_name_in_email_notifications_policy`, `web_mark_read_on_scroll_policy`, `automatically_follow_topics_policy`, etc.). I will note that we have replaced all of the realm-level fields whose names ended with `_policy` in favor of group-settings values (there's ~4 read-only still in the API, but those are for backwards-compatibility only), but there's still 5 hanging off `user` that do not have to do with permissions and thus I expect to remain indefinitely. (So we'd have 6 of these rather than 5 to migrate to a string-based approach if we were to merge it with this model). 
- There's also a handful of other IntEnum format fields on `UserProfile` that don't have `policy` in their name. (`email_address_visibility`, `web_channel_default_view`, `user_list_style`, `desktop_icon_count_display`, `color_scheme`, `demote_inactive_streams`). Only a couple are things I'd expect non-web clients to be interested in.

@Saubhagya Patel FYI.

## GET /streams with new permissions

*2025-02-19 to 2025-02-24 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/GET.20.2Fstreams.20with.20new.20permissions/with/2096775)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-19 22:17 UTC

So with the new "content access" and "metadata access" concepts proposed in #**design>Add setting for who can access a private channel #32747**, we need a plan for how to adjust this API endpoint: https://zulip.com/api/get-streams.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-19 22:18 UTC

The way it works, we have a set of parameters for what channels to include, and it gives you the union of those selections.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-19 22:19 UTC

The existing ones are the following:
- **include_public**: Include all public channels.
- **include_web_public**: Include all web-public channels.
- **include_subscribed**: Include all channels that the user is subscribed to.
- **exclude_archived**: Whether to exclude archived streams from the results.
- **include_all_active**: Include all active channels. The user must have administrative privileges to use this parameter.
- **include_default**: Include all default channels for the user's realm.
- **include_owner_subscribed**: If the user is a bot, include all channels that the bot's owner is subscribed to.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-19 22:21 UTC

I think one thing that we could do is rework `include_all_active` to be "all channels that the acting user has metadata access to", removing the "administrators only" restriction. (It might want a name change, probably just `include_all` -- since the separate `exclude_archived` is what controls whether to include archived channels).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-19 22:23 UTC

The thing that we don't have is a natural "all channels the current user has content access to". I think there's two concepts that would allow adding it:
- `include_can_join`: All channels the current user can subscribe to through some mechanism, which implicitly means they have content access. I'm not sure this name is future-proof though; in theory, we could in the future have a valid set of permissions where you can see the messages in but not subscribe to.
- `include_can_access_content` might be OK for all channels where you have content access?

**Greg Price** · 2025-02-19 22:26 UTC

I think it'd make sense to have a parameter whose name matches the new "content access" concept.

**Greg Price** · 2025-02-19 22:26 UTC

(like `include_can_access_content`)

**Greg Price** · 2025-02-19 22:32 UTC

And yeah, it seems like all of these filters come with an implicit "but only include channels the user has metadata access to". So it'd make sense to let anyone make a request with `include_all_active`, and it just also comes with that same condition.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-02-20 01:15 UTC

OK, so I think the changes we want are:
- Add a `include_can_access_content` that includes all where you have content access for any reason (subscribed, it being a public channel, or a permissions setting).
- Adjust behavior of `include_all_active` to be permitted for non-administrators, limited to metadata access.
- Rename `include_all_active` to `include_all`, leaving a deprecated alias so existing clients keep working. Since both default to `False`, I think we can just have the code check if either parameter was `true` for triggering its behavior.

@Shubham Padia FYI.

**Vinayak Palya** · 2025-03-11 07:01 UTC

Related to [#33343](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/33343).

**Current behavior**

The search API's `channel` operator currently only accepts a single channel ID as its operand:
```json
[{
  "operator": "channel",
  "operand": "123"
}]
```

**Proposed Change**

Extend the `channel` operator to accept either:

1. A single channel ID (current behavior)
2. An array of channel IDs (new behavior)
```json
[{
  "operator": "channel",
  "operand": ["123", "456", "789"]
}]
```

**Vinayak Palya** · 2025-03-11 07:02 UTC

**Backend Changes:**
* Update `zerver/lib/narrow.py` to handle arrays for the `channel` operator.
* Modify message filtering logic to match messages from any of the specified channels.

A quick initial question: how would you propose this be represented in a #narrow URL?

**Greg Price** · 2025-03-11 07:11 UTC

That's the other part of the API for any search/narrow filters.

**Vinayak Palya** · 2025-03-11 07:38 UTC

For searching across multiple channels, representing  #narrow URL format as ,
/#narrow/channel/123,456,789
which will be similar to the following existing pattern for dm,
/#narrow/dm/1,2,3.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-11 17:24 UTC

I think it'd be better to do something like `/channels/123,456,789/`. We have a lot of existing code that expects a single channel ID in a `/channel/{channel_id}/` as part of links to a single conversation, and all of that code could break if we start allowing arrays there. It's like 10x less code that looks at `/channels/` URLs.

I guess this is probably a format where we'd not want to have a `-{channel_name}` there, since there's multiple names. (For DMs, it's `1,2,3-group`, but I'm not sure that `-group` is adding anything).

The current implementation in zerver/lib/narrow.py, the channels operator only accepts "public" as an operand:

elif operator in ["stream", "streams", "channel", "channels"]:

It looks like we can support `operand=[channel_id, …]` in a **backward-compatible way** by extending `by_channel()` to handle `str | int | list[int]`, similar to how `by_dm()` already branches today. That would let us enable multi-channel search immediately without breaking existing single-channel narrows or tests.

For example, something along these lines in `by_channel()`:

```python
if isinstance(operand, (str, int)):

    ]

        for cid in operand
    ]
```

The relevant snippets are 
``` python 
def user_directly_controls_user(user_profile: UserProfile, target: UserProfile) -> bool:
    """Returns whether the target user is either the current user or a bot
    owned by the current user"""
    if user_profile == target:
        return True
    if target.is_bot and target.bot_owner_id == user_profile.id:
        return True
    return False
```
``` python
unsubscribing_others = False
    if principals:
        people_to_unsub = bulk_principals_to_user_profiles(principals, user_profile)
        unsubscribing_others = any(
            not user_directly_controls_user(user_profile, target) for target in people_to_unsub
        )
```
So `user_directly_controls_user` returns `True` for owned bots and `unsubscribing_others` evaluates to `False` meaning the backend treats the bot exactly like the user,whatever behaviour the user has to unsubscribe themselves is also applied to their bots.

## We're generating relative links that doesn't start with "/".

*2025-03-20 to 2025-03-21 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/We.27re.20generating.20relative.20links.20that.20doesn.27t.20start.20with.20.22.2F.22.2E/with/2130282)*

**Pieter K** · 2025-03-20 11:26 UTC

PR: #33906
Issue: #33907

in `markdown.__init__.rewrite_local_links_to_relative()`, we're reformatting local links into relative links that don't start with "/".

```python
def rewrite_local_links_to_relative(db_data: DbData | None, link: str) -> str:
    """If the link points to a local destination (e.g. #narrow/...),
    generate a relative link that will open it in the current window.
    """

    if db_data:
        realm_url_prefix = db_data.realm_url + "/"
        if link.startswith((realm_url_prefix + "#", realm_url_prefix + "user_uploads/")):
            return link.removeprefix(realm_url_prefix)

    return link
```
e.g, `#narrow/channel/999-hello` instead of `/#narrow/channel/999-hello`

**Pieter K** · 2025-03-20 11:26 UTC

#33906 has a fix for `rewrite_local_links_to_relative`, but that'll probably open up a can of worms in some areas. A [comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/32272#discussion_r1881025576) from Tim:
>Meanwhile, `markdown: Fix relative link reformatting.` is a high-risk (but probably correct) change, because of how annoying it is to fix historical bugs in those links. Can you extract it to its own pull request, and post in "#api design" about it? I suspect we'll want to do your fix, but with a documented API change, and some hand-testing that mobile and terminal clients don't break.

This thread follows up on the discussion in Tim's comment.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-20 16:13 UTC

I am not sure what behavior is correct here, and want to be careful to not randomly mess with it. Definitely a measure twice, cut once type of change.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-03-20 18:11 UTC

You have called this a “fix”—can you explain why you think this was broken?

I expect it was intentional, since by default a link to `/#foo` causes the browser to reload the whole page from the server while a link to `#foo` does not.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-03-20 18:19 UTC

It’s worked this way for 8 years (#7247, #7250), which isn’t an argument that it’s good, but is an argument that some explanation is needed for changing it.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-03-20 18:23 UTC

My feeling is that `#foo` is better from an API perspective. The fact that the web frontend serves pages on `/` ought to be considered a detail of this particular frontend, not permanently etched into the API, so that other frontends are free to make different choices (although we probably don’t strictly adhere to this principle elsewhere).

**Greg Price** · 2025-03-20 21:31 UTC

Yeah, I don't see an explanation for why the links should be like `/#foo`.

Both `#foo` and `/#foo` are relative links. The first one specifies a new fragment at the same path (and scheme and host/port) as the base URL. The second one specifies a new path and new fragment, at the same host/port (and scheme) as the base URL.

The fragment-only form seems better for links within Zulip, for the reasons Anders described.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-20 21:33 UTC

Yeah, so probably this is not a change we want. If there's any existing code that can't parse the form we're using, that's the code to fix.

**Pieter K** · 2025-03-21 05:07 UTC

Ok, I closed #33907

* to be getting `peer_add`/`peer_remove` events;
* to know whether a user is a bot, when they get such an event.

Currently clients always know the latter for all users, except when they're a guest. (And I guess in that case they still learn it around the time of a `peer_add` — not sure if before or after.)

That will change, though, with #**api design>defer loading user data**.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-28 20:37 UTC

Done: #**api design>defer loading user data@2139310**

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-28 20:43 UTC

Another question for this is what the server does to be able to provide it. I feel like this is one of those things that is probably worth just adding as a field on `stream`, so it's cached and available... it should not be hard to transactionally maintain (though we do need to not forget about deactivating/reactivating users as things that can change it, and to check whether users are bots for doing the math right).

The main risk associated with that will be that we need to lock the `Stream` object when modifying its subscribers -- so this could create lock contention if many API requests are trying to edit subscribers to a given channel at once (whether just users joining at the same time, or something else). And we'd need to be careful about lock ordering to avoid creating deadlock potential for bulk operations that, say, add users to many channels at once.

## Extending include_subscriber for parse subscriber data

*2025-03-28 to 2025-04-01 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Extending.20include_subscriber.20for.20parse.20subscriber.20data/with/2139412)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-28 22:02 UTC

As part of #**api design>trimming subscriber data**, one detail that we'll want to design is how clients request from the server that they want some subscriber data, but are OK with having incomplete subscriber data.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-28 22:12 UTC

One idea is to just change the existing `include_subscribers` boolean parameter to also accept the string `"partial"`, in addition to `true/false`. If passed, the server would be permitted to:
- Send `subscribers` lists for channels that are a subset of the true subscribers to that channel, at its discretion, but always including complete data for all bots in the organization.
- Maybe for now, there'd be no additional guarantees in the API description for what is included.

(Probably the initial version for prototyping could do something silly, like just sent subscriber data for bots, since that seems fairly convenient for testing logic to fetch more data). 

I think for the first version, we would not expose it in the API at all, i.e.:
- `fetch_initial_state_data` and `do_events_register` would accept it as `include_subscribers: bool = True | Literal["partial"],`, and might translate that to `True` for `apply_events`.
- `build_page_params_for_home_page_load` would pass that value for `/` if run via `env PARTIAL_SUBSCRIBERS=1 ./tools/run-dev`, and `True` otherwise, so it's convenient to test code for this without disrupting production behavior. (We'll need to always hand-test components with that variable turned off before merging, though!)
- Make this an undocumented feature, only accessible via `home.py`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-28 22:12 UTC

So with that plan, I think we can procrastinate specifying for the API docs with a feature level bump exactly what guarantees the server is making about what will be included in that data set.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-28 22:27 UTC

I think this would work as the code for doing the filtering for testing. (No impact in production, doesn't actually save any work, but easy to write and verify)
```
diff --git a/zerver/lib/subscription_info.py b/zerver/lib/subscription_info.py
index cf4941659e..f76e240037 100644
--- a/zerver/lib/subscription_info.py
+++ b/zerver/lib/subscription_info.py
@@ -466,6 +466,7 @@ def bulk_get_subscriber_user_ids(
     stream_dicts: Collection[Mapping[str, Any]],
     user_profile: UserProfile,
     subscribed_stream_ids: set[int],
+    partial_subscribers: bool = False,
 ) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
     """sub_dict maps stream_id => whether the user is subscribed to that stream."""
     target_stream_dicts = []
@@ -533,6 +534,19 @@ def bulk_get_subscriber_user_ids(
         stream_id = recip_to_stream_id[recip_id]
         result[stream_id] = list(user_profile_ids)
 
+    if partial_subscribers:
+        bot_users = set(
+            UserProfile.objects.filter(
+                is_bot=True, realm=user_profile.realm, is_active=True
+            ).values_list("id", flat=True)
+        )
+        for stream_id, users in result:
+            output = []
+            for user_id in users:
+                if user_id in bot_users:
+                    output.append(user_id)
+            result[stream_id] = output
+
     return result
 
 
@@ -809,6 +823,7 @@ def gather_subscriptions_helper(
             all_stream_dicts,
             user_profile,
             subscribed_stream_ids,
+            partial_susbcribers = include_subscribers == "partial",
         )
 
         for lst in [subscribed, unsubscribed]:
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-03-28 22:31 UTC

And just to put this here, we'll also care about what we can do as optimized SQL for actually doing the fetch. 
```
        SELECT                                                                       
            zerver_subscription.recipient_id,                                        
            zerver_subscription.user_profile_id                                      
        FROM                                                                         
            zerver_subscription                                                      
        WHERE                                                                        
            zerver_subscription.recipient_id in %(recipient_ids)s AND                
            zerver_subscription.active AND                                           
            zerver_subscription.is_user_active                                       
        ORDER BY                                                                     
            zerver_subscription.recipient_id,                                        
            zerver_subscription.user_profile_id                                      
```

So there may be some fancy work required to make a really fast query, involving denormalization, as we try to define the best possible behavior.

In #27415, we're working on adding support for including HTML5 audio previews for uploaded sound files. I'd like to decide on the HTML representation for these that we'd like to use. The PR currently proposes this:

``` html
<div class="message_inline_audio">
    <a href="http://example.com/audio.mp3">
        <audio controls preload="metadata" src="https://external-content.zulipcdn.net/...">
        </audio>
    </a>
</div>
```

This is very parallel to how we do `video` tags, which I don't have handy in the API docs.

For comparison, here's our existing documented image HTML:
``` html
<div class="message_inline_image">                                                                      
    <a href="/user_uploads/path/to/image.png" title="image.png">                                        
        <img data-original-dimensions="1920x1080"                                                       
          data-original-content-type="image/png"                                                        
          src="/user_uploads/thumbnail/path/to/image.png/840x560.webp">                                 
    </a>                                                                                                
</div>                                                                                                  
```

## Should is_moderator have admins

*2025-04-10 to 2025-04-22 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Should.20is_moderator.20have.20admins/with/2150733)*

**Shubham Padia** · 2025-04-10 12:23 UTC

#**backend>is_moderator returns false for admins.** . `user.is_moderator` on the backend returns false for admins and owners right now. Which also means that in the state data and events, `is_moderator` will be false for admins and owners.

If we suddenly start returning true for is_moderator for admins and owners, how would the other frontends react to it? With web, we can make some changes since they'll both get deployed together. But the important one might be mobile here (and maybe two platforms?). If it makes no behavioural difference, we can go ahead with changing it, otherwise we can come up with some sort of transition plan.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 17:31 UTC

This would make it more consistent with `is_admin`. Though note that `is_guest` has sorta the opposite meaning.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 05:02 UTC

It looks like both mobile apps ignore `is_moderator` entirely, in favor of `role`. So there's no compatibility constraint there to changing its meaning.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 05:05 UTC

And when zulip-mobile did use `is_moderator` (only ever for pre-4.0 servers), it did so in a way where it would have behaved the same way after such a change:
```js
  const { isOwner, isAdmin, isModerator, isGuest } = getRealm(state);

  if (isOwner) {
    return Owner;
  } else if (isAdmin) {
    return Admin;
  } else if (isModerator) {
    return Moderator;
  } else if (isGuest) {
    return Guest;
  } else {
    return Member;
  }
```

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 05:09 UTC

I agree this would be a good change, so that both `is_admin` and `is_moderator` mean "is at least" rather than "is exactly".

It's true that `is_guest` is different. Even there, though, I think of it as "is at most" more than as "is exactly".

And all of these — after this change to `is_moderator` — can therefore be interpreted as "is XYZ, *as opposed to a normal member*". That aligns each of them with the set of people I'd normally mean, or understand someone else to mean, when writing "the admins of this organization" or "the moderators of this organization" etc.

## topics view URL format

*2025-04-10 to 2025-04-21 · 22 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/topics.20view.20URL.20format/with/2151332)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 19:12 UTC

In #30155, we're looking at adding a new type of channel view that lists the topics in that channel, rather than being the channel's combined feed. We should think about what URLs to use for this.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 19:13 UTC

Currently, we have `/#narrow/channel/{channel_id}` as the main URL for linking to a channel. And that takes you to the channel feed in the web app.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 19:14 UTC

We also have a web app setting for what the default behavior is of clicking on a channel, with basically 3 options:
- Channel feed
- Newest topic in channel
- List of topics

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 19:15 UTC

We intend to offer in the channel menu the other useful choices -- e.g., if your default if channel feed, there'll be a "List of topics" option.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 19:16 UTC

For `Back` button reasons, we thus kinda want URLs for explicitly those views -- in that probably the base #**api design** URL syntax would take you to the default view for that channel.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 19:17 UTC

So we may want to define URLs for those views, like `/#topics/channel/{channel_id}`.

The other option is that we could have the extra state not live in the URL itself, but instead just in the `state` attached to `window.history` entries.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-10 19:19 UTC

A dedicated URL syntax would make it possible to send someone a link specifically to the channel feed within a channel, or specifically to the list of topics view for a channel. 

But it would also mean clients now have a new URL variant that they need to parse and do something with.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2025-04-11 02:40 UTC

Another use case is someone wanting to bookmark the topics list view for a channel but use `newest topic in channel` as their default setting.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 04:38 UTC

Hmm interesting. This might be a bit tricky.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 04:38 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> Currently, we have `/#narrow/channel/{channel_id}` as the main URL for linking to a channel. And that takes you to the channel feed in the web app.

I think this ought to continue to refer to the channel feed. Otherwise the meaning of `/#narrow/…` becomes quite irregular.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 04:39 UTC

> For `Back` button reasons, we thus kinda want URLs for explicitly those views -- in that probably the base #**api design** URL syntax would take you to the default view for that channel.

Yeah, and there's a reason to make that the case even independently of considerations about the Back button: if someone just refers generally to some channel in a message they send, and you follow that link, it seems like that ought to show you your default way of viewing that channel.

So that'd suggest having 4 URLs:
* the channel feed, namely `/#narrow/…`
* each of the 2 other options
* the default — which for any given user would be equivalent to one of the above, but a different one depending on the user's settings

That sounds awfully complicated, though.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 19:43 UTC

Yeah. And I am not sure that the specific views necessarily make sense as a thing to even try to translate in other clients.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 19:50 UTC

Well, here's a proposal:
- We use `/#recent/channel/{channel_id}` for the new topics view for a channel. Clients can parse this if they choose, but they don't have to, just as mobile currently doesn't handle links to the main `/#recent` view. (But might if they add a similar enough view). I'm currently leaning towards "recent" because that's what it is defined as -- the recent topics in the channel -- even though it's currently styled more like the inbox view.
- The setting for what links in the left sidebar do probably just needs to control what URLs we put in the left sidebar. So the channel links would be to `/#recent/channel/{channel_id}`, not to `/#narrow/channel/{channel_id}-{channel_name}`.
- We adjust the [API documentation](https://zulip.com/api/message-formatting#links-to-channels-topics-and-messages) to detail that clients can decide what channel view `a.stream` channel link elements take you to -- i.e., the `href` for those is the default behavior of the link that also encodes the channel alongside the `data-stream-id` field, but clients can override that default.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 19:52 UTC

I think this proposal achieves our goals here:
- Clients can decide how both the left sidebar and formal channel links in messages work.
- You can generate other links that don't use that behavior. E.g. Markdown syntax to generate such a link that doesn't get the `.stream` class applied (`[channel name](/#narrow/channel/{channel_id})`) can link to the combined feed. And similarly you can just link to `/#recent/channel/{channel_id}`. (We'd want to add those as test cases just to make sure we're making an explicit decision that those don't get rewritten). 

So this channel would be linked using [this for combined feed](#narrow/channel/378-api-design) and [this for topic list](#recent/channel/378-api-design).

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2025-04-21 03:11 UTC

Thanks for making the proposal clear to me. I don't like using `#recent` here due to 2 reasons:
* We are showing full list of topics in the channel and not just recent.
* It might limit our ability to expand on recent view based URL hash. Like adding filters to recent view from URL hash.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-21 18:24 UTC

OK, we can use `#topics` as the prefix. The view is all the topics in the channels sorted by recency, so recent isn't totally off base, but I also don't see much benefit to overloading in that way, which would be confusing in the code, even if not to users..

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-21 20:59 UTC

Yeah, I agree with those reasons for `#topics` over `#recent`.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-21 21:00 UTC

I don't entirely follow this part:

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> - You can generate other links that don't use that behavior. E.g. Markdown syntax to generate such a link that doesn't get the `.stream` class applied (`[channel name](/#narrow/channel/{channel_id})`) can link to the combined feed. And similarly you can just link to `/#recent/channel/{channel_id}`. …

If I write a link like #**api design** (as `#**api design**`, the thing I get with autocomplete after typing `#`), what URL would that link to in this proposal?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-21 21:44 UTC

You'd get an `<a class="stream" href="{channel feed URL}">` as you get right now. 

The idea is that the client apps could have either a click handler or other processing code that rewrites those URLs only when the `.stream` class is present to have other client-defined behavior. 

So the web app might, say, have those `.stream` class links take you to the your preferred view type for a channel as per your web app settings. But if you made a normal Markdown link to that same URL, it would not be rewritten, and so would still take you to the channel feed.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-21 21:46 UTC

Cool, that sounds like a good plan.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-21 22:01 UTC

Concretely, what that plans means is that this project just needs to add the new `/#topics/` URL format for itself, and we don't need to make any other changes to be able to integrate it -- any such `.stream` class processing can just be a follow-up feature for the web client (or other clients) with no API impact.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-21 22:01 UTC

If we end up doing that, we could add a sentence in https://zulip.com/api/message-formatting about the channel link format suggesting the idea.

Currenlty, this is what I have done:

```py
if (
        invite.referred_by_id != user_profile.id
        and not user_profile.is_realm_admin
        and not user_profile.can_create_multiuse_invite_to_realm()
    ):
        # Guest users case will not be handled here as it will
        # be handled by the decorator above.
        raise JsonableError(_("Insufficient permission"))
```
```py
def can_create_multiuse_invite_to_realm(self) -> bool:
        return self.has_permission("create_multiuse_invite_group")
```

```py
def has_permission(self, policy_name: str, realm: Optional["Realm"] = None) -> bool:
        from zerver.lib.user_groups import user_has_permission_for_group_setting
        from zerver.models import Realm

        if policy_name not in Realm.REALM_PERMISSION_GROUP_SETTINGS:
            raise AssertionError("Invalid policy")

        if realm is None:
            # realm is passed by the caller only when we optimize
            # the number of database queries by fetching the group
            # setting fields using select_related.
            realm = self.realm
        allowed_user_group = getattr(realm, policy_name)
        setting_config = Realm.REALM_PERMISSION_GROUP_SETTINGS[policy_name]
        return user_has_permission_for_group_setting(allowed_user_group, self, setting_config)
```

## Syncing group membership

*2025-04-15 to 2025-04-21 · 28 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Syncing.20group.20membership/with/2154643)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-15 18:42 UTC

In #34398, we're looking at adding support for synchronizing groups from a third-party database using SCIM. I imagine we'll add parallel features for LDAP and other providers soon as well.

One thing on my mind is that if the membership of a group is being synchronized from an external database, you probably don't want it to be possible to edit that group's membership inside Zulip. There's two possible failure modes, both pretty bad:
- Confusion -- if the changes get overwritten on the next sync.
- Drift -- if the third-party system sends deltas, like SCIM does in some settings, and thus you just get out of sync.

At the same time, we do have some things that can't be synced, e.g. which bot users are members of a given group. (Bots won't exist in the third-party database).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-15 18:43 UTC

Probably for this to work well, we'll want something in the database to mark which groups are synced from another database, and those groups should have their name and direct user membership not editable, with some tooltips/error messages that indicate the reason is that they're synced from "provider name".

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-15 18:45 UTC

I think this means we probably want a new field on the UserGroup object, possibly string-format, that contains the name of the user/groups database provider that the group was synced from, in a human-readable form that can be displayed in tooltips and error messages, e.g., "Okta", not "SCIM" or "scim". I think this might be a good Python type definition for it?

- `members_managed_by: "str" | None`

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 04:24 UTC

That general plan sounds reasonable.

Is there meant to be any semantics to the different string values beyond showing in error messages? E.g. if one group says "Okta" there and the other says "LDAP", is it intended for the server or client to be able to do anything with the information that those seem to be different data sources?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 18:35 UTC

I expect the functional semantics to be:

> If not `null`, this group's direct membership cannot be edited by Zulip clients, because it is synced from a third-party group membership database. The value of this field will be a user-facing name for the authentication backend, appropriate for use in tooltips or error messages explaining how the group's membership can be edited.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 18:38 UTC

The alternative option would be to use the `name` fields from the `external_authentication_methods` data structure (https://zulip.com/api/get-server-settings) and get the display name from there. 

A flaw with that plan is that the SCIM protocol just does account synchronization, not authentication, so we'd probably need a separate mapping, and it just feels like it'd end up very complex.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 18:39 UTC

Meanwhile this leaves open the possibility that you could hook up your own custom group sync code to your employee directory and just put "ExampleCorpDirectory" in that field and have everything work.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 18:41 UTC

The main thing we've not discussed that I'm worried about with this design direction is how `members_managed_by` gets cleared; I'm not entirely sure that SCIM, for example, gives an easy way for Zulip to know what the complete set of groups that it manages is and thus remove that field from any groups that are no longer being synced by the third party.

LDAP is also fairly messy around this, mainly due to `django-auth-ldap` limitations.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 18:46 UTC

Yeah, that seems worth thinking more about.

Otherwise those semantics sound good.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-16 18:51 UTC

It's probably not common for a group to transition from being synced from elsewhere, to being no longer synced from elsewhere but still relevant. (As opposed to no longer synced from elsewhere because it was deleted there, and ought to be deleted in Zulip too.)

Perhaps it'd be helpful to also have a timestamp for when the group was last synced from elsewhere? I think that'd help a lot if an admin is looking at the groups and trying to manually clean up in that situation — if most groups were last updated last night, but this one last month, that lets them be a lot more confident in concluding it's not getting synced.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 18:53 UTC

Yeah, and then we could have the "Group details" section in the web UI say "Last synced from Okta 12 hours ago" or something. I think the only problem with that is that while LDAP supports that sort of thing, SCIM I think just likes to send deltas? Not sure, maybe it also includes a daily full sync for each group. 

@Mateusz Mandera may know.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-04-17 19:34 UTC

Yeah, Okta just sends deltas. Even though it is aware that a group's state is out of sync - because it always does a `GET` for a group's current info before making changes. But it proceeds to e.g. send just a `add` operation to add a new user, ignoring the fact that it just saw Bob in the Zulip group when he's not supposed to be there.

## Marking a user as spammer

*2025-04-16 to 2026-05-26 · 65 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Marking.20a.20user.20as.20spammer/with/2155854)*

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2025-04-16 18:13 UTC

[#33561](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/33561) implements the feature of marking a user as a spammer and deleting the user's messages simultaneously. The design follows the discussion in #**design>Add option to mark user as a spammer.** .

In this implementation, we pass `is_spammer: True` and `message_delete_action` (an integer with the following values: `0` – no delete action, `1` – delete messages in public streams only, and `2` – delete all messages) to the `DELETE /users/{user_id}` endpoint.

The complete flow is as follows: the endpoint above is called, which triggers the `deactivate_user_backend` function. This, in turn, calls the `_deactivate_user_profile_backend` function, which finally invokes the `do_deactivate_user` function to perform the action.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2025-04-16 18:13 UTC

Before deleting the messages, I have added a check in `do_deactivate_user` to allow deletion only when `is_spammer: true`, but I have not added this check to any other function.

```py
if is_spammer:
    # The full name of the spam user is changed to "Deleted user."
    if user_profile.full_name != "Deleted user" and not user_profile.is_bot:
        check_change_full_name(user_profile, "Deleted user", acting_user=acting_user)

    # TODO: Change avatar image to that of an inaccessible user.
    if user_profile.avatar_source != UserProfile.AVATAR_FROM_GRAVATAR:
        do_change_avatar_fields(
            user_profile, UserProfile.AVATAR_FROM_GRAVATAR, acting_user=acting_user
        )

    delete_deactivated_user_messages(user_profile, message_delete_action)
```

This concern was raised by @Sahil Batra [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/33561#discussion_r2044202790). I’d like to ask: should we add this check to the other functions as well to raise an error if `is_spammer` is not `true`?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 18:23 UTC

I think the actual question here is whether we want it to be possible via the API to delete a user's messages during account deactivation without them specifically being marked as a spammer. (Whether or not we expose that in the UI).

To me, that seems reasonable -- you can imagine other reasons to want to delete everything a user has sent. Though if we're doing that, one does wonder if we want a "Delete all messages sent by user X" API endpoint that is just separate from user deactivation.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-04-16 18:30 UTC

I think the right API design for this might be:
- We rename `is_spammer` to `display_as_deleted_user` -- since that's what the feature is actually doing. (Even if the use case will often be that they're a spammer).
- We introduce a `POST /users/{user_id}/delete_messages` API endpoint that attempts to delete messages sent by the user according to the policies defined above. We should use an Enum a la `MessageEditHistoryVisibilityPolicyEnum` to have the options have string names. This API endpoint will want to be careful to check that the acting user is an administrator and has permission to delete messages in the organization. I assume we want this endpoint to allow deleting messages that are inaccessible to the administrator, e.g., DMs sent by a spammer to other users.
- Metadata as to whether the user was reported as a spammer could be stored using the `deactivation_reason` feature or something similar; I'm OK procrastinating that until after we have completed #33561 with the above.

I think it might make sense to just do a prep PR adding those two API changes, without the UI, so we can focus on just that part of the project.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-18 06:31 UTC

@Prakhar Pratyush [pointed out](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-architecture/pull/2#discussion_r2046898755):

````quote
I think, this is somewhat not perfect:

```
1. The server makes a batched API call to the push bouncer (authenticated
   with the server’s API key) with arguments `device_id` and `encrypted_content`.
   - (That is, the HTTP request has a list of `(device_id, encrypted_content)` pairs.)
   - (It’s OK, just inefficient, if all batches generated by the server are,
     in practice, 1 notice in an initial version)
```

My understanding is:

* for each missed message (which `handle_push_notification` receives) we'll fetch the `bouncer_device_id`s associated with that user
* Make an API call to bouncer with arguments `apns_encrypted_content`, `fcm_encrypted_content` & list of `bouncer_device_id`s (instead of a list of `(device_id, encrypted_content)` pairs as proposed).

We can't map `device_id` with `encrypted_content` (to create the pairs) without knowing the `token_kind`, which is encrypted for the server.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-18 06:34 UTC

I agree that looks like an oversight in the previous draft of this design.

I think probably a good solution is to let the server have the `token_kind` value — just a single bit, APNs vs FCM, or equivalently iOS vs. Android.

That seems like a pretty innocuous piece of information: whether the client is an Android device or an iOS device. I think few people would expect that they're keeping that a secret from their Zulip server anyway. And then the server can know whether to prepare an FCM-style or an APNs-style payload for the given device.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-04-18 06:42 UTC

Any downside of this approach ?
> * Make an API call to bouncer with arguments `apns_encrypted_content`, `fcm_encrypted_content` & list of `bouncer_device_id`s (instead of a list of `(device_id, encrypted_content)` pairs as proposed).

This will also help us to avoid sending repetitive `encrypted_content` in (`device_id`, `encrypted_content`) pairs, if the user is using multiple android/apple devices. (Though, I agree that this "multiple" won't be a large number in practice).

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-18 07:46 UTC

That approach would mean always sending two copies per user, instead of usually sending one.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-18 07:47 UTC

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-04-18 07:52 UTC

to fetch the list of devices to send to. This is per-user .

Greg's [suggestion](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-architecture/pull/2#discussion_r2056977181) regarding the "bouncer key":
> It occurs to me we should have a plan to be able to rotate these: make a fresh key, then distribute clients that can work with both the old and the new key, then at some point later stop using the old key.

`bouncer_public_key` will be stored on `PushDevice` & later used to make an API call to bouncer for registration.

**Greg Price** · 2025-04-30 07:31 UTC

* Generate a new keypair.

* Make a new client release with the new public key.
* Wait like a year or two, so that almost all clients have updated.
* Have the bouncer stop accepting the old key.

These are shared across the realm, so multiple users might be editing them independently at the same time. If the API expresses those edits by just sending the new complete list of channels in the folder, then that risks getting the results wrong: I add channel A, you add channel B, and it could end up with the list missing either one of those.

That's the same problem we discussed in the context of group-based permission lists, and solved with the concept of the [group-setting update](https://chat.zulip.org/api/group-setting-values#updating-group-setting-values). Here the risks of that causing a very bad outcome may be somewhat lower — but at a minimum it'd feel silly, and glitchy, if we both try adding channels to a folder and it winds up not having them both (and didn't give either of us an error).

**Pieter K** · 2026-09-09 10:02 UTC

Currently the outgoing/embedded bots have hard coded [triggers](https://chat.zulip.org/help/outgoing-webhooks#triggering). In #**general>Feature feasibility check - expanding outgoing webhooks** there was a feature request to add a new way to trigger the outgoing webhooks.

As a first step toward that goal, #35250 makes it possible to configure what events trigger a bot. This involves adding a new parameter to `POST /bots` and `PATCH /bots/{bot_id}` for specifying the bot's triggers and splitting the existing trigger(s) into distinct trigger options.

This topic mainly discusses the API changes for #35250, but the new trigger is mentioned here and there.

**The current consensus for the API change:**
- The new parameter for the bot triggers is called `triggers`. This will be added to the `POST /bots` and `PATCH /bots/{bot_id}` endpoints.
- The `triggers` field is a list-of-strings of trigger types. e.g `["all_direct_mentions", "dms_received"]`

**Things that are still unclear:**
- The names for the [trigger options](https://chat.zulip.org/help/outgoing-webhooks#triggering). Currently we landed on:
  - `"all_direct_mentions"` for the **@-mention** trigger. 
  - `"dms_received"` for the **Send a direct message** trigger.
  - `"all_received"` for any message the bot receives -- this one we plan to add, and it's outside the scope of [#35250](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/35250).

  @Tim Abbott is not sold with the `all_*` token for these names. See #**api design>Adding service bot trigger types. #34524@2267915**.
  I think the `"all_direct_mentions"` name is inaccurate. See #**api design>Adding service bot trigger types. #34524@2518504**
  
- Do we need to make this change opt-in? Currently #35250 will return an error if the `triggers` field is not specified.

And we have [`POST /user_groups/{group_id}/deactivate`](https://chat.zulip.org/api/deactivate-user-group) endpoint to deactivate the group.

Now do we want to support deactivating groups by passing `deactivated: True` to [`PATCH /user_groups/{group_id}`](https://chat.zulip.org/api/update-user-group) endpoint as well? @Tim Abbott mentioned that it might lead to some issues when deactivating group and updating settings in the same request.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-15 22:30 UTC

I don't have a strong opinion on this. Just wanted to note that the main impacts of having deactivation/reactivation on the same endpoint as changing other settings are:
- It's more annoying to pass extra parameters to the deactivation/reactivation operation -- e.g., a "deactivation reason", since we'd need to contaminate the "change settings" endpoint with them.
- It means you can ask to do 2-3 other things that may or may not commute with deactivation/reactivation in the same request, which can likely lead to bugs
- It's easier to find it in API documentation search, since it'll have its own page.

I think overall I kinda feel like it'd be better for both deactivation and reactivation to be their own endpoints.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-19 19:24 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> A few technical considerations: * We probably want it to be a single style for both dark and light themes, so looking good with both types of backgrounds is important. * There's two ways to do this sort of thing. One is for an image to be generated on the server when a user account is created, and s …

I brought up some technical questions here. But I think it's worth talking about how `avatar_source` works and how we'd want to manage that detail.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-09 22:26 UTC

So thinking about how we'd do the engineering for a change here, I expect we'll want to continue using `avatar_source` as a enum for what type of avatar a user has. And I'd like to make the following change to the spec. 
- Currently, we ask the server for the avatar if `avator_source="U"`, and use Gravatar if `avatar_source="G"`, and throw an error otherwise.
- Instead, we should use Gravatar if `avatar_source="G"`, ask the server if `avatar_source="U"` or any unhandled value.

Then, if we want to add a new avatar source, we just need the server to be able to serve those avatars successfully, and mobile clients can handle that, even if a nicer mobile implementation might be able to just draw the avatars for that source locally. (As would very likely be the case for an initials avatar source, for example).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-09 22:27 UTC

Thoughts? I think it'd be a pretty easy no-op API change to update the documentation to make that recommendation, and then a fairly small change to the Flutter client to make sure it doesn't throw an error if it sees a new value for `avatar_source`, which is the main prerequisite for introducing new avatar source values, which we might not be ready to do in production for a few months.
