## Notifying users on unsubscribe

*2026-05-21 to 2026-10-13 · 19 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Notifying.20users.20on.20unsubscribe/with/2465318)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-05-21 16:50 UTC

In PR #38601, we are adding a Notification Bot DM that's sent to a user when they've been unsubscribed from one or more channels by another user. The DM mentions who removed them and which channel(s) they were unsubscribed from, using a single bulk message send to avoid per-user queries. Self-unsubscribes and bots are skipped. This mirrors the existing "you were just subscribed" DM that fires when someone is added to a channel.

On the subscribe side, PR #31206 added an opt-out mechanism for the pre-existing "you were subscribed" DM - a bulk cap, a request param so callers can disable the DMs, and a response field so callers know whether the DMs were actually sent. Design thread: [#api design > options for notifying new channel
subscribers](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/options.20for.20notifying.20new.20channel.20subscribers/).

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-05-21 16:50 UTC

In [this comment](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/options.20for.20notifying.20new.20channel.20subscribers/near/2199784), @Tim Abbott  landed on the naming convention used:

- `MAX_BULK_NEW_SUBSCRIPTION_MESSAGES` - server-side cap (100 by default); past this many recipients in one operation, the DMs are skipped.
- `send_new_subscription_messages` - request parameter on the subscribe endpoint; lets callers explicitly disable the DMs.
- `new_subscription_messages_sent` - response field on the subscribe endpoint; tells callers whether the server actually sent the DMs (false if the cap was hit or the request opted out).

The unsubscribe path doesn't currently expose any of these controls. Since bulk unsubscription via the API runs into the same considerations as bulk subscription, we'd like to mirror the same shape on the
unsubscribe side, with parallel names:

- New server-side cap `MAX_BULK_NEW_UNSUBSCRIPTION_MESSAGES = 100`, also exposed to clients alongside `max_bulk_new_subscription_messages`.
- New request parameter `send_new_unsubscription_messages: bool = True` on the unsubscribe endpoint, letting API callers explicitly disable the DMs.
- New response field `new_unsubscription_messages_sent: bool` on the unsubscribe endpoint, telling callers whether the server actually sent the DMs.
- Documented in `zulip.yaml` with the usual changelog entry.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-05-21 16:51 UTC

Two follow-up issues came up in the original thread after #31206 merged: PR #35798 fixed the cap inadvertently skipping channel announcements along with the DMs, and PR #35970 was a docs clarification for what `new_subscription_messages_sent: False` meant on new-channel creation. Neither applies here, since unsubscribing doesn't involve channel announcements or new-channel creation - just the DM to the affected user.

Two questions:

1. Does mirroring the subscribe-side approach make sense here?
2. The "new" prefix reads slightly awkwardly for unsubscribe ("newly unsubscribed" vs. "newly subscribed"), but I'd probably lean toward keeping it for naming similarity with the subscribe side. Drop "new" for the unsubscribe variants, or keep?

Anything else worth considering?

## Allow deleting items in a message's edit history

*2026-05-30 to 2026-08-18 · 45 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Allow.20deleting.20items.20in.20a.20message.27s.20edit.20history/with/2470554)*

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-05-30 04:01 UTC

I'm working on a PR (#39299) that adds the ability to delete a message's edit history (issue #19632).

Users who have permission to delete a message (e.g. admins, or the message sender within the deletion time window) can delete the prior versions stored in that message's edit history. The current message content is preserved and only the previous versions are removed. An audit record is kept noting who deleted the history.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-05-30 04:07 UTC

We are introducing a new endpoint, `DELETE /messages/{message_id}/history`that  removes the previous content versions from a message's edit history and returns `{"result": "success", "msg": ""}` on success. The permission model mirrors that of deleting the message itself: if you can delete the message, you can delete its history.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-05-30 04:08 UTC

The endpoint returns a `400` error if the message does not exist or the user lacks access, and also a `400` ("This message has no content edits to delete.") if the message was never content-edited, i.e. it has only move history or no history at all.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-05-30 04:10 UTC

**Changes to `GET /messages/{message_id}/history`.** 

After deletion, the history response still returns one entry per former content edit, but those entries now have `prev_content` and `prev_rendered_content` stripped. A new optional field `history_deleted_by` (integer user ID) is added to those entries so clients can render an audit notice like "Content deleted from this message's history by {User}" rather than a blank slot. Move-only entries are left entirely untouched , i.e., if the message was also moved to a different topic or channel, those entries remain in full, since `prev_topic` and `prev_stream` are not considered sensitive in the same way.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-05-30 04:11 UTC

A `update_message` event is sent so connected clients can refresh the message's "(edited)" indicator without a page reload. The event carries a new boolean field `edit_history_deleted: true`, which tells the frontend to keep the existing `last_edit_timestamp` on the message rather than overwriting it with `edit_timestamp`, since deleting history is not itself a content edit.

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-06-01 13:10 UTC

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-06-02 17:13 UTC

For the event, I'd like the meaning to align better with the action being taken. Here are my concerns with adding a boolean "history_deleted_by" field to the update-message event as a way to signal this action being taken ("delete all content revisions from the message's edit history"):

- It doesn't communicate that the scope is "all content revisions". I think we'd run into trouble in a future where we want to support deleting one specific revision, or to delete all revisions including channel/topic changes.
- It depends too much on that "audit record" feature and the specific details of that feature:
  - If we want to make that record optional, i.e. sometimes not record who deleted the revision, we'd have to design a whole new way of signaling to clients that edit history was deleted.
  - If we want to record *more* details on that record, such as a timestamp, I don't think tacking new fields onto the "update-message" event is a great way to do that, especially with the concern about communicating which history revision(s) are affected.
  - Reading edit-history data is subject to `message_edit_history_visibility_policy`, so I assume we should only send the event to some clients. Rather than add a new condition on sending the existing update-message event, it might feel cleaner if we added a new event type.

So let's think about adding a new event type, like `type: "message_edit_history" / op: "delete"`. It would carry
- the message ID
- the scope of the deletion ("all content revisions")
  - Let's think about using an enum for this, like `"scope": "all_content_revisions"`, rather than carrying the whole new `edit_history` list. IIRC there was a prior discussion highlighting the case of messages with extremely long edit histories, and this seems like a fine way to avoid problems in that case.
- metadata like the user who took the action, and a timestamp.

It would only be sent to users who can access the message *and* read messages' edit history.

> * How did you decide we should remove `prev_content`/`prev_rendered_content` from a revision object, instead of `content`/`rendered_content`? Is that correct? When should we delete both?

By removing `prev_content`, we hide the prior revision's text while the entry itself (timestamp, user, edit happened) is preserved. 

Removing `content` would require rewriting the reconstruction logic and would still leak data through adjacent entries.

As for "when should we delete both", I think only `prev_content`/`prev_rendered_content` exist in raw storage, so there is no `content` to delete.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-30 08:32 UTC

> * What's the plan for altering `content_html_diff` on a revision object?

When `prev_content` is removed from an entry, `fill_edit_history_entries` already skips the `if "prev_content" in edit_history_event:` block, so `content_html_diff` is never computed and won't appear in the API response. 
**So, we don't need any extra handling.**  

But this should be explicitly documented in the OpenAPI spec -- the description for `content_html_diff` should note it is absent when the revision has been redacted.

We remove them completely . `prev_content`, `prev_rendered_content`, and `prev_rendered_content_version` are popped from the entry, not set to None. The entry gets `revision_deleted_by` and `revision_deleted_at` added in their place.

## Behaviour of services array of embedded bots

*2026-06-12 to 2026-06-26 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Behaviour.20of.20services.20array.20of.20embedded.20bots/with/2477676)*

**Sathwik Kumar Shetty** · 2026-06-12 17:21 UTC

While working on #38228, I found some discrepancy about the documentation of `services` array of embedded bots and the implemented. The description for `services` field for the [`BasicBotBase` component](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blame/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/openapi/zulip.yaml#L27540) in `zulip.yaml` has the below description.

> An array containing extra configuration fields only relevant for
> outgoing webhook bots and embedded bots. This is always a single-element
> array.

This component is referenced  and used in the response documentation of endpoints `GET /events`, for [bot creation](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blame/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/openapi/zulip.yaml#L4722) and [bot update](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blame/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/openapi/zulip.yaml#L4772) along with [`POST /register`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blame/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/openapi/zulip.yaml#L18804).

The events get their `services` array from [get_service_dicts_for_bot](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/actions/users.py#L845) and the register endpoint gets `services` array from [get_service_dicts_for_bots](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/actions/users.py#L872). For embedded bots, both construct an empty service array when the bot has no  `BotConfigData`entries(e.g.,`helloworld` bot, which need no config); even though every embedded bot has a `Service` row entry with its services name . Which contradicts the statement in the docs stating that "This is always a single-element array.". 
The created-bot event for embedded bots is tested [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/tests/test_events.py#L3486) via [`check_realm_bot_add`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/933da929ae198c6976301612021ca5529b16a2c5/zerver/lib/event_schema.py#L394)  and checks for the presence and shape of `services`, but it  doesn't exercise the edge case of embedded bot without config data. It passes `config_data={"foo": "bar"}` to `helloworld`, which doesn't need any config. Removing that line makes the test fail on `check_realm_bot_add`'s `assert len(services) == 1` (the schema encoder encodes the same "exactly one element claim").
```python
with self.verify_action(num_events=4) as events:
            self.create_bot(
```

## hide_link_previews message flag

*2026-06-13 to 2026-09-09 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/hide_link_previews.20message.20flag/with/2478038)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-13 14:01 UTC

Requesting sign-off on a new message flag for [#21766](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/21766). When a message contains a link, Zulip auto-generates a preview card below it; this feature lets a recipient hide that preview on a specific message, just for their own view, without affecting how anyone else sees the message. Implementation is in [#38241](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/38241). PR under review by @Shubham Padia .

It's implemented as a per-recipient `UserMessage` flag, `hide_link_previews`, set through the existing flags endpoints (`POST /messages/flags` and `POST /messages/flags/narrow`) - much like `collapsed`, a per-user toggle for how a single message is shown. Reusing the flags system keeps this small: no new endpoint or event, just the flag. When it's set, clients hide the preview for that user. It applies to OpenGraph website previews (the `.message_embed` block) only. It can be set on any message; clients only show the option when the message actually has a preview.

The main goal here is to confirm the overall shape is right - and to get thoughts on whether `hide_link_previews` is the best name.

## Per-channel default for push notifications

*2026-06-16 to 2026-06-29 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Per-channel.20default.20for.20push.20notifications/with/2479672)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-16 07:08 UTC

I'm adding a per-channel default for the `push_notifications` subscription setting (#23873): an org admin can mark a channel so that *new* subscribers get `push_notifications=True` instead of inheriting their account-level default. Existing subscribers and re-subscribing users are untouched.

PR #38596 (under review by @Sahil Batra) implements it as a `push_notifications_enabled` boolean on the channel, settable via `POST /channels/create`, `POST /users/me/subscriptions`, and `PATCH /streams/{stream_id}`, and exposed on channel objects in register / events / get-streams. It's modeled as a plain boolean: checked forces the default on for new subscribers; unchecked leaves each person's account-level default untouched. Setting it is gated on org-admin.

Two things I'd like to confirm on the API shape:

1. `push_notifications_enabled` is wording-identical to the realm-level `realm_push_notifications_enabled` (which means "this server has mobile push configured"), and it doesn't convey that it's a *default for new subscribers* rather than a channel-wide on/off. I'd lean toward renaming it to `push_notifications_default` - it pairs with the per-subscription `push_notifications` field and reads as a default rather than an on/off switch. Is that an improvement, or is the current `push_notifications_enabled` fine as-is?

2. The issue notes this may extend to the other four per-subscription notification settings (desktop / audible / email / wildcard mentions), so a channel could eventually carry defaults for all five. Those per-subscription settings (`push_notifications`, `desktop_notifications`, `audible_notifications`, `email_notifications`, `wildcard_mentions_notify`) are already five separate flat fields on the subscription object, so I'm leaning toward matching that here - `push_notifications_default`, `desktop_notifications_default`, etc. - rather than grouping them under one object. Any objection, or a preference for grouping?

Otherwise the shape seems right to me - happy to hear any other concerns, or a sign-off if it looks good.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-19 11:17 UTC

Tagging @Chris Bobbe for feedback.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-06-23 21:49 UTC

I agree let's align the name with the per-channel field, and mark the "default" semantics. How about `default_push_notifications`? Looks like we've more commonly put "default" at the beginning than the end; e.g. `default_language`, `default_group_name`, and `realm_default_twenty_four_hour_time` are some hits in a search of https://zulip.com/api/register-queue .

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-06-23 21:50 UTC

Yeah I think separate flat fields `default_push_notifications`, `default_desktop_notifications`, etc., is the right plan, vs. grouping.

It is verbose but might make it clear that it is for new subscribers as the behavior is that we use the setting only when user is a new subscriber of the channel, i.e. no `Subscription` exists already for the user-channel pair.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-06-25 19:34 UTC

> i.e. no `Subscription` exists already for the user-channel pair.

`Subscription` here is a database record, right? Do those not get cleared when the user unsubscribes? I'm trying to understand the client-facing reason to say `*_for_new_subscribers`. Is it because of this part in #38596:

? If so, I think that's a reasonable behavior, but not one I'd want to pin the names to. If we omit `_for_new_subscribers` then we'll have the flexibility to change the behavior later if desired, such that returning subscribers get the default applied, not just new subscribers.

## Zulip server native MCP implementation

*2026-06-18 to 2026-08-20 · 40 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Zulip.20server.20native.20MCP.20implementation/with/2481447)*

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-06-18 04:49 UTC

We are planning to support server native MCP implementation. There already are tools like - [`zulipmcp`](https://github.com/windborne/zulipmcp) that use `python-zulip-api` + `fastmcp` for a mcp which is great for conversational UX.

After some brainstorming with Claude, here is the recommended implementation approach for a V1:

* User has a separate API key for mcp authentication so that it can be separately revoked and is easier to track for usage.
* Add a `POST /api/v1/mcp` endpoint which clients can call for list various available methods and authenticate.
* We return a single JSON response for each request.

We will have a small list of available methods for now like search messages, get messages, list channels, list topics, send message and list users.

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-06-23 22:13 UTC

Is there not a protocol we'd need to implement between our new MCP server and MCP clients in the wild, completely separately from the Zulip Server/client protocol (our REST API)? I'm not feeling super equipped to evaluate this proposal.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-06-24 06:47 UTC

We will be using [JSON-RPC 2.0 Specification](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification), which is the standard, so we need to implement our methods and responses using that.

We don't specifically have to use `/api/v1` endpoint, we can use `/mcp` as well to signal this is not a REST endpoint.

I can try openeing a PR so that we can see it live to understand how everything comes together but basically it will be using the same methods as REST API to return data using this new endpoint.

E.g. (and these are just initial thoughts):
- We won't change or repurpose tool names, because a user's permission choices are keyed by these (e.g. in Claude Code, tool auto-approvals, allow/deny-lists)
- We won't change what a tool and its params *mean* (e.g. `limit` switches from "newest N" to "N around anchor"). That could break people's saved prompts/skills/etc. in subtle and unexpected ways, like someone's workflow suddenly needing twice as many tokens because the agent was prompted to expect something different than what it got, and it has to work around.
- Changes to tools need an #**api design** discussion, like any other API changes. Might be worth mentioning MCP under "Some types of API changes that one might not realize are API changes" in the [API-design doc](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/processes/api-design.html).

## Make wildcard mention permissions configurable per-channel

*2026-06-19 to 2026-07-03 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Make.20wildcard.20mention.20permissions.20configurable.20per-channel/with/2482037)*

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:08 UTC

I am starting to work on  **[38384](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/38384): Make wildcard mention permissions configurable per-channel**. 

The org-level `can_mention_many_users_group` on `Realm` controls who can use `@all`/`@everyone`/`@channel` when a channel has more than 15 subscribers. The request is to add a per-channel override of this setting.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:09 UTC

I am starting this thread for the API discussion on this issue.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:10 UTC

I'd like to propose adding a `can_mention_many_users_group` field to the `Stream` model, analogous to the existing realm-level setting of the same name.

Unlike our current stream-level group permission settings, this field would be nullable. A value of `null` would be the default and would indicate that the channel inherits the organization's `can_mention_many_users_group` setting. If a non-null group is configured, it would completely override the realm-level setting for that channel, matching the behavior of other stream-level permission overrides.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:11 UTC

**Reading the setting**

The field would be included anywhere stream or subscription objects are returned:
* `GET /api/v1/streams`
* `GET /api/v1/users/me/subscriptions`
* The `streams` and `subscriptions` arrays returned by `POST /api/v1/register`
* Stream update events returned by `GET /api/v1/events`

The value would be either a `GroupSettingValue` (group ID or anonymous group object) or `null`.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:12 UTC

**Writing the setting**

The following endpoints would accept an optional `can_mention_many_users_group` parameter:
* `POST /api/v1/users/me/subscriptions`
* `PATCH /api/v1/streams/{stream_id}`

For stream creation, the parameter would default to `null` (inherit from realm).

For stream updates, explicitly passing `null` would remove any channel-level override and restore inheritance from the realm setting. This would introduce a new pattern for permission settings, since existing group-setting fields cannot currently be reset to `null` via the PATCH API.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:15 UTC

The enforcement logic would be in `stream_wildcard_mention_allowed()` in `zerver/lib/message.py`.

```py
def stream_wildcard_mention_allowed(sender: UserProfile, stream: Stream, realm: Realm) -> bool:
    if num_subscribers_for_stream_id(stream.id) <= Realm.WILDCARD_MENTION_THRESHOLD:
        return True
    if stream.can_mention_many_users_group_id is not None:
        # Channel-level override; use it instead of the realm setting.
        return user_has_permission_for_group_setting(
            stream.can_mention_many_users_group_id,
            sender,
            Stream.stream_permission_group_settings["can_mention_many_users_group"],
            direct_member_only=False,
        )
    # No channel-level override — fall back to the realm setting.
    return can_mention_many_users(sender)
```

Currently, this function always evaluates permissions using the realm's `can_mention_many_users_group` setting. So,
1. If `stream.can_mention_many_users_group_id` is non-null, evaluate permissions against that channel-level group.
2. Otherwise, fall back to the realm-level setting.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:15 UTC

No changes would be needed for `topic_wildcard_mention_allowed()`, since topic wildcards only notify thread participants and don't naturally fit into a channel-level restriction model.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:16 UTC

The `server_supported_permission_settings` object in `POST /api/v1/register` must include the new field in `stream`, so clients know it exists and whether it requires a system group. The schema for this response needs an `is_optional` flag so clients know `null` is a valid value for this specific setting.

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2026-06-19 07:20 UTC

Some open questions I have: 

1. Should channel-level settings affect `@topic` wildcards?
2. Should channel admins receive an implicit bypass?
3. Is `is_optional` the right metadata name?

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-06-19 11:28 UTC

> Unlike our current stream-level group permission settings, this field would be nullable. A value of `null` would be the default and would indicate that the channel inherits the organization's `can_mention_many_users_group` setting. If a non-null group is configured, it would completely override the realm-level setting for that channel, matching the behavior of other stream-level permission overrides.

I am not sure if we should allow `null` value for this setting.

And for other permissions, which both have a organization level and channel level permission, the current behavior is for the users in realm-level setting group should have permissions for all channels and then user only in channel-level setting group can have permission for that specific channel. So, for that particular channel, users in both the realm-level setting group and the channel-level setting group have permission. Why we want to change this behavior for setting and instead override the realm-level setting permission?

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-06-23 21:24 UTC

(replying to Aman (whilstsomebody))
> 1. Should channel-level settings affect `@topic` wildcards? 2. Should channel admins receive an implicit bypass?

So, in practice, the permission check would work like this:

* If the sender belongs to the realm's `can_mention_many_users_group`, they can use wildcard mentions in any channel.
* Otherwise, check whether they belong to the channel's `can_mention_many_users_group`.

*2026-06-25 to 2026-08-09 · 4 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Filter.20messages.20by.20a.20specific.20reaction.2E/with/2484873)*

**Santhosh Kumar** · 2026-06-25 07:32 UTC

We are implementing a new narrow operator:

`reaction:<emoji_name>`

which returns messages that have at least one reaction matching the specified emoji. The operand is an emoji name (eg: `reaction:octopus`). The server resolves the name to the corresponding `(emoji_code, reaction_type)` and filters messages using an `EXISTS` subquery on `zerver_reaction`. Invalid emoji names are rejected with an error.

To support efficient execution of this query, we add a composite index on `(emoji_code, message_id)` in `zerver_reaction`.

Current PR: #37605.

## Bulk message deletion + undo

*2026-06-29 to 2026-08-09 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Bulk.20message.20deletion.20.2B.20undo/with/2486898)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-29 16:13 UTC

Putting up a PR for #16427 (selecting multiple messages to delete) - #39596. Would appreciate a sign-off on the API surface and approach.

The feature: choosing **Delete messages** (renamed from **Delete message**) in a message's action menu enters a selection mode - a banner takes over the top bar, a checkbox appears on every message you have permission to delete, and the one you opened the menu on starts selected. You tick the ones you want and confirm, and they're deleted in a single action, with a drafts-style **Undo** toast that restores them within a short window.

Here's the API surface it adds, and why each piece is there:

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-29 16:13 UTC

**1. New endpoint - `DELETE /messages`**
Bulk-deletes a list of message IDs in a single request. Today you can only delete messages one at a time (one request each), which is slow and is what the selection UI needs to batch. It's all-or-nothing: every message must exist and pass the exact same access and delete-permission checks as single-message deletion, or the whole request is rejected and nothing is deleted - so a user can never end up with a half-deleted selection. Capped at 1000 IDs per request, and the rows are locked the same way the single-delete path locks them.

**2. New schema field (migration) - `acting_user` on `ArchiveTransaction`**
When messages are deleted they're moved to an archive, grouped under an `ArchiveTransaction`. We add `acting_user` to record who did a manual deletion. That's what later lets us authorize that same user - and only them - to undo it.

**3. New endpoint - `POST /messages/restore`**
This is the Undo. It re-inserts the just-deleted messages straight back from the archive, with their original IDs, reactions, flags, and attachments intact. It's scoped to the user who deleted them and only works within a short, server-enforced window (~30s).

**4. New event - `restored_message`, delivered through Tornado**
When messages are restored, the server has to tell everyone who had them to put them back on screen - otherwise undo wouldn't visibly do anything until a reload. Real-time events go out through Tornado, so this adds a new delivery path there: a `restored_message` handler that personalizes the payload per client exactly like the message-send path, but emits `restored_message` and sends no notifications - recipients already saw and were notified about these messages before the delete. I kept it as a separate path rather than threading a flag through the existing message-send handler, to avoid entangling the hot send path.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-29 16:13 UTC

On the undo: deferring the delete for 30s isn't an option - it would leave the messages visible to everyone else during the window. So we delete immediately and restore from the archive when Undo is clicked, scoped to the deleter and a fixed ~30s window (following the issue's undo flow). Under the hood this reuses the archive-restore code (`restore_*_from_archive`) that so far has only been run by server admins for disaster recovery - now invoked by the undo to bring back the messages the user just deleted.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-07-02 21:23 UTC

Bumping this for a review of the API design above (the two endpoints and the restored_message event) - I'd like to confirm the shape before building further on it. Does it look right, or any suggestions?

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-07-07 17:40 UTC

> Capped at 1000 IDs per request, and the rows are locked the same way the single-delete path locks them.

Why we need to put limit on number of IDs? We have delete topic endpoint which deletes much more messages in a single request.

> It's scoped to the user who deleted them and only works within a short, server-enforced window (~30s).

I am not sure of this. Was this decided when discussing the expected behavior for this feature?

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-08-09 22:18 UTC

I think starting with a migration to add `acting_user` to `ArchiveTransaction` as a prep PR makes sense to me.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-08-09 22:19 UTC

But I don't see how the above design can possibly work; we'd need the IDs for those `ArchiveTransaction` entries to be available to the client. Would it just be the API response from the deletion endpoint?

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-08-09 22:20 UTC

I do think limiting to 1K messages per request is a good idea. The topic deletion server-side code I think has some logic to offload to a queue for large topics, but in any case that feels naturally atomic.

If a client has a reason to delete more than 1K messages by ID, it seems better for the client the paginate, like we do for other endpoints like fetching messages in bulk.


## GitHub link-preview API: GitHub-specific vs generic

*2026-06-30 to 2026-07-05 · 32 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/GitHub.20link-preview.20API.3A.20GitHub-specific.20vs.20generic/with/2487546)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-30 16:05 UTC

I'm adding hover previews for GitHub issue and pull-request links (#19710, PR #39630): hovering such a link in a message shows a small tooltip with the issue/PR's title, author, and open/closed/merged state. It currently supports public repositories only.

Before finalizing the API I'd like to settle one design question: should the preview endpoint be GitHub-specific, or generalized now so other platforms (GitLab, etc.) can be added later without changing the API?

Today it's GitHub-only and looks like:
`GET /json/url_preview?platform=github&owner=…&repo=…&number=…`

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-06-30 16:05 UTC

A few decisions under that:

**1. Parameter names.** They currently use GitHub's vocabulary - `owner`, `repo`, `number`. A platform-neutral set would be `namespace`, `repository`, `id` (e.g. GitLab calls the owner a "namespace"). Keep GitHub's terms, or switch to generic ones?

**2. Endpoint and function names.** `/json/url_preview` and the backend helper `get_link_preview_data` are fairly broad, while the feature itself handles only git-platform issue/PR links. Keep the broad names, or narrow them to match the current scope?

**3. Should the API include a parameter for the link type (issue vs pull request)?** It doesn't need one today: GitHub gives issues and PRs a single shared numbering sequence - there's no separate issue #5 and PR #5; a given number is one or the other - so the server just looks up the number and GitHub's response tells it which type it is. Other platforms break that assumption: GitLab numbers issues and merge requests independently, so #5 could be either, and you'd have to know the type up front to fetch the right one. Add an explicit `object_type` parameter now to be ready for that, or only when such a platform is actually added?

For the private part, the backend thread landed on a GitHub App with per-user OAuth (user access tokens) - so GitHub itself enforces access, and a preview resolves only if that user actually has read access to the repo. Public repos would still be served directly from a shared cache - no App, no per-user OAuth (just an optional server token for rate limits, short TTL) - so no one's pushed through an auth flow to preview a public link.

Locking the API now doesn't box us in, either: because the client sends structured pieces (`platform`/`owner`/`repo`/`number`) rather than a raw URL, the server can check a repo's visibility and serve public repos from the shared cache while routing private ones through the requester's own token - without changing what the client sends. So v1 can ship public-only and still be forward-compatible with the private path.

## GET /messages/raw_content

*2026-07-01 to 2026-08-10 · 13 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/GET.20.2Fmessages.2Fraw_content/with/2488137)*

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2026-07-01 14:26 UTC

Prev discussion was held in [#issues > Quoting shows undefined](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/9-issues/topic/Quoting.20shows.20undefined). 

Here's a proposal Claude and I came up with:

### `GET /messages/raw_content`

`bulk_access_messages()` already runs the full `has_message_access` check over a set of messages in bounded bulk queries. So:
- **Request:** `message_ids` (JSON list, capped at `MAX_MESSAGES_PER_FETCH`). No apply_markdown/narrow/anchor.
- **Response:** `{"messages": [{"id": 11, "content": "raw source"}, ...]}` — just the raw markdown per id.
- **Access:** `Message.objects.filter(id__in=..., realm_id=user.realm_id)` → `bulk_access_messages(...)`. Matches `GET /messages/{id}` for all cases (public-unsubscribed, DM, private+shared-history); explicit realm filter + per-message check.
- **Missing/inaccessible ids:** : TBD


### Why not reuse `GET /messages`?
- **Payload bloat (the main reason for a dedicated endpoint):** `GET /messages` returns full `MessageDict`s — rendered HTML content, sender + avatar, reactions, flags, edit-history, topic links, etc. — when all we need is one raw string per message. Quoting N messages shouldn't ship N heavy dicts.
- **Flag on it:** also bolts a second access model onto our most cross-realm-sensitive endpoint GET /messages, and doesn't fix the bloat.


### Questions

1. Name/shape appropriateness? Response as `[{id, content}]` vs `{id: content}` map?
1. Omit inaccessible ids (proposed) vs. error like `GET /messages/{id}`?

## Hiding individual link previews

*2026-07-12 to 2026-08-06 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Hiding.20individual.20link.20previews/with/2494045)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-07-12 21:24 UTC

PR #38175 (fixes #19466) lets anyone who can edit a message remove an individual auto-generated link preview. The URL is stored on the message and its preview is suppressed for everyone on re-render, the link text itself stays. On review, @Sahil Batra noted this is really a display property, not a content edit, and probably should not ride on the message-edit endpoint - so wanted to settle the API shape here before going further.

Current shape: a single `hide_preview_url` string parameter on `PATCH /messages/{id}`, the message-edit endpoint. There's no way to unhide.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-07-12 21:24 UTC

**Proposed design, copying the reactions endpoint**: a dedicated `messages/{message_id}/hidden_previews` endpoint where `POST` hides a preview and `DELETE` unhides it, each taking the preview's URL - exactly like `POST`/`DELETE` on `.../reactions`. The server updates the message's stored list of hidden URLs and re-renders; the existing `update_message` event carries the new rendered content, just as today. Hiding a preview only changes how the message looks, not what it says - so it makes sense to keep it separate from the edit endpoint. 

On whether we want to unhide previews: I'm not proposing we build an unhide button in this PR - the confirmation modal already prevents accidental hides, so l think hide only is a fine this PR.
But it's worth picking a design that leaves room for it. With `POST`/`DELETE`, unhide is already there in the API - we can build the UI for it later on. The current single-parameter design has no slot for unhide, so adding it later would mean reworking the API again.

Adding a list parameter later won't break anything already using the endpoint, so another option is to start with one URL now and extend to a list if/when we add a "remove all previews on a message" action. Either works - do folks have a preference?

For implementation of this part, here is a proposal:

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-07-13 10:28 UTC

Clients register with `long_term_idle_reactivation` client capability to indicate that they can handle this new mode of loading users.

While the user is long term idle, we return `{queue_id, last_event_id: -1, long_term_idle_reactivating: true, long_term_idle_days: 90}` instead of full response.

We send a new `reactivated` event with the full response typically returned by `/register` when the user is activated.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-07-14 04:51 UTC

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-07-27 11:25 UTC

There has been a couple of reports from users not being able to send DMs using email even when they have access to the user's email. 

The problem is that we use `email` field of a user object to fetch users, and `email` field is set to a user's real email only when the `email_address_visibility` is set to `Everyone`. So currently a user can send email using the fake email if visibility is not set to everyone and using the real email when email visibility is set to everyone.

```typescript
export function get_external_account_link(
    field_data: settings_components.ExternalAccountFieldData,
    value: string,
): string | undefined {
    const field_subtype = field_data.subtype;
    let field_url_pattern: string;

    if (field_subtype === "custom") {
        if (!field_data.url_pattern) {
            return undefined;
        }
        field_url_pattern = field_data.url_pattern;
    } else {
        const external_account = realm.realm_default_external_accounts[field_subtype];
        assert(external_account !== undefined);
        field_url_pattern = external_account.url_pattern;
        // Use as text fields when there is no URL pattern
        if (!field_url_pattern) {
            return field_url_pattern;
        }
    }
    return field_url_pattern.replace("%(username)s", () => value);
```

## split long messages PR #38357

*2026-08-17 to 2026-09-09 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/split.20long.20messages.20PR.20.2338357/with/2510502)*

**Sairam Bisoyi** · 2026-08-17 13:07 UTC

I'd like to confirm the API and data-model shape for scheduling the split messages 
part of this PR.
We know schedules messages live on server so scheduling a split message means the
server has to create the parts as an ordered group and then remember that they are
tgether otherwise its n unrelated scheduled messages that cant be displayed edited or
deleted as one. This needs a small API +schema change.

- For creating the parts, I schedule them all in one request (a new
split_message_contents list on POST /json/scheduled_messages) so the server
creates them together and returns all their ids. I went with the single
request because it's one DB write and one event instead of N, it's atomic (you
never end up with only some parts scheduled), and the server can decide the
delivery order itself. Does that sound right?

- To know which scheduled messages belong to the same split message, I add a
split_group_id column: a server-generated id shared by all parts of one message,
null for normal scheduled messages and expose it in the API. That needs a
small migration.

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-08-19 13:29 UTC

How do we handle sending split messages instantly? Do we make multiple requests to message send endpoint? If yes, then what happens if one of those request fails?

**Sairam Bisoyi** · 2026-08-19 14:35 UTC

@Tim Abbott had framed this in #28626 where we send the first block and on success push the remainder into the compose box and recurse. The PR follows the same, instant split makes one POST to message send endpoint per part sequentially. Each part is sent from previous part's success callback so they go out in the composition order. 

If one of the requests fails, we stop there and we don't fire the rest. The parts that already succeeded stay sent; the failing part plus everything after it is restored to the compose box (with the blank-line delimiters intact, so hitting Send again re-splits and sends just the remainder), and we show a banner:
"N messages were already sent before this one failed. The unsent content is back
in your compose box." 
After each successful part we also rewrite the draft down to the still-unsent remainder, so a reload mid-send can't re-send a part that already went through.

Instant send is sequential and non atomic we can have say "2 of 3 sent" and the user retries the rest. A scheduled split message is created as one atomic bulk request, so it's all-or-nothing. There's no partial-schedule state, because nothing is echoed or delivered at creation time.

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-08-21 07:24 UTC

Ohk. How we would handle editing of scheduled messages? If we have N ScheduledMessage rows for a message being split into N parts and user updates recipient of one of them, then what happens?

I was thinking if we could just store it as a one row and then split them when we send them. Of course that would mean that while editing it will be shown as a single message in compose box. But that would also mean that user can change ordering.

**Sairam Bisoyi** · 2026-08-26 08:26 UTC

So right now the PR does store N rows, but they're not loose rows. They're created together in one request, share a delivery time, and share a split_group_id the server assigns (null for normal scheduled messages, sent in the API/events). So the client always knows which rows are one composed message.

On the recipient question, we don't actually let you edit a single part on its own, exactly to avoid that inconsistency. In the scheduled messages view the parts show up as one row ("Will be sent as N messages"), deleting it deletes all of them, and editing reopens the whole thing in the compose box (parts rejoined, splitting turned back on). You edit it as one message and on reschedule the old parts are dropped and it's split fresh, so recipient/topic/time always apply to the whole thing and you never get a group with mismatched recipients. Ordering is by (scheduled_timestamp, id) so they still go out in order.
So it kind of already behaves like one message for editing/deleting, the group id is for grouping them together.

Thoughts on this current approach?

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-08-27 11:32 UTC

`scheduled_timestamp` will be same for all the messages, right? And then what happens if the messages are reordered?

**Sairam Bisoyi** · 2026-08-27 20:49 UTC

`scheduled_timestamp` is the same for all of them. The order comes from when the id tiebreaks the worker sorts by (scheduled_timestamp, id), and since the parts are bulk-created in one request in composition order they get ascending ids, so they go out in order.

The only way to reorder right now is the edit flow: it reopens the whole message in the compose box, you move the parts around there, and on reschedule the old rows get deleted and it's split and created fresh in the new order. So it works, but only by recreating.

*2026-08-18 to 2026-10-01 · 22 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/Link.20previews.20in.20the.20compose.20preview/with/2511238)*

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-08-18 13:44 UTC

PR #38630 makes link previews show up in the compose box's message preview (#19465). PR currently under review by @Aman (amanagr). It has two API changes, which I'd like to get approved here.

`POST /messages/render` takes a new optional boolean `fetch_link_previews`, defaulting to `false`. When it's set, the server includes any link previews it already has cached in the `rendered` HTML and fetches the remaining ones in the background.

A new `compose_link_preview` event delivers that result to the user who made the request. It has `content`, the draft's Markdown as sent in the request, and `rendered_content`, the same draft re-rendered with the fetched previews. The client applies it only if `content` still matches the current draft, so a late update for an edited draft is discarded.

This reuses what sent messages already do: cached embeds are baked into the render, and the rest are fetched by the `embed_links` worker and delivered as an update. API docs for both are in the PR.

**Aadyot Nandan S** · 2026-09-05 07:41 UTC

Before this change the endpoint queued nothing, so zero events. Now a request can queue one `embed_links` job, and a job sends at most one event, so 200 a minute is the worst case, and only to the user who asked. That would take a script sending 200 different drafts a minute, each with a link we haven't fetched yet. Repeating the same draft text within a minute doesn't queue a second job, and once a link is cached nothing is queued at all. In practice it's one event per preview of a draft with a new link, and none if the link is already cached.

Though this isn't a new ceiling. Sending a message with a link already queues the same kind of job, under the same limit.

## PR #39929: Let admins change user email addresses

*2026-09-03 to 2026-09-09 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/PR.20.2339929.3A.20Let.20admins.20change.20user.20email.20addresses/with/2519280)*

**BALUDU VAMSI** · 2026-09-03 18:39 UTC

Hi everyone! @Sahil Batra suggested we discuss the API design for PR #39929 (which fixes #12203) here before moving forward.

The goal of the PR is to allow Organization Administrators to edit other users' email addresses directly from the manage user UI. To support this securely, the PR introduces the following backend/API changes:
1. **New Setting:** Added a new `ADMINS_CAN_CHANGE_USER_EMAILS` setting to control this permission.
2. **State Data:** Exposed this permission to the frontend client via a new `can_change_user_emails` boolean in the state data so the UI knows whether to make the email field editable.
3. **Security Notifications:** Updated the backend action (`zerver/actions/user_settings.py`) to automatically send an email notification to *both* the old and new email addresses whenever an admin changes a user's email, ensuring users are aware if their email gets updated.

Does this API approach and permission structure look good to everyone, or are there any adjustments you'd like to see made to how `ADMINS_CAN_CHANGE_USER_EMAILS` is implemented?

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-09-09 12:42 UTC

I am not sure about the server setting name. The user should have `can_change_user_emails` permission as well and having the name says server admins can appear that all server admins can change emails.

**BALUDU VAMSI** · 2026-09-09 16:20 UTC

Thanks @Sahil Batra! That's a great point.

Right now, there are two distinct concepts in play:
1. The per-user permission `user_profile.can_change_user_emails` (which already exists in the backend and can only be granted by server admins via `./manage.py change_user_role`).
2. The server-level setting in `settings.py`, which is currently named `ADMINS_CAN_CHANGE_USER_EMAILS` (and exposed as `server_admins_can_change_user_emails` in state data).

Having "server admins" in `server_admins_can_change_user_emails` is indeed confusing because in Zulip terminology that sounds like system staff, rather than a server-level toggle for organization admins. Furthermore, `ADMINS_CAN_...` implies all admins can do it automatically without needing the individual `can_change_user_emails` permission bit.

To fix this, which direction makes the most sense to you?

- **Option 1: Do we need the server-level setting at all?**
  Since `user_profile.can_change_user_emails` is `False` by default and can only be granted via CLI by someone with server access, the server owner already has explicit gatekeeping control over who has this capability. If we drop the server setting and purely rely on `current_user.can_change_user_emails && current_user.is_admin`, the API and configuration remain very clean.

- **Option 2: If we want a server-level master switch (e.g. for Zulip Cloud to completely disable the feature):**
  We could rename the server setting to reflect that it's a feature switch rather than an automatic grant:
  - In `settings.py`: `EMAIL_CHANGE_BY_ADMIN_ENABLED` or `CAN_CHANGE_USER_EMAILS_ENABLED`
  - In state data: `server_email_change_by_admin_enabled` or `server_can_change_user_emails_enabled`

- **Option 3: If the server setting was intended to grant the capability to ALL organization admins without needing `manage.py`:**
  If the goal was for self-hosted instances to avoid running `manage.py` per admin, then enabling `ORGANIZATION_ADMINS_CAN_CHANGE_USER_EMAILS = True` would allow any realm admin (or owner) to change emails without needing the individual `can_change_user_emails` flag.

Let me know what you think aligns best with Zulip's permission model here!

## realm icon/logo delete idempotency

*2026-09-14 to 2026-09-14 · 1 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/realm.20icon.2Flogo.20delete.20idempotency/with/2523613)*

**Agnish Bauri** · 2026-09-14 18:30 UTC

While documenting `DELETE realm/icon` and `realm/logo` (#39670), we noticed that delete endpoints, behave differently from avatar.

Avatar's delete guards with `if avatar_source == AVATAR_FROM_USER:` so it will reset when a custom avatar is there or otherwise there is no-op.

But `delete_icon_backend` / `delete_logo_backend` call `do_change_icon_source`/`do_change_logo_source` and those always bump the version, write a log entry, and send an event, even when no custom icon/logo is set. So an "idempotent / succeeds without making changes" note would be inaccurate here.

@Sahil Batra and I lean towards making them idempotent for consistency with avatar. Does this seem right?

## reject negated with narrow operator #40187

*2026-09-24 to 2026-09-30 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/reject.20negated.20with.20narrow.20operator.20.2340187/with/2528571)*

**Hitanshu** · 2026-09-24 02:53 UTC

Hey! I opened #40187 (fixes #40185), which changes the behavior of the `with` narrow operator in the API

**Current behavior:** the backend silently ignores negation on `with` so `{"operator": "with", "operand": <id>, "negated": true}` is treated the same as the positive term

**Proposed change:** reject a negated `with` term as an invalid narrow (HTTP 400, "Invalid narrow operator: Negated 'with' operator") This matches the web client, which already treats it as invalid (`web/src/filter.ts`)

**Questions:**
1. is rejecting the right behavior or would you prefer something else (e.g. keep ignoring it or like a different error)?
2. I plan to add an API_FEATURE_LEVEL bump, changelog entry and `**Changes**` note since clients sending a negated `with` will now get an error Let me know if you'd prefer a different approach

**Lauryn Menard** · 2026-09-24 09:48 UTC

@Aman (amanagr) mentioning you since you probably are aware of whether allowing the negative `with` operator was intentional or not when implementing the feature.

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-09-25 03:51 UTC

When implementing the feature we didn't consider to reject the negated "with" operator. Even the frontend logic for that was added recently. We can reject the narrow and throw an error for invalid narrow.

I don't think an API feature level bump is required since no clients would send negative "with" operators to server intentionally.

**Hitanshu** · 2026-09-25 08:52 UTC

Thanks @amanagr, that’s helpful. I won’t add an API feature-level bump or a changelog note since this corrects unintended behavior rather than changing the intended API contract

**Chris Bobbe** · 2026-09-29 17:03 UTC

I think it would be appropriate to make a feature-level bump and changelog, because this change removes something that the server accepts from clients. That fits the API-design doc's definition of an API change:

https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/processes/api-design.html#what-is-an-api-change
> ## What is an API change? An “API change” is anything that adds, removes, or changes the meaning of anything that the server sends to clients, or that the server accepts from clients.

**Hitanshu** · 2026-09-30 05:21 UTC

Thanks @Chris Bobbe , agreed, that's an API change. I've updated #40187 with a changelog fragment and **Changes** notes for all three affected endpoints and left `API_FEATURE_LEVEL` for the merge tooling.
